The lām is the response to an omitted oath; قد is a particle of certainty; جاءت رسلنا: a verb and an agent; إبراهيم is a direct object; and بالبشرى is attached to جاءت.
(قالُوا سَلاماً قالَ سَلامٌ): قالوا: a verb and an agent; سلاما is a maṣdar governed by an omitted verb, as already mentioned, i.e. "we greet you with a greeting"; قال is a past verb; and سلام is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "upon you"; the meaning of supplication permitted the mubtadaʾ to be indefinite, and this is preferable to making it the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "my saying is 'peace'"; the justifications for beginning with an indefinite will come in the section on Benefits. (فَما لَبِثَ أَنْ جاءَ بِعِجْلٍ حَنِيذٍ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; as for ما in ما لبث, it may be negative, with لبث a past verb whose agent is أن and what is in its scope, i.e. "his bringing"; or the agent is latent, its implied form being "Ibrāhīm", and أن and what is in its scope is its khabar, the implied form being "so his delay" or "the one he delayed was the measure of his bringing".
(فَلَمَّا رَأى أَيْدِيَهُمْ لا تَصِلُ إِلَيْهِ نَكِرَهُمْ وَأَوْجَسَ مِنْهُمْ خِيفَةً): the fāʾ is conjoined to an omitted element, the implied form being "so he brought it near to them, but they did not stretch out their hands, so he said: Will you not eat? So when he saw their hands"; the seeing here is by the eye; أيديهم is a direct object; the clause لا تصل إليه is a ḥāl clause; the clause نكرهم has no grammatical position because it is the response of لما; وأوجس منهم is conjoined to نكرهم; خيفة is a direct object; and منهم is a ḥāl because it was originally an adjective of خيفة. (قالُوا لا تَخَفْ إِنَّا أُرْسِلْنا إِلى قَوْمِ لُوطٍ): لا تخف: لا is prohibitive and تخف is jussive by it; inna and its ism; the clause أرسلنا is its khabar, نا being the deputy agent; and إلى قوم لوط is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أرسلنا. (وَامْرَأَتُهُ قائِمَةٌ فَضَحِكَتْ فَبَشَّرْناها بِإِسْحاقَ وَمِنْ وَراءِ إِسْحاقَ يَعْقُوبَ): وامرأته: the wāw is circumstantial or resumptive; امرأته is a mubtadaʾ and قائمة a khabar; فضحكت is a past verb whose agent is "she"; فبشرناها is also a conjunction, a verb, an agent and a direct object; بإسحاق is attached to بشرناها; ومن وراء إسحاق is a fronted khabar and يعقوب a postponed mubtadaʾ. (قالَتْ: يا وَيْلَتى أَأَلِدُ وَأَنَا عَجُوزٌ): يا ويلتا is an expression said in wonder at a marvellous matter that breaks custom, whether good or evil; it is the one addressed, annexed to the yāʾ of the speaker which has turned into alif, likewise in "yā lahfā" and "yā ʿajabā"; it is also said that it is the alif of lamentation (nudba), on which one stops with the hāʾ of pause, and the discussion of it will come in its place. أألد: the interrogative is meant as wonder; the wāw is circumstantial; أنا is a mubtadaʾ and عجوز a khabar, and the clause is accusative as a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in أألد. (وَهذا بَعْلِي شَيْخاً إِنَّ هذا لَشَيْءٌ عَجِيبٌ): the wāw is circumstantial; هذا is a mubtadaʾ and بعلي a khabar; شيخا is a ḥāl, the governor in it being the verbal meaning in the demonstrative. Al-Zajjāj said: the accusative of the ḥāl here is among the subtleties of grammar. That is, when you say "this is Zayd standing, praying": if you intend to inform someone who does not know Zayd that he is Zayd, it is not permissible to say "this is Zayd standing", because he would be "Zayd" only so long as he is standing, and once he leaves standing he is not Zayd. You say "this is Zayd standing" only to someone who knows Zayd, so alerting acts on the ḥāl, the meaning being "Attend to Zayd while he is standing", or "I point out Zayd to you while he is standing".
Then inna and its ism; the shifted lām; شيء is its khabar and عجيب an adjective. (قالُوا: أَتَعْجَبِينَ مِنْ أَمْرِ اللَّهِ): the hamza is for interrogation, the intent being prohibition, i.e. "do not be astonished"; they did not rebuke her, because her astonishment was not denial but only bewilderment at what breaks custom; تعجبين is an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, the yāʾ being the agent; and من أمر الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تعجبين. (رَحْمَتُ اللَّهِ وَبَرَكاتُهُ عَلَيْكُمْ أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ إِنَّهُ حَمِيدٌ مَجِيدٌ): رحمة الله is a mubtadaʾ; وبركاته is conjoined to رحمة; عليكم is the khabar of رحمة; أهل البيت is accusative as ikhtiṣāṣ (specification), intended as praise; it may also be a vocative from which the vocative particle has been omitted, i.e. "O people of the house"; and inna with its ism and two khabars.
There is a difference between the accusative of praise and the accusative of ikhtiṣāṣ, and for this reason Sībawayh made them two separate chapters: the accusative of praise is a word that by its very placing includes praise, just as the accusative of blame includes blame by its placing; while the accusative of ikhtiṣāṣ occurs only for praise or blame but its wording by its placing includes neither praise nor blame, as in the line «بنا تميما يكشف الضباب» ("Through us, Tamīm, the fog is lifted") and the line «ولا الحجاج عيني نبت ماء» ("...nor al-Ḥajjāj, my eye..."). [Translator's note: the second verse fragment is given as in the source, incomplete.] (فَلَمَّا ذَهَبَ عَنْ إِبْراهِيمَ الرَّوْعُ وَجاءَتْهُ الْبُشْرى): the fāʾ is a conjunction; لما is temporal or connective; ذهب عن إبراهيم الروع: a verb and an agent; وجاءته البشرى is conjoined to ذهب; and the response of لما is omitted, its implied form being "he turned" or "he grasped, in order to dispute with them".
(يُجادِلُنا فِي قَوْمِ لُوطٍ): the clause يجادلنا is circumstantial or resumptive, and في قوم لوط is attached to يجادلنا. (إِنَّ إِبْراهِيمَ لَحَلِيمٌ أَوَّاهٌ مُنِيبٌ): inna and its ism; the shifted lām; حليم, أواه and منيب are three khabars. (يا إِبْراهِيمُ أَعْرِضْ عَنْ هذا): the sentence is the reported speech of an omitted saying, i.e. "the angels said"; أعرض is an imperative verb; عن هذا is attached to it, the pointing being to the dispute. (إِنَّهُ قَدْ جاءَ أَمْرُ رَبِّكَ وَإِنَّهُمْ آتِيهِمْ عَذابٌ غَيْرُ مَرْدُودٍ): inna and its ism; the clause قد جاء أمر ربك is the khabar; وإنهم: inna and its ism; آتيهم is its khabar; عذاب is the agent of آتيهم; غير is an adjective and مردود a muḍāf ilayhi.

* Rhetoric:
Representational metaphor (istiʿāra tamthīliyya) in His words: «When he saw that their hands did not reach it» (فلما رأى أيديهم لا تصل إليه): the non-reaching is made a metaphor for their refraining from eating; the meaning is "they do not stretch out their hands to eat it", for he does not intend to deny a reaching that arises from stretching out.

* Benefits:
The justifications for beginning with an indefinite:
What is obligatory in the mubtadaʾ is that it be definite, and beginning with an indefinite is permitted if it conveys a benefit, in several places, the most important of which are:
1- By verbal annexation, as in «Five prayers Allah has prescribed» (خمس صلوات كتبهن الله); the annexation may also be in meaning, as in «Say: each acts according to his manner» (قل كلّ يعمل على شاكلته), i.e. "each one".
2- By an adjective, in wording, as in «A believing slave is better than a polytheist» (لعبد مؤمن خير من مشرك); or in implication, as in "An (affair) has come from your Lord", i.e. "a great one"; or in meaning, when the indefinite is a diminutive, as in "rujayl (a little man) is with us", i.e. "a despicable man".
3- By its khabar being an adverbial, or a preposition and its genitive noun, fronted before it, as in «and above every possessor of knowledge is a knower» (وفوق كل ذي علم عليم) and «for every term is a decree» (ولكل أجل كتاب).
4- By its occurring after a negation, an interrogative, lawlā, or the idhā of surprise, as in: "No one is with us"; and as in «Is there a god with Allah?» (أإله مع الله); and the verse of the poet:
لولا اصطبار الأودى كل ذي مقة ... لما استقلّت مطاياهنّ للظّعن
(Were it not for the patience of every loving al-Awdī, their mounts would not have risen for departure.)
and as in: "I went out and behold a lion lying in wait".
5- By its being a governor, as in: "Giving a piastre for the sake of knowledge raises the nation."
6- By its being vague, like the conditional and interrogative nouns, the exclamatory mā, and the declarative kam.
7- By its conveying supplication for good or evil: the first as in «Peace be upon you» (سلام عليكم), and the second as in «Woe to the defrauders» (ويل للمطففين).
8- By its being a substitute for a qualified noun, as in: "A knowledgeable one is better than an ignorant one."
9- By its occurring at the head of a circumstantial clause, as in:
سرينا ونجم قد أضاء فمذ بدا ... محياك أخفى ضوءه كلّ شارق
(We travelled while a star was shining; then, when your face appeared, every rising one hid its light.)
10- By its being intended for classification, i.e. detailing and dividing, as in the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
فأقبلت زحفا على الركبتين ... فثوب نسيت وثوب أجر
(I approached, crawling upon my two knees; one garment I forgot, another I drag.)
11- By its being conjoined to a definite, or a definite being conjoined to it, as in: "Khālid and a man are learning grammar", or "a man and Khālid are learning grammar".
12- By its being conjoined to a qualified indefinite, as in «A kind word and forgiveness are better than charity followed by injury» (قول معروف ومغفرة خير من صدقة يتبعها أذى).
13- By its being intended for the reality of the genus and not a single individual of it, as in: "A date is better than a locust."
14- By its occurring as an answer, as in: "A man", in answer to one who said: "Who is with you?"

dervis-irab:113-117.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تَرْكَنُوا): al-rukūn to a thing is to be at rest in it through love for it, and to listen attentively to it. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "I inclined to Zayd (rakantu ilā Zayd)" means I relied on him. It has several dialects. One is of the pattern taʿiba, on which the saying of the Exalted «ولا تركنوا إلى الذين ظلموا» rests; and rakana rukūnan of the pattern qaʿada — al-Azharī said it is not the eloquent form. The third is rakana yarkanu with two fatḥas, which is not original but arises from the interpenetration of two dialects, because the pattern faʿila yafʿalu has a guttural as its ʿayn or lām." Al-Rāghib said: "The correct view is that one says rakana yarkanu with a fatḥa in both, and rakina yarkanu with a kasra in the past and a fatḥa in the imperfect, and with a fatḥa in the past and a ḍamma in the imperfect." It is gathered from al-Qāmūs and its commentary and other dictionaries that it is of the pattern dakhala and of the pattern taʿiba. As for its intransitive sense, its pattern is rakuna with a ḍamma on the kāf, meaning he was steady and dignified.
(زُلَفاً): with a ḍamma on the zāy and a fatḥa on the lām: the plural of zulfa from the night, i.e. a portion. In al-Qāmūs: al-zulfā is a portion of the night; the plural is zulaf and zulafāt, like ghuraf and ghurafāt. Al-ʿAjjāj said:
تاج طواه الأين مما رجفا ... طيّ الليالي زلفا فزلفا
(A [camel] excellent, whom weariness has folded from his trembling, the folding of the nights, portion after portion.)
(أُتْرِفُوا): they were given luxury. Tarifa, like fariḥa, means he lived in luxury; atrafathu l-niʿma means the blessing made him insolent and made him transgress.

* I'rab:
(وَلا تَرْكَنُوا إِلَى الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا فَتَمَسَّكُمُ النَّارُ): The wāw is resumptive; lā is prohibitive; تركنوا is an imperfect verb jussive by lā and the wāw is the fāʿil; إلى الذين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تركنوا; the clause ظلموا is the ṣila. As for فتمسكم: the fāʾ is causal; تمسكم is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied an after the fāʾ that follows a prohibition; the kāf is mafʿūl bihi; and النار is the fāʿil. (وَما لَكُمْ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ مِنْ أَوْلِياءَ ثُمَّ لا تُنْصَرُونَ): The wāw is circumstantial or also resumptive, and the clause is circumstantial, i.e. "the Fire will touch you while you have no helper", or resumptive; mā is negative; لكم is a fronted khabar; من دون الله is ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of أولياء; min is a redundant preposition; أولياء is genitive in form by a fatḥa, nominative in position, because it is a delayed mubtadaʾ. Thumma is a conjunction; lā is negative; تنصرون is an imperfect verb. It is not made accusative as a sequel to تركنوا, because this is a conjunction of clauses, a verbal clause conjoined to a nominal clause. (وَأَقِمِ الصَّلاةَ طَرَفَيِ النَّهارِ وَزُلَفاً مِنَ اللَّيْلِ): The wāw is a conjunction; أقم is an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent, implied "you"; الصلاة is mafʿūl bihi; طرفي النهار is accusative as a ẓarf attached to أقم, and what is meant by the two ends of the day is the morning and the afternoon; زلفا is also accusative as a ẓarf attached to أقم; and من الليل is naʿt. (إِنَّ الْحَسَناتِ يُذْهِبْنَ السَّيِّئاتِ ذلِكَ ذِكْرى لِلذَّاكِرِينَ): Inna and its noun; the clause يذهبن is its khabar; the nūn is the fāʿil of يذهبن; السيئات is mafʿūl bihi; ذلك is the mubtadaʾ; ذكرى is the khabar; and للذاكرين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element as naʿt of ذكرى. (وَاصْبِرْ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُضِيعُ أَجْرَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ): واصبر is conjoined to أقم; the fāʾ is causal; inna and its noun; the clause لا يضيع is its khabar; and أجر المحسنين is mafʿūl bihi. (فَلَوْلا كانَ مِنَ الْقُرُونِ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ أُولُوا بَقِيَّةٍ يَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ الْفَسادِ فِي الْأَرْضِ): The fāʾ is resumptive; lawlā is hortative. Perhaps parsing kāna as complete is preferable, since the meaning is "why was there not found, or why did there not occur", so من القرون is attached to it or to an omitted element as ḥāl; من قبلكم is ḥāl from القرون; and أولو is its fāʿil, its sign of nominative being the wāw because it is appended to the sound masculine plural; بقية is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause ينهون عن الفساد is naʿt of أولو بقية; and في الأرض is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to الفساد. If we make kāna incomplete, then من القرون is attached to an omitted element as ḥāl, the clause ينهون is its khabar, and أولو بقية is its noun. The maṣdar accompanied by the article governs overt objects, so it is more fitting for it to govern interpreted ones and ẓarfs; it may also be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from الفساد. (إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِمَّنْ أَنْجَيْنا مِنْهُمْ): Illā is a particle of exception, and قليلا is a disconnected exception (munqaṭiʿ), lest the meaning be spoiled. We relay here the words of al-Zamakhsharī: "Its meaning is 'but a few of those We saved from the generations forbade corruption, and the rest of them abandoned forbidding'." Then he said: "If you say, 'Is there any ground on which this exception can be taken as connected?' I say: if you make it connected, as the apparent sense of the speech has it, the meaning would be corrupt, because it would then be an exhortation to those possessed of remnant to forbid corruption, and not to the few among them who were saved, as you say, 'Why did your people not recite the Qur'an, except the righteous among them?', meaning the exception of the righteous from those being exhorted to recite the Qur'an. If you say that in their being exhorted to forbid corruption lies the sense of its negation concerning them, so that it is as if it had been said 'there were not among the generations those possessed of remnant, except a few', the exception would be connected and the meaning sound, and its accusative would rest on the basic rule of exception, even though the more eloquent would be to put it in the nominative as a badal." As for ممن: it is naʿt of قليلا; the clause أنجينا is the ṣila; and منهم is ḥāl. (وَاتَّبَعَ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا ما أُتْرِفُوا فِيهِ وَكانُوا مُجْرِمِينَ): واتبع is conjoined to an implied element indicated by the speech, implied as "so they did not forbid corruption, and ... followed"; الذين is the fāʿil; the clause ظلموا is the ṣila; mā is mafʿūl bihi; the clause أترفوا is the ṣila; فيه is attached to أترفوا; كانوا مجرمين is kāna with its noun and khabar; and the clause is conjoined to أترفوا. (وَما كانَ رَبُّكَ لِيُهْلِكَ الْقُرى بِظُلْمٍ وَأَهْلُها مُصْلِحُونَ): The wāw is resumptive; mā is negative; كان is an incomplete past verb; ربك is its noun; as for ليهلك, the lām is the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd), which is preceded by a negated kāna; يهلك is made accusative by an implied an after the lām; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the omitted khabar, i.e. "intending to destroy", and the explanation of that has already preceded; القرى is mafʿūl bihi; بظلم is ḥāl from the fāʿil; and أهلها: the wāw is circumstantial, أهلها is a mubtadaʾ and مصلحون is the khabar, and the clause is circumstantial from the mafʿūl bihi, i.e. the towns.

* Rhetoric:
In the saying of the Exalted «ولا تركنوا إلى الذين ظلموا», to the end of the verse, there are many arts of rhetoric before which necks are cut off, and we shall set them out as follows:

1- Harmony of expression with meaning (i'tilāf al-lafẓ maʿa l-maʿnā):
Since inclining toward those who do wrong is less than the deed of the wrongdoers, the punishment for it must be less than the punishment of the wrongdoers; and the touch of the Fire is in reality less than burning. Since burning is the punishment of the wrongdoer, justice requires that the touch be the punishment of the one who inclines to the wrongdoer. For this reason, mighty and exalted, He turned away from saying, for example, ... [Translator's note: the source has an ellipsis here and the sentence is evidently incomplete] "so that you enter the Fire", because entering is the likely occasion of burning, and He singled out the touch to point to what the inclining calls for in punishment, and to distinguish between what the wrongdoer deserves and what the one who inclines to him deserves, although the touch of the Fire may be used in a general sense meaning burning. But this general use is figurative, and the reality is what we have said, because the reality of touch is the first meeting of the body with the heat of the Fire. When an expression admits several possibilities, it is directed to what the indications point to. The harmony in this verse is in meaning.

2- Insertion (al-idmāj):
Allah the Exalted has inserted His description as just, so the art of boasting is connected with the art of discipline, since the apparent sense of the verse is discipline, and for it the admonition came in this chapter, together with the description of the True One, mighty and exalted, as just.
3- Extension (al-basṭ):
He did not say "the wrongdoers" (al-ẓālimīn) but turned to His saying «الذين ظلموا», because the first allows for the continuity of wrongdoing, which does not suit touching, and the emphasis that the second expression achieves — wrongdoing occurring only rarely — is not attained with it, so that the meaning suits the meaning of inclining and touching, and true emphasis is achieved. For when He forbids inclining toward one whose wrongdoing has continued, forbidding inclining toward one who has done wrong only once is even more fitting, and when He forbids inclining toward the wrongdoer, forbidding the deed of wrongdoing is all the more fitting.
On this occasion we record here a letter that is a sign in rhetoric and fits the occasion. When al-Zuhrī mixed with the sultans, a brother in religion wrote to him: "May Allah keep us and you, Abū Bakr, safe from trials. You have come to a state in which whoever knows you should pray to Allah for you and ask mercy for you. You have become an old man, weighed down by the favours of Allah through what He made you understand of His Book and taught you of the Sunna of His Prophet. It is not so that Allah took the covenant from the scholars; the Exalted said: «لتبيننه للناس ولا تكتمونه». Know that the easiest of what you have committed and the lightest of what you have borne is that you have comforted the loneliness of the wrongdoer and eased the path of error by your nearness to one who did not render a right and did not abandon falsehood when he drew you near. They took you as a pivot on which the millstone of their falsehood turns, a bridge over which they cross to their trial, and a ladder by which they climb to their misguidance. Through you they introduce doubt to the scholars, and with you they lead the hearts of the ignorant. How little they built for you compared to what they ruined of yours, and how much they took from you compared to what they corrupted of your religion! What assures you that you are not among those of whom Allah said: «فخلف من بعدهم خلف أضاعوا الصلاة، واتبعوا الشهوات فسوف يلقون غيّا»? For you deal with One who is not ignorant and who preserves against you what is not forgotten. Heal your religion, for sickness has entered it, and prepare your provisions, for the long journey has come near. «وما يخفى على الله من شيء في الأرض ولا في السماء». Peace."

dervis-irab:118-123.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلَوْ شاءَ رَبُّكَ لَجَعَلَ النَّاسَ أُمَّةً واحِدَةً): The wāw is resumptive; law is a conditional particle of prevention; شاء ربك is a verb and a fāʿil; the lām occurs in the apodosis of law; جعل الناس أمة is jaʿala with its two objects; and واحدة is naʿt. (وَلا يَزالُونَ مُخْتَلِفِينَ إِلَّا مَنْ رَحِمَ رَبُّكَ): The wāw is a conjunction; لا يزالون is an incomplete imperfect verb, the wāw is its noun and مختلفين is its khabar. As for إلا من رحم ربك, al-Zajjāj said it is a disconnected exception in the sense of lākin, implied as "but whoever your Lord has had mercy upon, he does not differ". Abū l-Baqāʾ was content to say: it is excepted from the fāʿil pronoun in يزالون. (وَلِذلِكَ خَلَقَهُمْ وَتَمَّتْ كَلِمَةُ رَبِّكَ): لذلك is attached to خلقهم, and the demonstrative refers to disagreement and mercy; خلقهم is a verb, a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; تمت كلمة ربك is a verb and a fāʿil, and what is meant by His word is His eternal decree and His binding judgment. (لَأَمْلَأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ مِنَ الْجِنَّةِ وَالنَّاسِ أَجْمَعِينَ): لأملأن جهنم is the answer to an implied oath, implied as "by an oath, I shall surely fill"; أملأن is an imperfect verb indeclinable on the fatḥa; جهنم is mafʿūl bihi; من الجنة is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أملأن; al-jinna is al-jinn, and the tāʾ is for emphasis; and أجمعين is tawkīd. (وَكُلًّا نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ مِنْ أَنْباءِ الرُّسُلِ ما نُثَبِّتُ بِهِ فُؤادَكَ): It is permissible that كلا be accusative as a maṣdar, implied as "and all the stories We relate to you", with the clause نقص عليك in the position of naʿt of his word وكلا; and it may be accusative as an object, with the muḍāf ilayhi omitted and the tanwīn as its compensation, implied as "every report We relate to you". من أنباء is naʿt of كلا; and mā is a relative noun in the accusative position as a badal from كلا, and it is also said to be redundant. On the first view it is parsed as an object, and the clause نثبت به فؤادك is the ṣila; the meaning of firming the heart is increasing its certainty and what contains the reassurance of the heart. (وَجاءَكَ فِي هذِهِ الْحَقُّ وَمَوْعِظَةٌ وَذِكْرى لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ): وجاءك is a verb and a mafʿūl bihi; في هذه is attached to جاءك, and the demonstrative refers to the sūra or to the reports related in it; الحق is the fāʿil of جاءك, and what follows is conjoined to it. (وَقُلْ لِلَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ اعْمَلُوا عَلى مَكانَتِكُمْ): للذين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to قل; the clause لا يؤمنون is the ṣila; اعملوا is an imperative verb and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the content of the saying; and على مكانتكم is ḥāl, i.e. "while you remain firm in your standing", and the discussion of makāna has preceded. (إِنَّا عامِلُونَ): Inna and its noun and khabar. (وَانْتَظِرُوا إِنَّا مُنْتَظِرُونَ): انتظروا is an imperative verb and the wāw is the fāʿil; إنا منتظرون is inna with its noun and khabar; and the threat is plain. (وَلِلَّهِ غَيْبُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَإِلَيْهِ يُرْجَعُ الْأَمْرُ كُلُّهُ): لله is a fronted khabar; غيب السموات is a delayed mubtadaʾ; إليه is attached to يرجع; الأمر is its nāʾib fāʿil; and كله is tawkīd. (فَاعْبُدْهُ وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَيْهِ وَما رَبُّكَ بِغافِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ): The fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ; اعبده is an imperative verb, a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; وتوكل is conjoined to اعبده; عليه is attached to توكل; mā is Ḥijāzī; ربك is its noun; the bāʾ is a redundant preposition; غافل is genitive in form and accusative in position, its khabar; عما is attached to غافل; and يعملون is the ṣila of mā.

dervis-irab:45-49.t:
* I'rab:
(وَنادى نُوحٌ رَبَّهُ فَقالَ: رَبِّ إِنَّ ابْنِي مِنْ أَهْلِي) The wāw is resumptive. The call, as appears, was before the ship sailed, because it is a request for the rescue of his son, and there is no sense in the request except when rescue is possible. نادى نوح is a verb and an agent; ربه is a direct object; فقال: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and قال is a past verb conjoined to نادى by explicative conjunction (ʿaṭf tafsīr), because the saying mentioned is the very call. رب is a muḍāf vocative added to the omitted yāʾ of the first person; inna and its noun; and من أهلي is its khabar (predicate). He brought this up only because Allah the Exalted had promised him the rescue of his family. The exegetes have a long discussion about the sonship of this son, which lies outside the scope of this book. (وَإِنَّ وَعْدَكَ الْحَقُّ وَأَنْتَ أَحْكَمُ الْحاكِمِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction; inna, its noun and its khabar; وأنت أحكم الحاكمين is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar, and the clause is also conjoined. (قالَ يا نُوحُ إِنَّهُ لَيْسَ مِنْ أَهْلِكَ) قال is a past verb whose agent is the latent pronoun of Allah; inna and its noun, and the clause ليس من أهلك is the khabar of إن, and من أهلك is the khabar of ليس. (إِنَّهُ عَمَلٌ غَيْرُ صالِحٍ) inna and its noun; the pronoun refers to his son, and there is no justification for the statement of those who said that the pronoun refers to his request, as al-Jalāl and others held, because the eloquence of the speech rules it out. عمل is the khabar of إن, and this is a case of putting the adjective in the place of the thing described when the meaning is apparent, which has already been pointed out. Of it is the saying of ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa:
أيها القائل في غير الصواب ... أخّر النصح وأقلل من عتابي
(O you who speak other than what is right, put off your counsel and lessen your reproach of me.)
and his saying also:
وكم من قتيل لا يباء به دم ... ومن غلق رهنا إذا ضمّه منى ومن مالىء عينيه من شيء غيره ... إذا راح نحو الجمرة البيض كالدمى
(How many a slain man for whom no blood is paid in retribution, and how many a pledge left pawned when Minā gathers him, and one who fills his eyes with nothing but her, when the white ones like statues head toward the Jamra.)
[Translator's note: the two verses seem to be run together in the source, and the text is as printed; my gloss is tentative.]
He meant "O man, the killer" and "how many a man slain". And the saying of al-Khansāʾ:
ترتع ما رتعت حتى إذا ادّكرت ... فإنما هي إقبال وإدبار
(She grazes as long as she grazes, until, when she remembers, she is nothing but approaching and turning away.)
غير صالح is an adjective of عمل, and the clause is a reason for the negation of his being among his family who are saved. (فَلا تَسْئَلْنِ ما لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ) The fāʾ is the eloquent (faṣīḥa) fāʾ; لا is prohibitive; تسأل is an imperfect verb jussive by لا, and the nūn is the nūn of protection (wiqāya), and the yāʾ of the first person, omitted for lightness, is a direct object; ما is a second direct object; the clause ليس is a ṣila; the noun of ليس is علم and لك is its fronted khabar; and به is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to علم. (إِنِّي أَعِظُكَ أَنْ تَكُونَ مِنَ الْجاهِلِينَ) inna and its noun, and the clause أعظك is its khabar; أن and what is in its domain are in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "I warn you against being", and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أعظك; the noun of تكون is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you", and من الجاهلين is the khabar of تكون. The meaning of calling Nūḥ's request ignorance will come in the Benefits section. (قالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ أَنْ أَسْئَلَكَ ما لَيْسَ لِي بِهِ عِلْمٌ) inna and its noun, and the clause أعوذ is its khabar; بك is attached to أعوذ; أن and what is in its domain are accusative by removal of the preposition; and the i'rab of ما ليس لي به علم has already been given. (وَإِلَّا تَغْفِرْ لِي وَتَرْحَمْنِي أَكُنْ مِنَ الْخاسِرِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction; إن is conditional and لا is negative; تغفر is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); لي is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to it; وترحمني is conjoined to تغفر; أكن is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), its noun a latent pronoun, its implied form being "I"; and من الخاسرين is its khabar. (قِيلَ يا نُوحُ اهْبِطْ بِسَلامٍ مِنَّا وَبَرَكاتٍ عَلَيْكَ) اهبط is an imperative verb; بسلام is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl from the agent of اهبط, i.e. "accompanied by peace"; منا is an adjective of سلام, or is attached to سلام itself; وبركات is conjoined to سلام; and عليك is an adjective. (وَعَلى أُمَمٍ مِمَّنْ مَعَكَ) وعلى أمم is conjoined to عليك; ممن is an adjective of أمم; and معك is an adverbial of place, the ṣila of the relative. (وَأُمَمٌ سَنُمَتِّعُهُمْ ثُمَّ يَمَسُّهُمْ مِنَّا عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ) The wāw is resumptive; أمم is a mubtadaʾ, and it was permissible to begin with it because it is qualified, the implied form being "and nations from among those with you"; and the clause سنمتعهم is its khabar; or سنمتعهم is made an adjective and the omitted part is the khabar, omitted because his saying ممن معك indicates it. ثم is a conjunction implying delay; يمسهم is an imperfect verb and a direct object; منا is a ḥāl because it was an adjective of عذاب; عذاب is the agent; and أليم is a second adjective. (تِلْكَ مِنْ أَنْباءِ الْغَيْبِ نُوحِيها إِلَيْكَ) تلك is a mubtadaʾ; من أنباء الغيب is a first khabar; and the clause نوحيها إليك is a second khabar, and if you wish it is in the position of a ḥāl, i.e. "that being of the tidings of the unseen, revealed to you". (ما كُنْتَ تَعْلَمُها أَنْتَ وَلا قَوْمُكَ مِنْ قَبْلِ هذا) It is a third khabar, and this is the best of the i'rabs; كان and its noun, and the clause تعلمها is the khabar of كنت, and ها is a direct object; أنت is an emphasis (tawkīd) of the latent agent of تعلمها; ولا قومك is conjoined to أنت; and من قبل هذا is a ḥāl of the hāʾ in نوحيها or of the kāf in إليك, i.e. "you and your people being ignorant of it". (فَاصْبِرْ إِنَّ الْعاقِبَةَ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ) The fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ, i.e. "if you have learned this story and what it contains and what the event of the Flood came to, then be patient"; and the clause إن العاقبة للمتقين, inna with its noun and khabar, gives a reason. This is the purpose of the story of Nūḥ and the stories that will follow it.

* Benefits:
The exegetes have a long discussion on this verse and on the reason for describing Nūḥ's request as ignorance, which indicates a lack of infallibility (ʿiṣma); al-Zamakhsharī even held that there issued from Nūḥ, peace be upon him, what makes it necessary to ascribe ignorance to him and to reproach him for it. It would be long to quote what they adduced, or even to summarize it. The closest thing that can be said about it is that when the promise was issued to Nūḥ of the rescue of his family, except those of them against whom the word had already gone forth, he was not one who had uncovered the condition of his said son, nor was he informed of his inner self and the reality of his affair; rather he believed, from the outward condition, that he was a believer. So he stayed with holding to the general wording on account of established family membership, and no certainty of his son's disbelief opposed it so as to take him out of the family and put him among the excepted. So he asked Allah about him on that basis, and it became clear to him that in His knowledge he was among the excepted, and that he himself had no knowledge of that; therefore he asked about him. This is more fitting to be a clarification of an excuse than a rebuke. As for His saying «إني أعظك أن تكون من الجاهلين», what is meant by it is the prohibition against making the request in the future after Allah has informed him of the inner state of the matter, and that if the request occurred in the future he would be among the ignorant. The aim of that is to present what keeps him on the mark of infallibility, and exhortation does not require the occurrence of a sin. Nūḥ was apprehensive at his having ventured to ask his Lord about what he had not been given permission for, and feared destruction from that, so he took refuge with his Lord, was humble before Him, called upon Him and asked Him for forgiveness and mercy, because the good deeds of the righteous are the evil deeds of those brought near.

dervis-irab:77-83.t:
* Vocabulary:
(سِيءَ بِهِمْ): its original form is suwiʾa bihim, from al-sūʾ (evil); the wāw was made quiescent and its kasra was transferred to the sīn. One says "sūʾtuhu, so sīʾa", as one says "shaghaltuhu, so shughila" and "sarartuhu, so surra".
(ذَرْعاً): among their sayings is "so-and-so's dhirʿ was straitened". Al-dhirʿ is put in the place of capacity; the origin is that the camel measures with its forelegs in its walking, a measure (dhirʿ) according to the width of its stride; so when a load beyond its capacity is placed on it, its dhirʿ is straitened for that, it weakens and stretches out its neck. So narrowness of the dhirʿ became an expression for narrowness of capacity and ability. The meaning of His words «and he was straitened for them in dhirʿ» (وضاق بهم ذرعا) is that he found no escape from that unwelcome situation. Some scholars of the language said: its meaning is "his heart and breast were straitened for them", and its origin is not known unless it is said that al-dhirʿ is a metonym for capacity; the Arabs say "this is not in my hand", meaning "it is not in my capacity", because the forearm (dhirāʿ) is part of the hand. Others said: it is said "so-and-so was straitened in dhirʿ by such-and-such" when he fell into something unpleasant and cannot bear to get out of it.
In al-Qāmūs and al-Tāj, in summary: "Al-dhirʿ is a verbal noun: the stretching out of the hand. 'Ḍuqtu bi-l-amr dhirʿan' means I was unable to cope with it; 'he is wide in dhirʿ' means capable; and 'he is empty of dhirʿ' means his heart is free of worries and griefs."
(يُهْرَعُونَ): that is, some of them drive others. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "hurʿa and uhriʿa, both passive, when he is made to hurry." In al-Qāmūs: "al-hara (with vowelled letters, and like ghurāb) and al-ihrāʿ is walking in agitation and haste; 'he came yuhraʿu' (with ḍamma) and 'uhriʿa' (passive) so he is muhraʿ, trembling from anger or fear; 'he has hariʿa' (like fariḥa); and 'a man hariʿ' is one quick to weep."
(عَصِيبٌ): al-ʿaṣīb is severe, especially in evil. Its origin is from tightening; one says "ʿaṣabtu al-shayʾ" meaning I tightened it, and "ʿaṣabtu the thigh of the she-camel" so that she would let her milk down, and a "ʿaṣūb she-camel". "A ʿaṣīb day" and "ʿaṣabṣab" is as if it wrapped itself around the people with evil, or its evil is wrapped together part upon part. The poet said:
فإنك إن لم ترض بكر بن وائل ... يكن لك يوم بالعراق عصيب
(For if you do not satisfy Bakr ibn Wāʾil, you will have a dire day in Iraq.)
And the rajaz poet said:
يوم عصيب ويعصب الأبطالا ... عصب القوي السلم الطوالا
(A dire day, that binds the heroes, the way the strong binds the long salam [trees].) [Translator's note: the meaning of the second hemistich is uncertain; the gloss is tentative.]
(رُكْنٍ): al-rukn is the support of a building after the foundation; the two rukns of a mountain are its two sides. The rajaz poet said:
يأوي إلى ركن من الأركان ... في عدد طلس ومجد بان
(He takes refuge in a pillar among the pillars, among many [companions] and an established glory.) [Translator's note: the gloss of عدد طلس is tentative.]
(فَأَسْرِ): from asrā in the sense of sarā, i.e. he travelled by night. Al-Nābigha said:
أسرت عليه من الجوزاء سارية ... تزجي الشمال عليه جامد البرد
(A night-travelling cloud from al-Jawzāʾ moved over it, the north wind driving upon it frozen hail.)
It is also transmitted as "sarat". And Imruʾ al-Qays said:
سريت بهم حتى تكل مطيهم ... وحتى الجياد ما يقدن بأرسان
(I travelled by night with them until their mounts grew weary, and even the steeds were no longer led by halters.)
(سِجِّيلٍ): Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is said that it is an Arabicized word from sang-kil, by the evidence of His words 'stones of clay'; and it is said it is from asjalahu, when he sent it, because it is sent upon the wrongdoers; and it is said it is from what Allah decreed to punish with, from al-sijill, as in 'sijill for so-and-so'." Abū ʿUbayda said: "It is hard stones", and he recited a verse of Ibn Muqbil:
ورجلة يضربون البيض ضاحية ... ضربا تواصى به الأبطال سجينا
(And foot soldiers who strike the helmets in the open, a blow that the heroes urged one another to, sijjīn.)
"Sijjīn and sijjīl are of one meaning, and the Arabs interchange nūn and lām, so here the nūn was changed into lām." The author of al-Qāmūs was satisfied with his words: "al-sijjīl is dry clay."
(مَنْضُودٍ): piled one upon another; al-naḍd is putting things one on top of another. What is meant is to describe the stones as abundant.
(مُسَوَّمَةً): marked for punishment; al-taswīm is the mark.

* I'rab:
(وَلَمَّا جاءَتْ رُسُلُنا لُوطاً سِيءَ بِهِمْ وَضاقَ بِهِمْ ذَرْعاً): لما is temporal or connective; جاءت رسلنا لوطا: a verb, an agent and a direct object; the clause سيء بهم has no grammatical position; the deputy agent refers back to Lūṭ; بهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to it; and ذرعا is a tamyīz transformed from the agent. (وَقالَ هذا يَوْمٌ عَصِيبٌ): وقال is conjoined to ضاق; هذا is a mubtadaʾ; يوم a khabar and عصيب an adjective, and the sentence is the reported speech. (وَجاءَهُ قَوْمُهُ يُهْرَعُونَ إِلَيْهِ): the wāw is a conjunction; جاءه قومه: a verb, a direct object and an agent; the clause يهرعون is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl; and إليه is attached to يهرعون. (وَمِنْ قَبْلُ كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ السَّيِّئاتِ): the wāw is circumstantial; من قبل: من is a preposition and قبل an adverbial indeclinable on the ḍamma because it is cut off from annexation in wording but not in meaning, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يعملون; kāna and its ism; and the clause يعملون السيئات is the khabar of كانوا. (قالَ يا قَوْمِ هؤُلاءِ بَناتِي هُنَّ أَطْهَرُ لَكُمْ): هؤلاء is a mubtadaʾ and بناتي a khabar, and likewise His words هن أطهر لكم; they allowed بناتي to be a badal or an ʿaṭf bayān; هن is a separation pronoun with no position; أطهر is the khabar of هؤلاء; and لكم is attached to أطهر because it is an elative. An objection does not apply, the gist of which is that the elative implies sharing so that preference is valid, and so it would require that what they seek from men is pure; the answer is that this proceeds like «Is that better as a hospitality, or the tree of al-Zaqqūm?» (أذلك خير نزلا أم شجرة الزقوم), and it is known that there is no good at all in the tree of al-Zaqqūm. (فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَلا تُخْزُونِ فِي ضَيْفِي): the fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ; اتقوا الله: an imperative verb, an agent and a direct object; ولا تخزوني is conjoined to اتقوا الله; لا is prohibitive; تخزوني is jussive by لا, its sign of jussive being the deletion of the nūn; the nūn is for protection, the wāw is the agent and the yāʾ is a direct object; في ضيفي is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl. Al-ḍayf is originally a maṣdar, then it was applied to one who comes at night to the host, therefore it applies to masculine and feminine, singular, dual and plural; it can be dualized, so one says ḍayfān, and pluralized, so one says aḍyāf, ḍuyūf and ḍīfān. (أَلَيْسَ مِنْكُمْ رَجُلٌ رَشِيدٌ): the interrogative is for denunciation and reproach; ليس is an incomplete past verb; منكم is the fronted khabar of ليس; رجل is its postponed ism; and رشيد an adjective. (قالُوا: لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ ما لَنا فِي بَناتِكَ مِنْ حَقٍّ): علمت is suspended from acting by the negative ما; لنا is a fronted khabar; في بناتك is a ḥāl because it was originally an adjective of حق but was fronted; من is a redundant preposition; and حق is a postponed mubtadaʾ in position. (وَإِنَّكَ لَتَعْلَمُ ما نُرِيدُ): the wāw is a conjunction; inna and its ism; the shifted lām; the clause تعلم is its khabar; and ما may be maṣdariyya or relative, i.e. "you know what we want" or "you know our desire". (قالَ لَوْ أَنَّ لِي بِكُمْ قُوَّةً أَوْ آوِي إِلى رُكْنٍ شَدِيدٍ): لو is conditional; أن and what is in its scope is the agent of an omitted verb, its implied form being "had been established and settled"; as for Sībawayh, he sees it as a mubtadaʾ with no khabar, and the detail of that will come in the section on Benefits. أن is a particle resembling the verb, لي its fronted khabar, بكم a ḥāl from قوة since it was originally an adjective of an indefinite, and قوة the ism of أن. The response of لو is omitted, its implied form being "I would have done to you and made..."; أو is a conjunction; آوي is conjoined according to the meaning, the implied form of the speech being "or that I take refuge"; it is also permissible for the clause to be conjoined to the omitted clause ثبت if أن and what is in its scope is parsed as the agent of an omitted verb; and it is permissible that it be conjoined to قوة, because it was originally accusative by an implied أن, and when أن was omitted the verb became nominative, like His words «And among His signs He shows you» (ومن آياته يريكم); Abū al-Baqāʾ considered this view weak. إلى ركن is attached to آوي, and شديد is an adjective.
(قالُوا يا لُوطُ إِنَّا رُسُلُ رَبِّكَ لَنْ يَصِلُوا إِلَيْكَ): inna and its ism; رسل ربك is its khabar; لن is a particle of negation, accusative-governing, and futurity; يصلوا is an imperfect verb accusative by an implied أن; and إليك is attached to يصلوا. (فَأَسْرِ بِأَهْلِكَ بِقِطْعٍ مِنَ اللَّيْلِ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; بأهلك is a ḥāl, i.e. "accompanying them"; بقطع is a ḥāl from أهلك, i.e. "accompanying a portion"; you may make the bāʾ one of transitivity, attaching it to أسر; al-qiṭʿ here is half the night, because it is a portion of it equal to the rest; the discussion of al-qiṭʿ has already appeared in Sūrat Yūnus; and من الليل is an adjective of قطع. (وَلا يَلْتَفِتْ مِنْكُمْ أَحَدٌ إِلَّا امْرَأَتَكَ إِنَّهُ مُصِيبُها ما أَصابَهُمْ): the wāw is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive; يلتفت is an imperfect verb jussive by لا; منكم is a ḥāl because it was originally an adjective of أحد; أحد is the agent; إلا is a particle of exception; and امرأتك is excepted from His words فأسر بأهلك; in one reading it is nominative, a badal from أحد, and a detailed discussion of this exception will come. The meaning is "do not take her with you, but leave her behind with her people"; and it is said it is excepted from أحد. Then inna and its ism, the hāʾ being the pronoun of the matter and the account (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); مصيبها is a fronted khabar; ما is a relative noun, a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause أصابهم is the ṣila; and the sentence is the khabar of inna, because the pronoun of the matter is explained by a sentence whose two parts are stated. (إِنَّ مَوْعِدَهُمُ الصُّبْحُ أَلَيْسَ الصُّبْحُ بِقَرِيبٍ): inna and its ism; الصبح is its khabar; the hamza is for affirmative interrogation; ليس and its ism; the bāʾ is a redundant preposition; and قريب is genitive in form, in the position of the khabar of ليس. (فَلَمَّا جاءَ أَمْرُنا جَعَلْنا عالِيَها سافِلَها): لما is temporal or connective; جاء أمرنا: a verb and an agent; the clause جعلنا is the response of لما, نا being the agent; عاليها is the first direct object of جعل and سافلها the second direct object of جعلنا. (وَأَمْطَرْنا عَلَيْها حِجارَةً مِنْ سِجِّيلٍ مَنْضُودٍ مُسَوَّمَةً عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ): وأمطرنا is conjoined to جعلنا; عليها is attached to أمطرنا; حجارة is a direct object; من سجيل is an adjective of حجارة; منضود an adjective of سجيل; مسومة a second adjective of حجارة; and the adverbial عند ربك is attached to مسومة. (وَما هِيَ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ بِبَعِيدٍ): ما is the Ḥijāzī mā and هي its ism. There is disagreement about this pronoun: it is said it refers to the punishment understood from the context; it is said it refers to the stones, being the nearest mentioned; and it is said it refers to the destroyed towns; and all that they mentioned is permissible and sound. من الظالمين is attached to ببعيد; the bāʾ is a redundant preposition; and بعيد is genitive in form, in the position of the khabar of ما. It was not made feminine either because it was originally an adjective of an omitted place, its implied form being "and it is not at a distant place, but near"; or because ʿuqūba and ʿiqāb are one thing; or by interpreting the stones as punishment.

* Benefits:
1- Returning to «law»:
The discussion of law appeared in al-Baqara and elsewhere. Here we add the discussion of the noun occurring after the conditional law. It is well known that it is restricted to the verb, whether conditional or maṣdariyya, but a noun may follow it, in which case it is parsed as the agent of an omitted verb explained by what follows it. On this basis is explained the saying of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb to Abū ʿUbayda, when he was on his way to Syria and, during the journey, before arriving, news reached him that a plague had broken out there; he consulted about going toward it or returning to Medina, and they differed, then he made up his mind to return after a group of the Companions had advised it. Abū ʿUbayda ibn al-Jarrāḥ said to him: "Do you flee from the decree of Allah the Exalted?" ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said to him: "Had someone other than you said it, O Abū ʿUbayda! Yes, we flee from the decree of Allah to the decree of Allah." Thus غيرك is the agent of an omitted verb explained by قالها, the implied form being "law qālahā ghayruka", and the response of لو is omitted, i.e. "we would have excused him".
Al-Ghaṭamish al-Ḍabbī said:
أقول وقد فاضت لعيني عبرة ... أرى الأرض تبقى والأخلاء تذهب
(I say, while a tear has overflowed from my eye: I see the earth remaining and the friends departing.)
أخلاي لو غير الحمام أصابكم ... عتبت ولكن ما على الدهر معتب
(My friends! Had something other than death struck you, I would have reproached; but there is no reproaching Time.)
Thus غير is an agent of an omitted verb explained by أصابكم, the implied form being "had something other than al-ḥimām struck you" (al-ḥimām, with kasra on the ḥāʾ, is death) "I would have reproached". Among the remarks of al-Tibrīzī on this second verse is his saying: People recite "akhillāy" with a fatḥa on the yāʾ, as if they treated it as the shortening of the lengthened; but better by the rule of Arabic is to recite "akhillāʾ" with a kasra on the hamza, meaning "yā akhillāʾī", the yāʾ of annexation being dropped and the hamza left, as you say "yā ghulām". Also among such cases is their proverb «لو ذات سوار لطمتني» ("Had a woman wearing a bracelet slapped me"), taken from the saying of Ḥātim al-Ṭāʾī when a slave girl slapped him while he was a captive among some Arab clans; so ذات سوار is the agent of an omitted verb under the condition of explanation, the implied form being "law laṭamatnī dhāt siwār"; the one with the bracelet (dhāt al-siwār) is the free woman, because slave girls among the Arabs do not wear bracelets; and the response of لو is omitted, the implied form being "the matter would be lighter on me"; or it may be accusative by an omitted verb or a khabar of an omitted kāna. An example of the first: "Had I seen Zayd, I would have honoured him"; and of the second, as in "Seek, even a ring of iron" (التمس ولو خاتما من حديد), which has already been mentioned.
It is common for the doubled أن and its ṣila to follow law, as in «And if they had been patient» (ولو أنهم صبروا) and the verse we are at, which is «If only I had power over you» (لو أن لي قوة). There is disagreement over the i'rab of أن and what is in its scope, after all agreeing that it is nominative in position. Sībawayh and the majority of the Basrans said: it is a mubtadaʾ with no khabar, or its khabar is omitted, the implied form being "and had their patience been established"; while the Kufans, al-Zamakhsharī, and from the Basrans al-Mubarrad and al-Zajjāj went to the view that it is an agent of an implied "thabata", as mentioned before, i.e. "had their patience been established". More of the rulings of law will come in other places of this book.

2- The statements of the grammarians on «illā imraʾataka»:
The second benefit is the statements of the grammarians on the exception of امرأتك. They said:
«ولا يلتفت منكم أحد إلا امرأتك» with the nominative in the reading of Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Kathīr, so امرأتك is a badal from أحد, a part-from-whole badal; the accusative is good Arabic and is among the seven readings, but is contrary to the preferred, stronger one, and the one more widely read. Hence al-Zamakhsharī made the accusative an exception from أهلك, so that it is an exception from a complete positive (statement), and the nominative a badal from أحد; and it was objected that this entails a contradiction between the two readings, for the woman would be taken along on the nominative reading and not taken along on the accusative reading. The supporters of al-Zamakhsharī answered that her exclusion from the sentence of prohibition does not indicate that she was taken along, but that she was with them, and it has been reported that she followed them. Ibn Hishām refuted al-Zamakhsharī's i'rab and said that it is contrary to the apparent sense, and he expanded on this exception in the second direction of the fifth chapter.
I say: the most apparent of all this is that the exception is from the sentence of the command, i.e. "travel by night with your family", and the exception is discontinuous (munqaṭiʿ) in both readings; the justification of the nominative is that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the sentence after it, and in that case the accusative reading is good and not the weaker one, thereby avoiding the occurrence of the less preferred in the Qur'an. It has already been said concerning the son of Nūḥ «he is not of your family» (انه ليس من أهلك), because what is meant by "family" is the believers, and on this basis his wife is not of his family.

* Rhetoric:
In the words of Allah the Exalted: «Is not the morning near?» (أليس الصبح بقريب) is irsāl al-mathal or al-tamthīl (the sending forth of the proverb), a art that can be defined as what the speaker brings out running the course of current proverbs. It has already been alluded to and more of it will come. Our early scholars took pains to exhaust all the proverbs of the Noble Book, sūra by sūra in their order. As for Arabic poetry, we have mentioned earlier proverbs that the poet of immortality, Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī, included in his verses, and they came as a sign of originality, as we also mentioned a poem by Ibn Zaydūn. It is related that one of the shaykhs of al-Anbār in the time of al-Rashīd used to call the adhān and lead the prayer in a mosque, and when the time of the rose came he would hand the mosque's key to the people of the quarter, then plunge into the depths of his pleasure and not appear while there was a rose in the world. When he sat to his drink he would sing in a loud voice and say:
يا صاحبي اسقياني ... من قهوة خندريس
(O my two companions, give me to drink of old wine,)
خذا من الورد حظا ... بالقصف غير حبيس
(take your share of the rose, in revelry unrestrained,)
على وجينات ورد ... يذهبن همّ النفوس
(upon rose-like cheeks that banish the cares of souls.)
ما تنظران فهذا ... زمان حث الكؤوس
(What are you waiting for? This is the time of urging on the cups;)
فبادروا قبل فوت ... «لا عطر بعد عروس»
(so hasten before it is lost: "No perfume after the bride.")

farraa:1-3.t:
His saying: ﴿الۤر كِتَابٌ أُحْكِمَتْ آيَاتُهُ﴾.
You put «الكتاب» in the nominative (rafʿ) by the letters of the alphabet that precede it, as though you said: "The letters of the alphabet [are] this Qurʾān." If you wish, you may imply something to make it nominative, as though you said: "Alif Lām Rā: this is the Book."
His saying ﴿ثُمَّ فُصِّلَتْ﴾: with the lawful and the unlawful, and the command and the prohibition. That is why His saying ﴿ألاّ تعبدوا﴾ came.
Then He said ﴿وَأَنِ ٱسْتَغْفِرُواْ رَبَّكُمْ﴾, that is: its verses were set out in detail [to the effect] that you should not worship [other than Allah] and that you should seek forgiveness. So «أنْ» is in the position of the accusative (naṣb) because you dropped the preposition (al-khāfiḍ). «[Translator's note: the printed text reads «وأن استغفرا», evidently for «وأن استغفروا».]»

farraa:5-5.t:
His saying: ﴿أَلا إِنَّهُمْ يَثْنُونَ صُدُورَهُمْ لِيَسْتَخْفُواْ مِنْهُ﴾. It was revealed about some of those who used to meet the Prophet ﷺ with what he liked while concealing enmity and hatred towards him. That "folding" (al-thanī) is concealment. And Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said ﴿أَلا حِينَ يَسْتَغْشُونَ ثِيَابَهُمْ يَعْلَمُ الله﴾ what they conceal of enmity towards Muhammad ﷺ.
(Muḥammad related to us, saying:) al-Farrāʾ related to us, saying: The trustworthy ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak related to me from Ibn Jurayj, from a man — I think he was ʿAṭāʾ — from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he read (تَثْنَونى صُدُورُهُمْ). In Arabic it has the sense of «تَنْثَنى» ("they fold up"), as ʿAntara said:
وقولكَ للشىء الذى لا تناله * إذا ما هو احلولى أَلا ليت ذاليا
(And your saying, of the thing you cannot attain, when it has become very sweet: "Would that that were mine!")
It is of the verb pattern «افعوعلت» (ifʿawʿaltu).

farraa:6-6.t: His saying: ﴿وَيَعْلَمُ مُسْتَقَرَّهَا وَمُسْتَوْدَعَهَا﴾. Its «مستقرّ» is where it takes shelter by night or day. Its «مستودَع» is the place in which it dies or is buried.

farraa:7-7.t:
His saying: ﴿لَيَقُولَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوۤاْ إِنْ هَـٰذَآ إِلاَّ سِحْرٌ مُّبِينٌ﴾ (وسِحْر مبين). Whoever says (سَاحِرٌ مُبِينٌ) refers, in their words, to the Prophet ﷺ; whoever says (سِحْرٌ) refers to the speech. «[Translator's note: the printed text reads «ذهب إلا النبىّ», evidently for «ذهب إلى النبىّ».]»
(Muḥammad related to us, saying:) al-Farrāʾ related to us, saying: Abū Isrāʾīl related to me from al-Aʿmash, from Abū Razīn, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, that he read «ساحر» in three places: at the end of al-Māʾida, in Yūnus, and in al-Ṣaff.
al-Farrāʾ said: He did not mention the one in Hūd. Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb used to read it in four places and made this the fourth, meaning in Hūd.

farraa:11-11.t: His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ ٱلَّذِينَ صَبَرُواْ﴾ is in the position of the accusative by exception from His saying: ﴿ولَئِنْ أَذَقنَاهُ﴾, meaning man; then He made an exception from «الإنسان» because it has the sense of "people," as He, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿وَٱلعَصْرِ إنَّ الإنْسَانَ لَفِى خُسْرٍ إِلاَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾, so He excepted many from a singular word, because it is interpreted as a collective.

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿فَلَعَلَّكَ تَارِكٌ بَعْضَ مَا يُوحَىٰ إِلَيْكَ وَضَآئِقٌ بِهِ صَدْرُكَ﴾.
He is saying: your breast is straitened by what We reveal to you, so you do not convey it to them for fear that they say: "Why has a treasure not been sent down to you?" The «أن» in His saying ﴿أَنْ يَقُولوا﴾ is evidence of that. It is like His saying: ﴿يُبَيَّنُ اللّهُ لَكُمْ أَنْ تَضِلُّوا﴾. (مِن) would fit well in it and is then dropped, so it is in the position of the accusative, as He — Mighty and Majestic — said: ﴿يَجْعَلُونَ أَصَابِعَهُمْ فىِ آذَانِهِمْ مِنَ الصَّوَاعِقِ حَذَرَ الَموْتِ﴾. Do you not see that (مِنْ) fits well with «الحَذَر»? When it is dropped, it becomes accusative by the verb, not by the dropping of (من), as in the saying of the poet:
وأَغفرُ عوراء الكريم اصطناعَه * وأُعرِض عن ذات الّلئيم تَكَرُّماً
(I forgive the noble man's ugly word to win him over, and I turn away from the base man's [abuse] out of magnanimity.)

farraa:13-14.t: His saying: ﴿قُلْ فَأْتُواْ بِعَشْرِ سُوَرٍ مِّثْلِهِ مُفْتَرَيَاتٍ﴾. Then He, exalted be His mention, said: ﴿فَإِلَّمْ يَسْتَجِيبُواْ لَكُمْ﴾ and did not say «لك» ("to you", singular), though He had said at the beginning of the speech (قُلْ) and not «قولوا» ("say", plural). It is like His saying: ﴿عَلَى خَوْفٍ مِنْ فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَئِهِمْ﴾.

farraa:15-15.t:
His saying: ﴿مَن كَانَ يُرِيدُ ٱلْحَيَاةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَزِينَتَهَا﴾, then He said: (نُوَفِّ) [in the jussive], because the meaning lies in what comes after «كان». «كان» may be void in meaning, for a speaker says: «إن كنت تعطينى سألتك» ("if you would give me, I would ask you"), and it is like your saying: «إن أعطيتنى سألتك» ("if you give me, I will ask you"). Most often the condition (jazāʾ) comes such that it and its apodosis (jawāb) agree [in form]. If you say: «إن تفعل أَفعل», that is good. If you say: «إن فعلتَ أفعلْ», it is considered permissible. The [normal] speech is «إن فعلتَ فعلتُ». Zuhayr said, in permitting it:
ومن هاب أسباب المنايا ينلْنَه * ولو نال أسباب السمّاء بسُلّم
(Whoever fears the causes of death, they will reach him, even if he reached the tracts of the sky by a ladder.)
His saying: ﴿وَهُمْ فِيهَا لاَ يُبْخَسُونَ﴾. He is saying: whoever of the people of the qibla wants by his deeds the reward of this world, his reward is hastened for him and he is not shortchanged (lam yubkhas), that is, not diminished, in this world.

farraa:17-17.t:
His saying: ﴿أَفَمَن كَانَ عَلَىٰ بَيِّنَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّهِ وَيَتْلُوهُ شَاهِدٌ مِّنْهُ﴾ (The one upon clear evidence from his Lord is Muhammad ﷺ. «ويتلوه شاهد منه») means Gabriel (peace be upon him) recites the Qurʾān; the hāʾ [of «يتلوه»] refers to the Qurʾān. The explanation of that is: and a witness from Allah recites the Qurʾān. ﴿وَمِن قَبْلِهِ كِتَابُ مُوسَىٰ﴾: you put «الكتاب» in the nominative by «مِن». Or you could put it in the accusative, as in: "and he recites, before it, the Book of Moses." (إمَاماً) is accusative by qaṭʿ (detachment, i.e. as ḥāl) from (كتاب موسى) in both cases. It has also been said of His saying ﴿وَيَتْلُوهُ شَاهِدٌ مِّنْهُ﴾: it means the Gospel follows the Qurʾān, even though it was sent down before it; he takes it to mean that it follows it by confirming it. Then He said: and before the Gospel, the Book of Moses. «[Translator's note: the sentence beginning "Or you could put it in the accusative" has no completing clause in the source; it is translated as written.]»
No explicit apodosis (jawāb) came for His saying ﴿أَفَمَن كَانَ عَلَىٰ بَيِّنَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّهِ﴾, as in His saying in the Sūra of Muhammad ﷺ: ﴿أَفَمَنْ كَانَ عَلَى بَيِّنَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّهِ كَمَنْ زُيِّنَ لَهُ سُوءُ عَمَلِهِ﴾. The Arabs sometimes leave out the answer of a thing whose meaning is known, even though the answer is omitted. The poet said:
فأُقسم لو شَىْ أتانا رَسولُه * سِوَاك ولكن لم نجد لكَ مَدْفَعا
(I swear, if anything other than you had sent its messenger to us — but we found no way of repelling you.)
And Allah, Blessed and Exalted — and He is more truthful than the words of the poet — said: ﴿وَلَوْ أَنُّ قُرْآناً سُيِّرَتْ بِهِ الْجِبَالُ أَوْ قُطَّعَتْ بِهِ الأرْضُ﴾, and no answer was given for it, and Allah knows best. Some grammarians explain it, meaning that its answer is: (وَهُمْ يَكْفُرُونَ وَلَوْ أَنَّ قرآناً); but the first is closer to correct. Like it: ﴿وَلَوْ تَرَى إِذِ المُجْرِمُونَ﴾, ﴿وَلَوْ تَرَى الذِينَ ظَلَمُوا﴾, and His saying in al-Zumar: ﴿أَمْ مَنْ هُوَ قَانِتٌ آنَاءَ اللَّيْلِ سَاجداً وقَائِماً يَحْذَرُ الآخِرَةَ وَيَرْجُو رَحْمَةَ رَبِّهِ﴾, and no answer was given for it; His saying ﴿قُلْ هَلْ يَسْتَوِى الَّذِينَ يَعْلَمُونَ وَالَّذِينَ لاَ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ sufficed for it. So this is among the things whose answer is left out and what follows suffices for it. Likewise He said in Hūd: ﴿مَثَلُ الْفَرِيقَيْنِ كَالأَعْمَى وَالأصَمِّ وَالْبَصِيرِ وَالسَّمِيعِ هَلْ يَسْتَوِيَانِ مَثَلاً﴾ and did not say «هل يستوون» ("are they [plural] equal"). That is because the blind and the deaf are the description of one, and the seeing and the hearing are the description of one, as a speaker says: "I passed by the intelligent and the sensible man," meaning one person. The poet said:
وما أدرى إذا يمَّمت وجهاً * أريد الخير أيُّهما يلينى
أألخير الذى أنا أَبتغيه * أم الشر الذى لا يأتلينى
(I do not know, when I set out in some direction seeking good, which of the two will befall me: the good that I seek, or the evil that never fails to seek me.)
He said «أيّهما» ("which of the two") though he mentioned only the good, because the meaning is known: one who seeks good is guarding against evil. Likewise the saying of Allah, exalted be His mention: ﴿سَرَابِيلَ تَقِيكُم الْحَرَّ وَسَرَابِيلَ تَقِيكُمْ بَأْسَكُمْ﴾ [that is,] and they protect from the cold. It is so even though it is not mentioned.
His saying: ﴿وَمَن يَكْفُرْ بِهِ مِنَ ٱلأَحْزَابِ فَٱلنَّارُ مَوْعِدُهُ﴾: it is said [it means] of the kinds of unbelievers. And it is said that every unbeliever is a faction (ḥizb).

farraa:20-20.t: His saying: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ لَهُمْ مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مِنْ أَوْلِيَآءَ يُضَاعَفُ لَهُمُ ٱلْعَذَابُ﴾: then the heads of the unbelievers who lead astray. His saying: ﴿مَا كَانُواْ يَسْتَطِيعُونَ ٱلسَّمْعَ﴾ has two interpretations. Some exegetes explained it: the punishment is doubled for them because they were able to hear and did not do so. In that case the bāʾ ought to have entered, since He said: ﴿وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ بِمَا كَانُوا يَكْذِبُونَ﴾ — in more than one place in the Revelation the bāʾ has been brought in — but its omission is permissible, as you say in speech: «بأَحسن ما كانوا يعملون» and «وأحسنَ ما كانوا يعملون». And you say in speech: «لأجزينَّك بما عملت» and «وما عملت» ("I will surely repay you for what you did"). And it is said [the second interpretation]: they were not able to hear and they did not see, that is, Allah led them astray from that in the Preserved Tablet.

farraa:22-22.t:
His saying: ﴿لاَ جَرَمَ أَنَّهُمْ﴾. It is an expression that was originally equivalent to «لا بُدَّ أنّك قائم» ("there is no escaping that you are standing") and «لا محالة أَنّك ذاهب» ("inevitably you are going"); it ran on that pattern and their use of it became frequent until it came to mean «حقّا» ("truly"). Do you not see that the Arabs say: «لا جَرَم لآتينك» ("truly, I will come to you") and «لا جرم قد أحسنتَ» ("truly, you have done well")? And so the exegetes explained it in the sense of «الحقّ». Its origin is from «جَرَمت», that is, "I earned a sin," and «جَرَّمته». The saying of one who said that «جَرَمت» is like your saying «حَقُقت» or «حُقِقت» is of no account; the speaker was only confused by the saying of the poet:
ولقد طَعْنتُ أَبا عُيَيْنة طعنةً * جَرَمت فزارةُ بعدها أن تغضبا
(I dealt Abū ʿUyayna a thrust after which Fazāra were bound to be angry.)
They put (فَزارة) in the nominative and said: we make the verb belong to Fazāra, as if it were equivalent to «حُقَّ لها» or «حقَّ لها أن تغضب» ("it was right for her to be angry"). But «فَزارة» is accusative in the view of al-Farrāʾ, that is: the thrust brought upon them that they be angry.
Because of its frequency in speech, the mīm has been dropped from it, and the Banū Fazāra say: «لا جَرَ أَنك قائم». It is also joined at its beginning with «ذا»; one of the Banū Kilāb recited to me:
إن كلاباً والدِى لاذا جَرَمْ * لأَهْدِرَنَّ اليوم هدراً صادقا * هدر المعنَّى ذى الشقاشيق اللهِم *
(Kilāb is my father — truly, I shall roar today a true roar, the roar of a tethered stallion with frothing bladders, devouring.)
The position of «أنْ» is nominative, as in his saying:
أحقّا عبادَ الله جُرْأةُ مُحْلِقٍ * عَلَىَّ وقد أَعييتُ عادَ وتُبَّعا
(Is it true, O servants of Allah, that Muḥliq dares against me, when I have worn out ʿĀd and Tubbaʿ?)

farraa:23-23.t: His saying: ﴿وَأَخْبَتُوۤاْ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِمْ﴾. Its meaning is: they humbled themselves for their Lord and towards their Lord. The Arabs sometimes put (إلى) in the place of the lām. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿بِأَنَّ رَبَّكَ أَوْحَى لَهَا﴾, and He said: ﴿الْحَمْدُ لِلّهِ الَّذِى هَدَانَا لِهَذَا﴾, and He said: ﴿يَهْدِيهِمْ إِلَيْه صِرَاطاً مُسْتَقِيماً﴾, and He said: ﴿فَأَوْحَى إِلَيْهِمْ رَبُّهُمْ﴾. It is permissible in Arabic to say: «فلان يُخبِت إلى الله», meaning: he does that with his face turned towards Allah; for the meaning of al-ikhbāt is humility, so he is saying: he does it with his face towards Allah and for Allah. The exegesis has come: «وأَخبتوا فَرَقا من الله» ("they humbled themselves out of fear of Allah"); so «مِن» resembles the meaning of the lām and the meaning of «إلى» when you intend by it "on account of this" and "because of this."

farraa:27-27.t:
His saying: ﴿مَا نَرَاكَ إِلاَّ بَشَراً مِّثْلَنَا وَمَا نَرَاكَ ٱتَّبَعَكَ إِلاَّ ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ أَرَاذِلُنَا﴾. You put «الأراذل» in the nominative by «الاتّباع» (the verb "follow"), while the [first] verb at the beginning of the speech has fallen on its own noun. The Arabs hardly ever make what is brought back by «إلاّ» refer to anything but the mubtadaʾ (the head noun), not to a pronoun referring back to it; yet it is permissible. The clear case about which there is no question is to say: «ما قام أحد إلاّ زيد» ("no one stood except Zayd"). If you say: «ما أحد قام إلا زيد», putting Zayd in the nominative by what refers back in the verb of «أحد», it is rare but permissible. It is remote [to relate it] to the mubtadaʾ only because it is a pronoun (kināya), and in a pronoun no distinction is made between «أحد» and «عبدالله»; since it is ugly to say «ما قام هو إلاّ زيد» ("he did not stand except Zayd") and good to say «ما قام أحد إلا زيد», that became clear, because «أحد» is as if it were not in the speech, so referring [the excepted noun] to the verb is good. And «أحد» is not said of a definite noun or a pronoun, since — resembling a definite noun — it is as if it were not in the speech. Do you not see that you say «ما مررت بأحد إلا بزيد» (so it is as if you said: «ما مررت إلا بزيد» "I passed by none but Zayd"), because «أحد» is not conceived in the mind as something aimed at? And it is ugly to say «ليس أحد مررت به إلاّ بزيد», because the hāʾ has a form like that of a definite noun, and you do not say «ما قمت إلا زيد»; this is the reason for its ugliness. Likewise He said (ما نراك), then it is as though He dropped (نراك) and said: (ما اتَّبعك إلا الذين هم أراذلنا). So build on this whatever comes to you, if Allah wills.
﴿بَادِيَ ٱلرَّأْيِ﴾: do not put a hamza in (بادى), because the meaning is "in what appears (yaẓhar) to us and becomes manifest (yabdū)." Were you to read (بادئ الرأى) with hamza, meaning "at first thought," it would be correct. Someone recited to me:
أضحى لخالى شبهى بادى بدى * وصار للفحل لسانى ويدى
(My likeness to my maternal uncle became apparent at first sight, and my tongue and my hand came to belong to the stallion.)
and he did not put a hamza. Like it is what the Arabs say in the sense of "begin with this first": then they say: «ابدأ بهذا آثراً مّا», «وآثِر ذى أثِير» («وأثير ذى أثير»), «وإثْرَ ذى أثير», «وابدأ بهذا أوَّل ذاتِ يدين» and «وأدْنَى دَنِىّ». And they recited to us:
فقالوا ما تريد فقلت ألهو * إلى الإصباح آثِر ذى أَثِير
(They said: What do you want? I said: To amuse myself until morning, before anything else.)
His saying: ﴿بَلْ نَظُنُّكُمْ كَاذِبِينَ﴾ is like His saying ﴿يأيّها النَّبِىُّ إِذَا طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّساَء﴾, because they called Noah alone a liar, and it came out in the form of the plural; and His saying ﴿فَإنْ لَمْ يَسْتَجيبُوا لَكُمْ﴾: by «لكم» the Prophet ﷺ is meant. And His saying: ﴿فاعْلَمُوا﴾ is not for the Prophet ﷺ; it is only for the unbelievers of Mecca. Do you not see that He said ﴿فَهَلْ أَنْتُم مُسْلِمونَ﴾?

farraa:28-28.t:
His saying: ﴿وَآتَانِي رَحْمَةً مِّنْ عِندِهِ﴾.
It means the message (al-risāla); it is a favour and a mercy. His saying: ﴿فَعُمِّيَتْ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾: Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read it [so]. In the reading of Ubayy it is (فعمَّاهَا عَلَيْكُمْ). I have heard the Arabs say: «قد عُمِّىَ علىَّ الخَبَر» and «عَمِىَ علىَّ» with one meaning ("the news was obscured to me"). This is one of the cases where the Arabs shifted the verb onto something to which it does not belong, it originally belonging to something else; do you not see that it is the man who is blind to the news, or is blinded to it? But in its permissibility it is like the Arabs' saying: «دخل الخاتمُ فى يدى والخُفّ فى رِجْلى» ("the ring entered my hand and the boot my foot"), while you know that it is the foot that is put into the boot and the finger into the ring. They took liberties with that because the meaning is known — it does not belong to this one at one time and to that one at another; it belongs only to one. So they allowed that for this reason. The general body of readers read it (فعَمِيَتْ). «[Translator's note: the printed text reads «قاستخفّوا», evidently for «فاستخفّوا» ("they took liberties").]»
His saying ﴿أَنُلْزِمُكُمُوهَا﴾: the Arabs make the mīm of «اللزوم» quiescent and say: «أَنُلْزِمْكُمُوهَا». That is because the vowels have come in succession, so the mīm was made quiescent because of its own vowel and two vowels after it, and because it is nominative [i.e. carries ḍamma]; were it accusative, it would not be felt heavy and lightened. They feel heavy only a kasra followed by a ḍamma, or a ḍamma followed by a kasra, or two kasras in succession, or two ḍammas in succession. As for the two ḍammas, it is His saying: ﴿لاَ يَحْزُنْهُمْ﴾: they made the nūn quiescent because there is a ḍamma before it, and it was lightened, as they say (رُسْل). As for the two kasras, it is like their saying «الإبلْ» when lightened. As for the ḍamma and the kasra, it is like the saying of the poet:
وناعٍ يُخَبِّرنا بمُهْلَك سَيّدٍ * تَقَطَّع من وجد عليه الأناملُ
(And a herald of death informing us of the death of a lord, for grief over whom fingertips are cut to pieces.)
and if you wish, «تُقطَّع». And his saying with the two kasras:
* إِذا اعوجَجْن قلت صَاحِبْ قوِّمِ *
(When they swerved I said: "Companion, set them straight!")
meaning «صَاحبى». Ḍamma and kasra are felt heavy only because their articulation costs effort for the tongue and lips: the lips are rounded for the rafʿ, so the ḍamma is heavy, and one side of the mouth is drawn towards the kasra, so you find that heavy; whereas the fatḥa comes out of the opening of the mouth without effort. «[Translator's note: the printed text reads «منصولة», evidently for «منصوبة» ("accusative"), and the phrase «أو يُسْتَثْقَل» appears to be a stray repetition; both are translated as intended.]»

farraa:30-30.t:
His saying: ﴿وَيٰقَوْمِ مَن يَنصُرُنِي مِنَ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
He is saying: who will protect me from Allah? And likewise everything of this in the Qurʾān: «النصر» is in the sense of protection.

farraa:35-35.t:
His saying: ﴿فَعَلَيَّ إِجْرَامِي﴾.
He is saying: then upon me is my sin. In the exegesis it has come as "then upon me are my sins," so if it were read «أجرامى» according to the exegesis, it would be correct. Abū al-Jarrāḥ recited to me:
لا تجعلونى كذوى الأجرام * الدَّهْمَسِيَّيْنِ ذوِى ضِرغام
(Do not make me like the men of crimes, the two secretive ones, the men of lion-like fierceness.)
So he pluralised «الجُرْم» as «أجرام». Like that is ﴿واللهُ يَعْلَمُ إِسْرَارَهُمْ﴾ and (أَسْراَرهم); it has been read both ways. Of it also is ﴿وَمِنَ اللّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْهُ وإِدْبَارَ السُّجُودِ﴾ and (أَدْبَارَ السُّجُودِ). Whoever says (إِدْبَارَ) means the maṣdar (verbal noun), and whoever says (أسرار) means the plural of «السِّر».

farraa:36-36.t: His saying: ﴿فَلاَ تَبْتَئِسْ بِمَا كَانُواْ يَفْعَلُونَ﴾. He is saying: (do not be abased and do not grieve).

farraa:37-37.t: His saying: ﴿بِأَعْيُنِنَا وَوَحْيِنَا﴾ is like His saying ﴿ارْجِعُونِ﴾: it comes out in the plural while its meaning is singular, in line with what I explained to you of His saying ﴿بَلْ نَظُنُّكُمْ كاذِبِينَ﴾ [said] to Noah alone, and ﴿عَلَي خَوْفٍ مِنْ فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَئِهِمْ﴾.

farraa:40-40.t: His saying: ﴿وَفَارَ ٱلتَّنُّورُ﴾: it is the baker's oven. [The meaning is:] when water gushes up from the hottest place in your house, that is the sign of the punishment, so set out by night with your family. His saying ﴿مِن كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنِ ٱثْنَيْنِ﴾: the male and the female of every kind are a pair. His saying ﴿وَأَهْلَكَ إِلاَّ مَن سَبَقَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقَوْلُ﴾: he carried with him a wife of his other than the one who perished, three sons and their wives, and eighty people besides. That is His saying ﴿وَمَنْ آمَنَ وَمَآ آمَنَ مَعَهُ إِلاَّ قَلِيلٌ﴾, and (the eighty) are the "few."

farraa:41-41.t:
His saying: ﴿وَقَالَ ٱرْكَبُواْ فِيهَا بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ﴾ ﴿إن شئت جَعلت مَجْرها ومَرْساها﴾ in the position of the nominative by the bāʾ, as you say: "its sailing and its anchoring are in the name of Allah and by the command of Allah." «[Translator's note: the printed text places «إن شئت جعلت مجرها ومرساها» inside Qurʾānic brackets, though it is al-Farrāʾ's own wording ("if you wish, you may make «مجراها ومرساها»…"); translated as written.]» If you wish, you may make (بسم الله) a beginning sufficient in itself, like the saying of someone at slaughtering or at beginning a meal and the like: "In the name of Allah"; and (مجريها ومرسيها) is then in the position of the accusative, meaning: in the name of Allah at its sailing and at its anchoring. I have heard the Arabs say: «الحمد لله سِرَارَك وإِهلالك» ("praise be to Allah [from] your waning to your waxing"), and it has been heard from them: «الحمد لله ما إِهلالَك إِلى سرارك», meaning: between your crescent and your waning.
«المجرى» and «المرسى» — with ḍamma on both their mīms: Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī, al-Ḥasan and the people of Medina read thus. Muḥammad related to us, saying: al-Farrāʾ related to us, saying: Abū Muʿāwiya related to us from al-Aʿmash, from Muslim ibn Ṣubayḥ, from Masrūq, that he read it (مَجْراها) with fatḥa on the mīm and (مُرسها) with ḍamma on the mīm. He said: And al-Farrāʾ related to us, saying: Abū Muʿāwiya and others related to us from al-Aʿmash, from a man whom he named, from ʿArfaja, that he heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd read it (مجراها) with fatḥa on the mīm and with ḍamma on the mīm of «مرسيها». Mujāhid read (مُجْرِيها ومُرسِيها), making it among the attributes of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; it is then in the position of the genitive (khafḍ) in i'rab, because it is definite. It may also be accusative, because the like of it may be indefinite, since the alif and lām fit well on both of them; do you not see that you say in speech: «بسم الله المجريها والمرسِيها»? When you remove the alif and lām from it, you put it in the accusative. What shows you its indefiniteness is His saying: ﴿هَذَا عَارِضٌ مُمْطِرُنَا﴾ and His saying: ﴿فَلَمّا رَأَوْهُ عَارِضاً مُسْتَقْبِلَ أَوْدِيَتِهِمْ﴾: they annexed it to a definite noun and made it the naʿt (adjective) of an indefinite noun. And the poet said:
يا رُبَّ عابِطنا لو كان يأْمُلكم * لا قى مباعدةً منكم وحرمانا
(Many a one who envies us, had he hoped in you, would have met with distance and deprivation from you.)
And another's saying:
وَيا رب هاجى مِنْقَرٍ يبتغى به * ليَكْرُم لمّا أعوزته المكارمُ
(And many a satirist of Minqar seeks thereby to be thought noble, when noble deeds have failed him.)
And al-Kisāʾī heard a Bedouin say after the breaking of the fast: «رُبّ صائمه لن يصومه وقائمه لن يقومه» ("many a one who fasted it will not fast it [again], and who prayed in it will not pray in it [again]").

farraa:43-43.t:
His saying: ﴿سَآوِيۤ إِلَىٰ جَبَلٍ يَعْصِمُنِي مِنَ ٱلْمَآءِ﴾. (قَالَ) Noah (peace be upon him): ﴿لاَعَاصِمَ اليَوْمَ مِنْ أمرِ الله إلاَّ مَنْ رَحِمَ﴾. «مَن» is in the position of the accusative, because the one protected is other than the protector, and the one shown mercy is protected; so it is as though he put it in the accusative in the manner of His saying ﴿مَالَهُمْ بِهِ مِنْ عِلْمٍ إلاَّ اتّباع الظَّنِّ﴾. Whoever permits the nominative of «الاتّباع», or the nominative in the poet's saying:
وبلدٍ ليس به أنيسُ * إلاَّ اليَعَافِيرُ وَإِلاَّ العِيسُ
(And many a land with no companion in it except gazelles and white camels.)
it is not permissible for him to use the nominative in (مَن), because the one who said (إلاّ اليعافيرُ) made the gazelles and wild beasts the companions of the desert; likewise His saying ﴿إلاَّ اتِّبَاع الظَّنِّ﴾ is saying: their knowledge is conjecture. But in no way may you say: the protected is the protector. However, if you took «العاصم» in the sense of «معصوم», as though you said: "there is none protected today from the command of Allah," the nominative of (مَن) would be permissible. Do not deny that the passive participle (mafʿūl) may come out in the form of the active (fāʿil); do you not see His saying ﴿مِنْ مَاءٍ دَافِقٍ﴾, whose meaning — and Allah knows best — is "poured out" (madfūq), and His saying ﴿فىِ عِيِشَةٍ رَاضِيَةٍ﴾, whose meaning is "pleasing" (marḍiyya)? And the poet said:
دعِ المكارمَ لا ترحل لِبُغيتها * واقعد فإنك أنت الطاعم الكاسى
(Leave noble deeds — do not travel in quest of them — and sit, for you are the one fed and clothed.)
Its meaning is «المكسوّ» ("the clothed"). You can deduce that from the fact that you say «رضيتُ هذه المعيشةَ» ("I was pleased with this life") but not «رَضِيَتْ» [of the life itself], and «دُفِق الماء» ("the water was poured out") but not «دَفَق», and you say «كُسِى العريان» ("the naked man was clothed") but not «كسا». It is also read (إلاّ من رُحِم). And had it been said «لا عاصم اليوم من أمر الله إلاّ من رُحِم», it would be as though you said: Allah does not protect today any but the one shown mercy; but we have not heard anyone read it so.

farraa:44-44.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱسْتَوَتْ عَلَى ٱلْجُودِيِّ﴾: it is a mountain at Ḥaḍanān in the land of Mosul; its yāʾ is doubled. I have been told that one of the readers read (عَلَى الجُودِى) with the yāʾ unstressed. If that is sound, it is among the words that were used much by its people and so were lightened; or it may have been named with a feminine verb form like «حُطىِّ», «أصِرّى» and «صَرِّى», and then the alif and lām were brought in. Someone recited to me — he was al-Mufaḍḍal —:
وكفرتَ قوماً هُمْ هَدَوكَ لأقدِمى * إِذا زَجْر أبيكَ سَأْسَاْ واربُق
(And you were ungrateful to a people who guided you to «أقدمي» ["go forward!"], when your father's urging [of his donkey] was "saʾsaʾ" and "irbuq.")
And one of the Banū Asad recited to me:
لمّا رأيت أنها فى حُطّى * وفَتكتْ فى كذبى ولَطِّى
(When I saw that she was in "ḥuṭṭī" and went to extremes in my lying and my concealing.)
When the Arabs make the like of «حُطّى» and its kin a name and want to change it away from the verbal pattern, they turn the yāʾ into alif and say: «حُطَّا», «أصِرَّا» and «صِرَّا». Likewise those Persian names ending in yāʾ, such as «ماهى», «شاهى» and «شُنىِّ», they turn into alif and say: «ماها», «شاها» and «شنَّا». Someone recited to us:
أتانا حِمَاسٌ بابن ماها يسوقه * لِتُبْغِيه خيراً وليْسَ بفاعل
(Ḥimās came to us driving Ibn Māhā, that you might seek good for him — and he will not do it.)
﴿وَحَال بَيْنَهُمَا المَوْجُ﴾, that is: the water came between Noah's son and the mountain.
His saying: ﴿يٰأَرْضُ ٱبْلَعِي﴾: one says «بَلِعَتْ» and «بَلَعَتْ».

farraa:46-46.t:
His saying: ﴿يٰنُوحُ إِنَّهُ لَيْسَ مِنْ أَهْلِكَ﴾ whom I [promised] to save. «[Translator's note: the source has a gap here: «الذى و-- أنجيهم».]» Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿إِنَّهُ عَمَلٌ غَيْرُ صَالِحٍ﴾ (and the general body of readers follow it). Muḥammad related to us, saying: al-Farrāʾ related to us, saying: Ḥibbān related to me from al-Kalbī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, to that effect; he says: your asking Me about that of which you have no knowledge is a deed that is not righteous. And the general body of readers follow it.
