The clause «واتخذتموه» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the word of majesty (Allah), in the position of the accusative. «ما» in «بما تعملون» is maṣdariyya, and the preposition "with your deeds" (بعملكم) is attached to the khabar «محيط».

harrat-mujtaba:93-93.t: The preposition «على مكانتكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw in «اعملوا». The clause «إني عامل» is resumptive, and the clause «سوف تعلمون» is resumptive within the scope of the answer to the vocative. «من يأتيه»: a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The clause «وارتقبوا» is conjoined to the clause «تعلمون». «رقيب»: a second khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:94-94.t: «ولما»: the wāw is resumptive, and a particle of "occurrence upon occurrence" (wujūb li-wujūb). The preposition «منا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «رحمة». The preposition «في ديارهم» is attached to the khabar (predicate) of «أصبح», «جاثمين». The clause «فأصبحوا» is conjoined to the clause «أخذت».

harrat-mujtaba:95-95.t: «كأن لم يغنوا»: a lightened abrogating particle, and its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn). The clause «كأن لم يغنوا» is a second khabar (predicate) of the verb «أصبحوا», in the position of the accusative, and the clause «لم يغنوا» is the khabar of «كأن», in the position of the nominative. «بعدًا» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and its clause is resumptive. The preposition «لمدين» is a naʿt (adjective) of «بُعدًا». The kāf in «كما» is a noun meaning "like", an adjective of «بعدا»; «ما» is maṣdariyya, and the maṣdar (verbal noun) is muḍāf ilayhi (in genitive construct).

harrat-mujtaba:97-97.t: The preposition «إلى فرعون» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the preceding {أَرْسَلْنَا}. The clause «وما أمر فرعون برشيد» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the preceding «أمر فرعون», and the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) in the khabar (predicate) of «ما», which operates like laysa.

harrat-mujtaba:98-98.t: The clause «يقدم» is resumptive, and the clause «فأوردهم» is conjoined to the resumptive one. «وبئس الورد المورود»: the wāw is resumptive; a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); «المورود» is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "it". The implied form of the speech is: "evil is the place of watering — it is the one watered at", i.e. the Fire. The clause is circumstantial, and the clause "it is the one watered at" is explicative of the clause of blame.

mekki-muskil:107-107.t:
His saying {مَا دَامَت السَّمَاوَات وَالْأَرْض}: مَا is an adverb (ẓarf) in the position of accusative; its implied form is "the time of the lasting of the heavens and the earth".
His saying {إِلَّا مَا شَاءَ رَبك}: مَا is in the position of accusative as an exception (istithnāʾ) that is not from [the genus of] the first.

mekki-muskil:108-108.t: His saying {وَأما الَّذين سعدوا}: the reading of Ḥafṣ, al-Kisāʾī and Ḥamza is with ḍamma on the sīn (سُعِدوا), on the analogy of their saying مَسْعُود, and it is a rare, anomalous (shādhdh) usage. Their saying مَسْعُود came only by dropping the augment, as though from أسعده الله, while one does not say سعده الله; so it is like their saying أجنه الله فَهُوَ مَجْنُون: مجنون came on the pattern of جنه الله even though that is not said; likewise مَسْعُود came on the pattern of سعده الله even though that is not said. The ḍamma on the sīn in سعدوا is far-fetched according to most grammarians, except on the assumption of dropping the augment, as though He said وَأما الَّذين أسعدوا.

mekki-muskil:111-111.t:
His saying {وَإِن كلا لما ليوفينهم}: whoever reads إن with shadda brings it in its original form and makes it govern كل; the lām in لما is a lām of emphasis entering on مَا, which is the khabar (predicate) of إن, and ليوفينهم is the answer to the oath. Its implied form is: "and indeed all are a creation — or are human beings — whom He will surely pay in full (وَإِن كلا لخلق أَو لبشر ليوفينهم)". It is not good for مَا to be redundant (zāʾida), for then the lām would be entering on ليوفينهم, and its entering on the lām of the oath is not permissible. It has been said that مَا is redundant, but entered to separate between the two lāms that receive the oath, both of which are with fatḥa, so they were separated by مَا.
As for whoever lightens إن, he lightened it out of finding the doubling heavy, and made it govern كل just as it governs when doubled, and the lām in لما remains as it is.
As for the doubling of لمّا in the reading of ʿĀṣim, Ḥamza and Ibn ʿĀmir, its origin is لمن مَا; then the nūn was assimilated into the mīm, so three mīms came together in pronunciation, and the mīm with kasra was dropped. Its implied form is: "and indeed all are of those whom He created; your Lord will surely pay them in full (وان كلا لمن خلق ليوفينهم رَبك)". It has also been said that the implied form is لمَن مَا, with fatḥa on the mīm of من, so that مَا is redundant, and one of the mīms is dropped because of the repetition of the mīm in pronunciation, as we have mentioned; so the implied form is "for a creation whom He will surely pay in full (لخلق ليوفينهم)".
It has been said that لمّا in this place is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of لمّ ("to gather"), but it was treated in continuous speech as it is treated in pausal form; this is far-fetched, because treating something in continuous speech as it is treated in pause is permissible only in poetry. It has been related that al-Kisāʾī said: "I do not know the rationale for the doubling in لمّا." Al-Zuhrī read لمًّا, doubled and with nunation, as the maṣdar of لمّ.
If you made إن, in the state of lightening, mean مَا (negation), you would put كل in the nominative, and the doubling in لمّا would carry the meaning of إِلَّا ("except"), as He said إِن كل نفس لما عَلَيْهَا, meaning "there is no soul but that over it…", according to the reading of whoever doubles لمّا. In the codex (ḥarf) of Ubayy: وَإِن كل إِلَّا ليوفينهم, with إن meaning مَا. Al-Aʿmash read وَإِن كل لما ليوفينهم, making إن mean مَا and لمّا mean إِلَّا, with كل in the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) in all of that and ليوفينهم as the khabar. It has also been said that مَا is redundant in the reading of whoever lightens [لما], and ليوفينهم is the khabar.

mekki-muskil:116-116.t:
His saying {إِلَّا قَلِيلا مِمَّن أنجينا مِنْهُم}: accusative as a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ). Al-Farrāʾ permitted the nominative in it as a badal (substitute) from أولو; in his view it is like His saying إِلَّا قوم يُونُس: it is a disconnected exception, and in his view the nominative is permissible in it as a substitute, as [the poet] said:
... وبدلة لَيْسَ بهَا أنيس ... إِلَّا اليعافير والا العيس ...
(And many a land with no companion in it, except young gazelles and white camels.)
He put اليعافير in the nominative as a substitute from أنيس, whereas its due is the accusative, because it is a disconnected exception from the sentence.

mekki-muskil:87-87.t: His saying {أَو أَن نَفْعل فِي أَمْوَالنَا مَا نشَاء}: whoever reads it with the nūn in both [verbs] conjoins it to the object of نَتْرُك, which is مَا; it is not permissible to conjoin it to the object of تأمرك, which is أَن, because the meaning would change. Whoever reads مَا تشَاء with the tāʾ, then أَو أَن نَفْعل is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the object of تأمرك, which is أَن, unlike the first view. Whoever reads تفعل and تشاء with the tāʾ in both, it is permissible to conjoin أَو أَن تفعل to the object of نَتْرُك, which is مَا, and to the object of تأمرك, which is أَن. We have explained this verse on its own in another book.

mekki-muskil:89-89.t: His saying {شقاقي}: its meaning is "my opposition (مشاقي)", and it is in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as the agent of يجرمنكم.

mekki-muskil:91-91.t: His saying {ضَعِيفا}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the kāf in نرَاك, because it is from seeing with the eye.

mekki-muskil:93-93.t: His saying {من يَأْتِيهِ}: من is in the position of accusative (manṣūb) by تعلمون. In meaning it is like وَالله يعلم الْمُفْسد من المصلح, i.e. He knows these two kinds; likewise the meaning in the verse is: you will come to know these two kinds. Al-Farrāʾ permitted من to be interrogative, in which case it is in the position of nominative. The fact that the second من is a relative noun indicates that the first is also a relative noun and not an interrogative.

mekki-muskil:1-1.t: If you make هود a name for the sūra and say هذه هود ("this is Hūd"), it is a diptote according to Sībawayh and al-Khalīl, like a woman whom you named Zayd or ʿAmr. ʿĪsā [ibn ʿUmar] allowed it to be fully declined because of its lightness, just as هند, the name of a woman, is declined. If you assume the omission of a muḍāf (first term of a genitive construct) with هود, you decline it, meaning "this is the sūra of Hūd".

mekki-muskil:11-11.t: His saying {إِلَّا الَّذين صَبَرُوا}: الذين is in the position of the accusative as a connected exception (istithnāʾ muttaṣil). Al-Farrāʾ said: it is excepted from الإنسان, because that has the meaning of "people". Al-Akhfash said: it is a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ).

mekki-muskil:16-16.t: His saying {وباطل مَا كَانُوا يعْملُونَ}: باطل is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and what follows it is its khabar (predicate). In the ḥarf (reading) of Ubayy and Ibn Masʿūd it is وباطلاً in the accusative: they made ما redundant (zāʾida) and made باطلا accusative by يعملون, like قليلا ما تذكرون and قليلا ما تؤمنون.

mekki-muskil:17-17.t:
His saying {ويتلوه شَاهد}: the hāʾ in يتلوه is for the Qurʾān; on this view the hāʾ in منه is for Allah, exalted be His mention, and the witness is the Gospel, i.e. the Gospel from Allah follows the Qurʾān in being placed before it; so the hāʾ in قبله is also for the Gospel. It has been said that the hāʾ in يتلوه is for Muhammad, Allah bless him; then the witness is his tongue, and the hāʾ in منه is also for Muhammad, Allah bless him — and it has been said: for the Qurʾān — and likewise the hāʾ in قبله is for Muhammad, Allah bless him. It has been said that the witness is Gabriel, upon him be peace; on this view the hāʾ in منه is for Allah the Exalted, and in من قبله it is also for Gabriel. It has been said that the witness is the inimitability of the Qurʾān; on this view the hāʾ in منه is for Allah the Exalted, the hāʾ in قبله is for the Qurʾān, and the hāʾ in يؤمنون به is for the Qurʾān — and it has been said: for Muhammad, upon him be peace.
His saying {إِمَامًا وَرَحْمَة}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from كتاب موسى.

mekki-muskil:20-20.t: His saying {مَا كَانُوا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ السّمع}: ما is an adverb (ẓarf) in the position of the accusative; its meaning is "as long as", for ever. It has been said that ما is in the position of the accusative by omission of the preposition, i.e. "for what they used to…" (بما كانوا), just as one says جزيته ما فعل and بما فعل ("I repaid him [for] what he did"). It has been said that ما is negating, and the meaning is "they could not hear because of what had preceded for them [in decree]". And it has been said that the meaning is: they could not bear to hear from the Prophet, Allah bless him, because of their hatred of him, nor understand an argument — as you say "so-and-so cannot bear to look at so-and-so" when that is burdensome to him.

mekki-muskil:22-22.t:
His saying {لَا جرم أَنهم}: لا جرم according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh has the meaning of "truly" (حقا), in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); لا and جرم are a single word, made indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and the khabar (predicate) is أنهم; so أنّ is in the position of the nominative according to both of them. It is also reported of al-Khalīl that he said: أنّ is in the position of the nominative by جرم, and جرم has the meaning of بُدّ, so its meaning is "no escape" and "inevitably". Al-Khalīl said: لا was brought so that it be known that the addressee did not begin his speech, but was only answering one who had addressed him. Al-Zajjāj said: لا is a negation of what they thought would benefit them. The original meaning of جرم is "earned", from their saying فلان جارم أهله, i.e. their earner; from it a sin is called جرم, because it is earned. So the meaning according to him is: "that does not benefit them"; then He began and said جرم أنهم في الآخرة هم الأخسرون, i.e. that deed earned them loss in the Hereafter; so on this view أنّ of أنهم is in the position of the accusative by جرم. Al-Kisāʾī said: its meaning is "there is no turning away and no preventing from their being in the Hereafter…", so أنّ on his view too is in the position of the accusative, by omission of the preposition.
«[Translator's note: the text reads «لاصد», evidently for «لا صدّ».]»

mekki-muskil:27-27.t:
His saying {بَادِي الرَّأْي}: بادي is accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), i.e. "in the first appearance of opinion"; this is on the reading of whoever does not pronounce it with hamza. It is also permissible for it to be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) with which a preposition has been omitted, like واختار موسى قومه. فاعل was permitted to be an adverb only as that is permitted for فعيل, such as قريب and مليء; فاعل and فعيل alternate, such as راحم and رحيم, عالم and عليم. That is good in فاعل because it is annexed to الرأي, and الرأي is something to which a maṣdar (verbal noun) is annexed, with the maṣdar becoming accusative with it as an adverb, as in your saying أما جهدَ رأيي فإنك منطلق ("as for my best opinion, you are leaving"). What governs the adverb is اتبعك. It is from بدا يبدو when something appears. In the reading of whoever does not use hamza it is also permissible for it to be from beginning (الابتداء), but he lightened the hamza. Whoever reads it with hamza, or assumes that the alif is a substitute for a hamza, also has it accusative as an adverb, and what governs it is again اتبعك.
So the implied form according to the one who takes it from بدا يبدو is: "No one has followed you, O Noah, except the lowest, as far as appears to us of opinion", as though they decided against him at the first that appeared to them of their opinion and did not follow it up with consideration; they only said what appeared to them without certainty. The implied form according to the one who takes it from beginning, and so uses hamza, is: "No one has followed you, O Noah, except the lowest at the start of the matter", i.e. "we do not see that, at the start of the matter, anyone followed you except the lowest".
The adverb was permitted to come late, after إلا and what follows it of the agent and its complement, because with adverbs a latitude is allowed that is not allowed with objects. If you said in ordinary speech ما أعطيت أحدا إلا زيدا درهما ("I gave no one except Zayd a dirham"), placing two nouns as objects after إلا, it would not be permissible, because the verb does not reach two nouns by means of إلا; it reaches only one noun, like the other particles. Do you not see that if you said مررت بزيد عمرو, making the verb reach both by one particle, it would not be permissible? Likewise if you said استوى الماء والخشبة الحائط, making two nouns accusative by one wāw, it would not be permissible — unless in all of that you bring the conjunctive wāw, and then it is permissible, and the verb reaches both by two particles. As for their saying ما ضرب القوم إلا بعضهم بعضا ("the people did not strike, except some of them [struck] others"), it was permitted only because بعضهم is a badal (substitute) from القوم, so the verb did not reach, after إلا, more than one noun.
«[Translator's note: the sentence «فالتقدير عنه قد جعله من بدأ يبدو» is as printed; «عنه» is evidently for «عند من». It is translated accordingly.]»

mekki-muskil:28-28.t:
His saying {فعميت عَلَيْكُم}: whoever among the readers reads it without doubling takes it in the sense of "you were blind to the reports that came to you", which are the mercy, so you did not believe in them; the reports themselves were not blind to them — had they been blind, they would have had an excuse in that; it is only they who were blind to them. So it is an inversion (maqlūb), like their saying أدخلت القلنسوة في رأسي ("I put the cap into my head") and أدخلت القبر زيدا ("I put the grave into Zayd"); you said all of this according to the outward wording, because the meaning is not obscure. Similar to it is the saying of the Exalted فلا تحسبن الله مخلف وعده رسله. It has been said that the meaning of فعميت, for the one who reads it without doubling, is "it was hidden"; on this view it is not inverted, and the reports that came from Allah — their understanding was hidden from them because of their little concern for them and their frequent turning away from them.
As for its meaning in the reading of Ḥafṣ, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī, who read it with doubling and ḍamma as a passive (فعُمِّيت), there is no inversion in it; rather, Allah made it blind to them because of the wretchedness He intended for them — He does what He wills, glory be to Him. This goes back to the first reading, because they were not blind to it until Allah made it blind to them. Ubayy read — and it is the reading of al-Aʿmash — فعمّاها عليكم, i.e. "Allah made it blind to you"; this is evidence for whoever reads with ḍamma and doubling.
نوح, the name of the Prophet, upon him be peace, is fully declined because it is foreign and light. It has been said that it is Arabic, from ناح ينوح ("to lament"); some of the exegetes said: he was named Noah only because of his much lamenting over himself.

mekki-muskil:31-31.t: His saying {تزدري أعينكُم}: the original of تزدري is تزتري; the dāl is a substitute for a tāʾ, because the dāl is a voiced letter, so it was paired with the zāy, since that is also voiced, whereas the tāʾ is voiceless and so differs from the zāy; the substitution was good because the two points of articulation are close. The implied form is تزدريهم أعينكم ("your eyes look down on them"); then the pronoun was omitted because of the length of the noun.

mekki-muskil:36-36.t: His saying {إِلَّا من قد آمن}: من is in the position of the nominative by يؤمن.

mekki-muskil:40-40.t: His saying {وَمن آمن}: من is in the position of the accusative by conjunction with اثنين or with أهلك. And من in His saying إلا من سبق is in the position of the accusative as excepted from الأهل.

mekki-muskil:41-41.t:
His saying {بِسم الله مجْراهَا وَمرْسَاهَا}: مجراها is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), مرساها is conjoined to it, and the khabar (predicate) is بسم الله; the implied form is "in the name of Allah is its sailing and its anchoring". It is permissible for both to be nominative by the prepositional phrase (ẓarf), because it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to what precedes it, namely اركبوا. It is also permissible for مجراها to be in the position of the accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), on the assumption of the omission of an adverb annexed to مجراها, in the manner of your saying آتيك مقدم الحاج ("I will come to you at the arrival of the pilgrims"), i.e. at the time of the arrival of the pilgrims; then the implied form is "in the name of Allah at the time of its sailing and its anchoring". It has been said that its implied form in the accusative is "in the name of Allah at the place of its sailing", and then the muḍāf was omitted. In the exegesis there is what indicates its accusative as an adverb: al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: at the time of its sailing he would say "In the name of Allah", and it would sail; and at the time of its anchoring "In the name of Allah", and it would anchor.
The bāʾ in بسم الله is attached to اركبوا. What governs مجراها, when it is an adverb, is the sense of the prepositional phrase in بسم الله; اركبوا does not govern it, because He did not mean "embark in it at the time of sailing and anchoring"; the meaning is only "say the name of Allah at the time of sailing and anchoring", and the implied form is "embark now, seeking blessing in the name of Allah at the time of sailing and anchoring".
If you make مجراها nominative as a mubtadaʾ with what precedes it as its khabar, the clause is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in فيها, because in the clause there is a referent (ʿāʾid) referring back to the hāʾ in فيها, namely the hāʾ in مجراها, since both are for the ship; and what governs the clause that is a ḥāl is the verbal sense contained in فيها. It is not good for this clause to be in the position of a ḥāl from the implied pronoun in اركبوا, because there is no referent in the clause referring back to the pronoun in اركبوا: the pronoun in بسم الله, if you make it the khabar of مجراها, refers only back to the mubtadaʾ, which is مجراها; and if you make مجراها nominative by the prepositional phrase, there is no pronoun in it; and the hāʾ in مجراها refers only back to the hāʾ in فيها.
If you make مجراها accusative as an adverb, بسم الله governs it, and the clause is in the position of a ḥāl from the implied pronoun in اركبوا, on the assumption of your saying خرج بثيابه ("he went out in his clothes") and ركب بسلاحه ("he rode with his weapons"); and from it is His saying وقد دخلوا بالكفر وهم قد خرجوا به: your sayings بثيابه, بسلاحه, بالكفر and به are all in the position of a ḥāl. So likewise بسم الله مجراها is in the position of a ḥāl from the implied pronoun in اركبوا when you make مجراها accusative as an adverb; its implied form is "embark in it, seeking blessing in the name of Allah at the time of sailing and anchoring". Then in بسم الله there is a pronoun referring back to the implied pronoun in اركبوا, which is the pronoun of those commanded, so the ḥāl from them is sound because of the pronoun that refers back to them. On this assumption it is not good for the clause to be in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun, which is the hāʾ in فيها, because there is no referent referring back to the owner of the ḥāl; and the pronoun in مجراها does not suffice, because it is not part of the ḥāl clause — it is only an idle (mulghā) adverb, and when it is idle the pronoun attached to it is not counted. مجراها would be part of the ḥāl clause only if you made it nominative as a mubtadaʾ. If you made the clause in the position of a ḥāl from the hāʾ in فيها while making مجراها accusative as an adverb, the implied form would become "embark in it [the ship] seeking blessing in the name of Allah at the time of sailing", and the meaning is not so: seeking blessing is not predicated of the ship; seeking blessing belongs only to those riding in it.
If you made مجراها and مرساها stand in the position of an active participle (ism fāʿil), it would be an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), and that would be permissible, and you would make it in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the name of Allah the Exalted. It was an adverb in the preceding discussion only on the basis that مجراها is not made to stand in the position of an active participle; but if you make مجراها in the sense of جارية and مرساها in the sense of راسية, its being an anticipated ḥāl is good.
By this question one can come to understand everything like it in speech and in the Qurʾān — that is for whoever understands it as it should be understood and reflects on it as it should be reflected on; for it is among the choicest of difficult questions.
As for fatḥa and ḍamma on the mīm in مجراها: whoever reads with fatḥa takes the speech on جرت مجرى ("it sailed a sailing"), and whoever reads with ḍamma takes it on أجراها الله مجرى ("Allah made it sail a sailing"). ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī read مجريها ومرسيها with yāʾ, making them both a naʿt (adjective) of Allah, exalted be His mention; it is also permissible for them to be in the position of the nominative by implying a mubtadaʾ, i.e. "He is its Sailer and its Anchorer".

mekki-muskil:42-42.t:
His saying {وَكَانَ فِي معزل}: whoever reads the zāy with kasra makes it a noun of place, and whoever reads it with fatḥa takes it as a maṣdar (verbal noun).
His saying {يَا بني اركب مَعنا}: the original of بني is with three yāʾs: the yāʾ of the diminutive; a yāʾ after it which is the third radical (lām al-fiʿl); and a yāʾ after the third radical which is the yāʾ of annexation (the first-person possessive). Therefore the third radical was given kasra, because the due of the yāʾ of annexation in the singular is that what precedes it always takes kasra. The yāʾ of the diminutive was assimilated into the third radical, because the due of the diminutive yāʾ is quiescence, and when two identical letters other than the letters of prolongation and softness come together and the first is quiescent, it must be assimilated into the second. The yāʾ of annexation was dropped because the kasra indicates it; dropping it in the vocative is most frequent in the speech of the Arabs, because it has taken the place of the nunation, and nunation in definite nouns does not remain in the vocative, so it became necessary to drop what is like the nunation and stands in its place, namely the yāʾ of annexation. Dropping it was strengthened in such a case by the meeting of burdensome identical letters together with the kasra, which is also heavy.
ʿĀṣim read it with fatḥa on the yāʾ. That is because he replaced the kasra of the third radical with a fatḥa, finding heavy the meeting of the yāʾs together with the kasra; so the yāʾ of annexation was changed into an alif, then the alif was dropped as the yāʾ is dropped, and the fatḥa remained as it was. Dropping the alif was strengthened because it is a compensation for what is dropped in the vocative, namely the yāʾ of annexation.
Ibn Kathīr read, in a place other than this, in Luqmān, with the yāʾ quiescent and lightened. That is because he dropped the yāʾ of annexation for the vocative, so a doubled yāʾ with kasra remained, and the kasra is like a yāʾ; this was found heavy, so he dropped the third radical, and the yāʾ of the diminutive remained quiescent.

mekki-muskil:43-43.t:
His saying {لَا عَاصِم الْيَوْم من أَمر الله}: what governs اليوم is من أمر الله, its implied form being "there is no protector from the command of Allah today". لا عاصم is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and من أمر الله is the khabar (predicate), with من attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted, its implied form being "there is no protector preventing from the command of Allah today". It is also permissible for من أمر الله to be an adjective of عاصم and to govern اليوم, with a khabar for عاصم implied. It is not permissible for من to be attached to عاصم, nor for اليوم to be made accusative by عاصم, because it would then be necessary to give عاصما nunation and not make it indeclinable on fatḥa, because whatever is attached to it and what it governs would become part of its completion, so it would become like your saying لا خيرا من زيد في الدار ("there is none better than Zayd in the house"). Its parallel is لا تثريب عليكم اليوم, which will come in its place, if Allah the Exalted wills.
His saying {إِلَّا من رحم}: من is in the position of the accusative as a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), with عاصم in its proper sense; its implied form is "no one prevents [anyone] from the command of Allah, but whoever Allah has mercy on is protected". It has been said that من is in the position of the nominative as a badal (substitute) from the position of عاصم; that is on two assumptions. One of them is that عاصم is in its proper sense, so the implied form is "none protects today from the command of Allah except Allah" — and it has been said: "except the Merciful One", and the Merciful One is Allah, exalted be His mention. The second assumption is that عاصم has the meaning of معصوم ("protected"), so the implied form is "none is protected from the command of Allah today except the one shown mercy".

mekki-muskil:46-46.t:
His saying {إِنَّه عمل غير صَالح}: the hāʾ refers back to the request, i.e. "your asking Me to save a disbeliever is an unrighteous deed". It has been said that its meaning is "your asking about what you have no knowledge of is an unrighteous deed". On these two assumptions the wording is a saying of Allah to Noah, upon him be peace. It has been said that it is a saying of Noah, upon him be peace, to his son: that is, he said to him "Embark with us and do not be with the disbelievers; your being with the disbelievers is an unrighteous deed", so this is a saying of Noah to his son connected to what precedes it. It has been said that the hāʾ in إنه refers back to the son of Noah, and in the speech there is the omission of a muḍāf (first term of a genitive construct), its implied form being "your son is one of unrighteous deeds". As for the hāʾ in the reading of al-Kisāʾī, it refers back to the son without disagreement, because he read عمِلَ with kasra on the mīm and fatḥa on the lām, and غيرَ in the accusative.
«[Translator's note: the text reads «مصلا», evidently for «متصلا» ("connected").]»

mekki-muskil:50-50.t:
His saying {من إِلَه غَيره}: غير may be nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of, or a badal (substitute) from, the wording of إله [i.e. its position]; it has been read with both [the nominative and the genitive]. The accusative as an exception is also permissible.
«[Translator's note: the text says «من لفظ إله», though the nominative is on the position of إله, its wording being genitive; «وقد قرئ بهما» refers to the nominative and genitive readings.]»

mekki-muskil:52-52.t: His saying {مدرارا}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from السماء. Its origin is with the hāʾ [i.e. the feminine ending], but the Arabs drop the hāʾ from مفعال by way of relation (nasab).

mekki-muskil:64-64.t: His saying {لكم آيَة}: آية is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الناقة.

mekki-muskil:66-66.t: His saying {وَمن خزي يَوْمئِذٍ}: whoever reads the mīm with fatḥa makes يوم indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, because of its annexation to an undeclinable word, namely إذ. Whoever reads the mīm with kasra declines it and puts it in the genitive, because الخزي is annexed to اليوم, and does not make it indeclinable.

mekki-muskil:67-67.t: His saying {وَأخذ الَّذين ظلمُوا الصَّيْحَة}: the tāʾ was dropped from أخذ only because the feminine noun, which is الصيحة, has been separated from its verb, which is أخذ, by His saying الذين ظلموا, which is the object of أخذ; so the separation stood in place of the feminine marker. At the end of the sūra, in the story of Shuʿayb, He said وأخذت, following the feminine according to the original and not counting the separation. It has been said that the tāʾ was dropped only because the femininity of الصيحة is not real, since it has no masculine from its own wording. And it has been said that the tāʾ was dropped only because it was taken according to the meaning of الصياح, since الصيحة and الصياح have the same meaning. Likewise is the reason in everything that resembles it.

mekki-muskil:69-69.t:
His saying {قَالُوا سَلاما}: سلاما is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun). It has been said that it is made accusative by قالوا, as you say قلت خيرا ("I said good"), because their speech is not quoted; السلام is only the meaning of what they said, so the verb "say" was made to govern it — just as you say قلت حقا ("I said: true") to someone you heard saying "There is no god but Allah": you did not mention what he said, you only brought a word that confirms his saying, so you made "say" govern it. Likewise سلام in the verse is only the meaning of what they said; it is not their very wording to be quoted. Had it been nominative, it would be quoted and would be their very words. So the accusative, always, in this and the like with the verb "say", is only the meaning of what they said, not their very words; and the nominative is on the basis that it is their very words, quoted from them.
His saying {قَالَ سَلام}: nominative as quotation of their speech; it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), or a mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "he said: it is peace", or "my affair is peace", or "upon you be peace". Making both accusative is permissible according to what has preceded, and making both nominative is permissible by quotation and implying.
His saying {فَمَا لبث أَن جَاءَ}: أن is in the position of the accusative on the assumption of the omission of the preposition, its implied form being "he did not delay in coming" (عن أن جاء). Al-Farrāʾ allowed it to be in the position of the nominative by لبث; its implied form according to him is "his coming did not delay", i.e. his coming with a calf was not slow. So on the first view لبث contains the pronoun of Abraham, and on the second view there is no pronoun in it. It has been said that ما has the meaning of الذي, and in the speech there is the omission of a muḍāf (first term of a genitive construct), its implied form being "and what Abraham tarried was the measure of his coming with a calf" — he wanted to show the extent of his delay; so لبث contains the agent pronoun, which is also Abraham.

mekki-muskil:71-71.t:
His saying {وَمن وَرَاء إِسْحَاق يَعْقُوب}: whoever reads يعقوب in the nominative makes it a mubtadaʾ (subject) with what precedes it as its khabar (predicate), and the clause is in the position of the accusative as an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara) from the implied accusative pronoun in بشرناها; then يعقوب is included in the good tidings. It is permissible to make يعقوب nominative by implying a verb, its implied form being "and after Isaac comes into being (يحدث) Jacob"; then يعقوب is not included in the good tidings.
Whoever reads يعقوب in the accusative makes it in the position of the genitive, by conjunction with إسحاق, but it is a diptote because of definiteness and foreignness; this is the view of al-Kisāʾī. It is weak according to Sībawayh and al-Akhfash unless the preposition is repeated, because you have separated the preposition [i.e. what stands for it] from its genitive noun by the prepositional phrase, and the due of the genitive noun is to be adjacent to the preposition, and the wāw has stood in place of the preposition. Do you not see that if you said مررت بزيد وفي الدار عمرو it would be ugly, and the right expression is مررت بزيد وعمرو في الدار, and بشرناها بإسحاق ويعقوب من ورائه? It has been said that يعقوب is accusative, construed on the position of بإسحاق; this too is far-fetched, because of the separation between the conjunction and the conjoined word by His saying ومن وراء إسحاق, as was the case with the genitive. On these two views يعقوب is included in the good tidings. It has been said that it is accusative by an implied verb indicated by the speech, its implied form being "and after Isaac We granted him Jacob"; then it is not included in the good tidings.
«[Translator's note: the text reads «ويحث», evidently for «ويحدث», and is translated accordingly.]»

mekki-muskil:72-72.t: His saying {وَهَذَا بعلي شَيخا}: شيخ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the one pointed to, and what governs the ḥāl is the pointing and the alerting [contained in the demonstrative]. This pointing is permissible only when the addressee knows the owner of the ḥāl, so that the benefit of the statement lies in the ḥāl. If he does not know the owner of the ḥāl, the benefit of the statement lies only in knowing the owner of the ḥāl, and a ḥāl may not occur for him, because the meaning would become that he is so-and-so in one state and not in another. If you said هذا زيد قائما ("this is Zayd, standing") to someone who does not know Zayd, it would not be permissible, because you would be telling him that the one pointed to is Zayd in the state of his standing, so that if he ceased standing he would not be Zayd. When the addressee knows Zayd himself, you have informed him only of the occurrence of the ḥāl from him; and when he does not know him himself, you have informed him only of who he is, so no ḥāl occurs from him, for the reason we mentioned. The nominative in شيخ is permissible in five ways, which we have left unmentioned because they are well known.

mekki-muskil:74-74.t: His saying {وجاءته الْبُشْرَى يجادلنا}: the view of al-Akhfash and al-Kisāʾī is that يجادلنا stands in the place of جادلنا, because the apodosis (jawāb) of لمّا must be a past verb, so the imperfect was put in its place — just as the due of the apodosis of a condition is to be imperfect, yet the past is put in its place. It has been said that the meaning is "he set about disputing with Us", so it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from Abraham, upon him be peace.

mekki-muskil:78-78.t:
His saying {هن أطهر لكم}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); nothing else is permissible according to the Basrans. It is related that ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read أطهرَ in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), making هن a separating pronoun (fāṣila); that is far-fetched and weak.
His saying {ضَيْفِي}: its origin is a maṣdar (verbal noun); therefore it is not put in the dual or the plural.

mekki-muskil:81-81.t:
His saying {إِلَّا امْرَأَتك}: Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Kathīr read it in the nominative, as a badal (substitute) from أحد. Abū ʿUbayd rejected the nominative as a badal and said: on this basis يلتفت would have to be nominative, making لا a negation; for if you substitute the woman for أحد and put يلتفت in the jussive as a prohibition, the meaning becomes that the woman was permitted to turn round, and that is not permissible; according to him the badal is not sound except with يلتفت in the nominative, and no one read it so. Al-Mubarrad said: the justification of this reading is that what is meant by the prohibition is the addressee, while its wording is directed to someone else — as you say to your servant لا يخرج فلان ("let so-and-so not go out"): the wording of the prohibition is for so-and-so, but its meaning is for the addressee, so its meaning is "do not let him go out". Likewise the meaning of the prohibition is only for Lot, i.e. "do not let them turn round, except your wife". Likewise your saying لا يقم أحد إلا زيد means "forbid them from standing, except Zayd".
As for the accusative in امرأتك, it is as an exception, because it is a prohibition and not a negation. It is also permissible for it to be excepted from His saying فأسر بأهلك — "except your wife"; on this view only the accusative is permissible for the woman, if you make her excepted from الأهل. The exception after the prohibition is good only because it is a complete statement, just as your saying جاءني القوم ("the people came to me") is a complete statement; then you say إلا زيد ("except Zayd"), making an exception and using the accusative.
«[Translator's note: the text writes «إلا زيد» without the accusative ending, though it speaks of the accusative.]»

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿الر﴾: the discussion of the disjointed letters (al-ḥurūf al-muqaṭṭaʿa) has preceded at the beginning of Sūrat al-Baqara.
﴿كتاب أحكمت آياته﴾: كتاب is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. «هذا كتاب» ("this is a Book"); the clause أحكمت آياته is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿كتاب﴾; and آياته is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
﴿ثم فصلت من لدن حكيم خبير﴾: ثم is a conjunction for sequence with delay; فصلت is a past verb built for that whose agent is not named (passive); من is a preposition, and لدن is an adverb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of a genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq) to ﴿فصلت﴾, or to an omitted adjective of كتاب; حكيم is the muḍāf ilayhi (second term of the genitive construct); and خبير is an adjective of حكيم.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿ألا تعبدوا إلا الله﴾: ﴿أن﴾: a maṣdar-forming particle that puts [the verb] in the accusative; ﴿لا﴾ is negative; ﴿تعبدوا﴾ is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن; and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from the maṣdar-forming ﴿أن﴾ and what falls in its scope is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) with an implied lām, i.e. «لئلا تعبدوا» ("so that you not worship"); and the clause ﴿لا تعبدوا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the maṣdar-forming ﴿أن﴾, with no grammatical position. Or ﴿أن﴾ is explicative (tafsīriyya), because "setting out in detail" (al-tafṣīl) carries the meaning of speech without its letters, as if it were said: He set out in detail and said: «لا تعبدوا إلا الله» ("worship none but Allah"); ﴿لا﴾ is then prohibitive, ﴿تعبدوا﴾ is a jussive (majzūm) imperfect verb, and the clause ﴿لا تعبدوا﴾ is explicative with no grammatical position. إلا: a particle of restriction (adāt ḥaṣr), and the Divine Name is the object of تعبدوا.
﴿إنني لكم منه نذير وبشير﴾: ﴿إن﴾ is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); the yāʾ is its noun (ism), and the nūn is for protection (nūn al-wiqāya); ﴿لكم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿نذير وبشير﴾; ﴿منه﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); نذير is the khabar of إنّ; and بشير is conjoined to نذير.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿وأن استغفروا ربكم ثم توبوا إليه﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿أن استغفروا﴾ is conjoined to ﴿ألا تعبدوا﴾; ربكم is the object of استغفروا; ﴿ثم﴾ is a conjunction; and توبوا is conjoined to ﴿استغفروا﴾. Or ﴿وأن استغفروا﴾ and what follows it is speech begun anew, cut off from what precedes it, on the tongue of the Prophet ﷺ, as an urging (ighrāʾ) from him to devote worship exclusively to Allah; this is indicated by His saying: ﴿إنني لكم منه نذير وبشير﴾.
﴿يمتعكم متاعا حسنا إلى أجل مسمى﴾: يمتعكم is a jussive imperfect verb, because it is the answer to the request (jawāb al-ṭalab), which is His saying ﴿وأن استغفروا ربكم﴾; the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿متاعًا﴾ stands as deputy for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it is a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar); حسنًا is an adjective; إلى أجل is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يمتعكم﴾; and مسمى is an adjective of ﴿أجل﴾.
﴿ويؤت كل ذي فضل فضله﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; يؤت is conjoined to يمتعكم and is jussive like it, the sign of its jussive being the deletion of the weak letter; the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he" (هو), i.e. Allah; ﴿كل﴾ is the first direct object; ذي فضل is the muḍāf ilayhi; and فضله is the second direct object.
﴿وإن تولوا فإني أخاف عليكم عذاب يوم كبير﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; إن is conditional; تولوا is a jussive imperfect verb because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the wāw is the agent; the fāʾ is linking (rābiṭa); إنّ is an abrogating particle, and the yāʾ is its noun; the clause أخاف عليكم is the khabar of إنّ; the clause ﴿فإني أخاف عليكم﴾ is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); عذاب is the direct object; يوم is the muḍāf ilayhi; and كبير is an adjective of ﴿يوم﴾.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t: ﴿إلى الله مرجعكم وهو على كل شيء قدير﴾: إلى الله is a fronted khabar, and مرجعكم is a postponed mubtadaʾ; ﴿هو﴾ is a mubtadaʾ; على كل شيء is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿قدير﴾; and قدير is the khabar of ﴿هو﴾.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿ألا إنهم يثنون صدورهم ليستخفوا منه﴾: ألا is a particle of opening (istiftāḥ) and drawing attention (tanbīh); إنّ is an abrogating particle, and the hāʾ is its noun; the clause يثنون صدورهم is its khabar; the lām is for causation (taʿlīl); يستخفوا is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām, and the interpreted maṣdar formed from the implied أن and the verb is genitive by the lām, the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to ﴿يثنون﴾.
﴿ألا حين يستغشون ثيابهم يعلم ما يسرون وما يعلنون﴾: ألا is an emphasis of the drawing of attention; حين is an adverb, and what governs it is implied, namely يستخفون; or it is an adverb of يعلم, i.e. does He not know their secret and their open [deeds] when they do such-and-such; the clause يستغشون is in the position of a genitive, the adverb being put in construct with it; ثيابهم is accusative by removal of the preposition (bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ); يعلم is an imperfect verb, and its agent is "he" (هو), Allah; ما is the direct object; the clause يسرون is the ṣila of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position; and ما يعلنون is conjoined to it.
﴿إنه عليم بذات الصدور﴾: إنّ is an abrogating particle, and the hāʾ is its noun; عليم is its khabar; and بذات الصدور is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿عليم﴾.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿وما من دابة في الأرض إلا على الله رزقها﴾: the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa) with no grammatical position; ما is negative; من is an extra (ṣila) particle; دابة is nominative (marfūʿ) in position and genitive by من in wording; إلا is a particle of restriction; على الله is a fronted khabar, and رزقها is a postponed mubtadaʾ; and the nominal clause is the khabar of دابة.
﴿ويعلم مستقرها ومستودعها﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; يعلم is an imperfect verb, and its agent is "he" (هو); مستقرها is the object of يعلم; and مستودعها is conjoined to مستقرها.
﴿كل في كتاب مبين﴾: كل is the mubtadaʾ; في كتاب is the khabar; and مبين is an adjective.

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿وهو الذي خلق السماوات والأرض في ستة أيام﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿هو﴾ is the mubtadaʾ, and الذي is the khabar; the clause خلق السماوات والأرض is the ṣila of الذي, with no grammatical position; and في ستة أيام is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to خلق.
﴿وكان عرشه على الماء﴾: كان is a defective (nāqiṣ), abrogating past verb; عرشه is its noun; and ﴿على الماء﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to its omitted khabar.
﴿ليبلوكم أيكم أحسن عملا﴾: the lām is for causation; يبلوكم is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām of causation, and the genitive-governing lām of causation together with what it governs is attached to خلق; أيكم is the mubtadaʾ, and أحسن is the khabar; عملًا is a tamyīz (specification); and the clause is in the position of an accusative as governed by يبلوكم, which has been suspended (ʿulliqa) from it by the interrogative أيّ.
﴿ولئن قلت إنكم مبعوثون من بعد الموت﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; the lām prepares for an oath (mūṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam); إن is a conditional particle that makes [the verb] jussive; ﴿قلت﴾ is a past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis; إنّ is an abrogating particle, and the kāf is its noun; مبعوثون is its khabar; and ﴿من بعد الموت﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿مبعوثون﴾.
﴿ليقولن الذين كفروا إن هذا إلا سحر مبين﴾: the lām is [that of] the answer to the oath, and the answer of the conditional [jazāʾ] is dispensed with by the answer to the oath; يقولن is an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa because it is attached to the nūn of emphasis, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath; إن is negative; هذا is the mubtadaʾ; إلا is a particle of restriction; سحر is the khabar; and مبين is an adjective.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿ولئن أخرنا عنهم العذاب إلى أمة معدودة﴾: ﴿ولئن﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and the lām prepares for an oath; عنهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أخرنا﴾; العذاب is the direct object; إلى أمة is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أخرنا﴾; and معدودة is an adjective of أمة.
﴿ليقولن ما يحبسه﴾: the lām is [that of] the answer to the oath; يقولن is a nominative imperfect verb, because it is separated from the nūn of emphasis by a separator, namely the wāw of the plural, which has been deleted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; ما is an interrogative noun, the mubtadaʾ; the clause يحبسه is the khabar; and the interrogation is for disapproval (inkār).
﴿ألا يوم يأتيهم ليس مصروفا عنهم﴾: ألا is a particle of interrogation and drawing attention [Translator's note: so in the source, «أداة استفهام وتنبيه»; elsewhere the author calls ألا a particle of opening (istiftāḥ) and drawing attention]; يوم يأتيهم is accusative as an adverb (ʿalā al-ẓarf), and it is governed by the khabar of ليس; its noun is latent, referring back to the punishment; مصروفًا is the khabar of ليس; and عنهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿مصروفًا﴾.
﴿وحاق بهم ما كانوا به يستهزئون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; the clause حاق is conjoined to the clause of ﴿ليس﴾, so it falls within the scope of ﴿ألا﴾; ﴿بهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿حاق﴾; ما is the agent of حاق; the clause كانوا is the ṣila of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position; the wāw is the noun of كان; به is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يستهزئون﴾; and the clause يستهزئون is the khabar of كان.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t:
﴿ولئن أذقنا الإنسان منا رحمة﴾: ﴿ولئن﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and the lām prepares for an oath; أذقنا is a past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis, and نا is the agent; الإنسان is the direct object; منا is a ḥāl; and رحمة is the second direct object.
﴿ثم نزعناها منه إنه ليئوس كفور﴾: ثم is a conjunction for sequence with delay; نزعنا[ها] is a verb, its agent and its direct object; منه is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿نزعناها﴾; إنّ is an abrogating particle, and the hāʾ is its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); يئوس is the khabar of إنّ; and كفور is a second khabar of ﴿إن﴾.

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿ولئن أذقناه نعماء بعد ضراء مسته﴾: ﴿ولئن﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and the lām prepares for an oath; أذقنا is a past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis, and نا is the agent; the pronoun is the first direct object; نعماء is the second direct object; بعد is an adverb attached to an omitted adjective of نعماء; ضراء is the muḍāf ilayhi; and the clause مسته is an adjective.
﴿ليقولن ذهب السيئات عني﴾: the lām is [that of] the answer to the oath, and the apodosis of the condition is omitted because the answer to the oath indicates it; يقولن is an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa; the clause ذهب السيئات is what is said (maqūl al-qawl); and ﴿عني﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿ذهب﴾.
﴿إنه لفرح فخور﴾: إنّ is an abrogating particle, and the hāʾ is its noun; the lām is the shifted lām; فرح is the first khabar, and فخور is a second khabar of ﴿إن﴾.

muyesser-irab:11-11.t:
﴿إلا الذين صبروا وعملوا الصالحات﴾: إلا is a particle of exception; الذين is excepted (mustathnā) from الإنسان, in the position of an accusative, because the lām in it is generic, so the exception is connected (muttaṣil); or the exception is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), and الذين is likewise excepted, in the position of an accusative; the clause صبروا is the ṣila of الذين, with no grammatical position; and عملوا الصالحات is conjoined.
﴿أولئك لهم مغفرة وأجر كبير﴾: أولئك is the mubtadaʾ; لهم is a fronted khabar, and مغفرة is a postponed mubtadaʾ; and the nominal clause is the khabar of أولئك.

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿فلعلك تارك بعض ما يوحى إليك وضائق به صدرك﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive; لعل is a particle of hope (tarajjī) that puts [its noun] in the accusative, and the kāf is its noun; تارك is its khabar; بعض is the direct object of تارك; ﴿ما﴾ is a relative noun, muḍāf ilayhi; the clause يوحى is the ṣila of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position; إليك is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿ضائق﴾ [Translator's note: so in the source; إليك presumably belongs with يوحى, while it is به that is attached to ضائق]; صدرك is the agent of ضائق; or ضائق is a fronted khabar and صدرك a postponed mubtadaʾ, the clause being a second khabar of ﴿لعلك﴾.
﴿أن يقولوا لولا أنزل عليه كنز أو جاء معه ملك﴾: أن together with what falls in its scope is a maṣdar in the position of an accusative as an object of purpose (mafʿūl min ajlihi), i.e. for fear of their saying; or it is a badal (substitute) for the hāʾ in His saying ﴿وضائق به صدرك﴾; لولا is for urging (taḥḍīḍiyya); أنزل is a past verb built for that whose agent is not named; عليه is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to it; كنز is the deputy agent; ﴿أو﴾ is a conjunction; جاء is a past verb; ﴿معه﴾ is an adverb attached to ﴿جاء﴾; ملك is the agent; and the clause ﴿فلعلك تارك بعض...﴾ is resumptive with no grammatical position.
﴿إنما أنت نذير والله على كل شيء وكيل﴾: إنما is [إنّ] restrained [from governing] by the restraining [ما] (kāffa wa-makfūfa); أنت is the mubtadaʾ, and نذير is its khabar; ﴿الله﴾ is a mubtadaʾ; ﴿على كل شيء﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿وكيل﴾; and وكيل is the khabar of ﴿الله﴾.

muyesser-irab:13-13.t:
﴿أم يقولون افتراه﴾: أم is a disconnected (munqaṭiʿa) conjunction, so it has the meaning of بل together with the interrogative hamza, the implied form being: «بل أيقولون افتراه» ("rather, do they say he invented it?"), the hamza being for disapproving interrogation (al-istifhām al-inkārī); or ﴿أم﴾ is connected (muttaṣila), and in that case a clause must be implied so that the balance [between the two alternatives] is correct, the implied form being: «أيقرون به أم يقولون: افتراه؟» ("do they acknowledge it, or do they say: he invented it?"); the clause افتراه is what is said; and ﴿يقولون﴾ is an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn.
﴿قل فأتوا بعشر سور مثله مفتريات﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition); ائتوا is an imperative verb and its agent; بعشر is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to it; سورة is the muḍāf ilayhi [Translator's note: so in the source, «وسورة»; the Quranic word is سور]; and مثله is an adjective.
﴿وادعوا من استطعتم من دون الله إن كنتم صادقين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ادعوا is conjoined to ﴿فائتوا﴾, and the wāw is the agent; مَن is the direct object; the clause استطعتم is the ṣila of ﴿مَن﴾, with no grammatical position; ﴿من دون الله﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl; إن is conditional; ﴿كنتم﴾ is a defective, abrogating past verb, and the tāʾ is its noun, and it is the protasis; صادقين is the khabar of كنتم; and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. then bring and call.

muyesser-irab:14-14.t:
﴿فإلم يستجيبوا لكم فاعلموا أنما أنزل بعلم الله﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; إن is conditional; لم is a particle of negation, conversion [to the past] and jussive; يستجيبوا is jussive by ﴿لم﴾, and it is the protasis; the wāw is the agent, and the pronoun refers back to ﴿من استطعتم﴾; لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يستجيبوا﴾; the fāʾ is linking; اعلموا is an imperative verb and its agent; أنما is [أنّ] restrained by the restraining [ما] (kāffa makfūfa), which together with what it governs stands in place of the two objects of اعلموا; أنزل is a past verb built for that whose agent is not named; and بعلم الله is a ḥāl, i.e. bound up with the knowledge of Allah, so the bāʾ is for accompaniment (mulābasa).
﴿وأن﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; أن is lightened from the heavy [أنّ] (mukhaffafa min al-thaqīla), and its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), omitted. ﴿لا﴾: the lā of generic negation.
﴿إله﴾: the noun of لا, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of an accusative.
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of restriction.
﴿هو﴾: a badal for the position of لا together with its noun, because its position is nominative as mubtadaʾ; or a badal for the pronoun latent in the omitted khabar. The clause ﴿لا إله إلا هو﴾ is in the position of a nominative as the khabar of أن.
﴿فهل أنتم مسلمون﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; هل is an interrogative particle; أنتم is the mubtadaʾ; and مسلمون is the khabar.

muyesser-irab:15-15.t: ﴿من كان يريد الحياة الدنيا وزينتها نوف إليهم أعمالهم فيها وهم فيها لا يبخسون﴾: من is a conditional noun that makes [the verb] jussive, in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ; the noun of كان is a latent pronoun referring back to مَن; the clause يريد الحياة الدنيا is the khabar of كان; كان is the protasis, jussive in position; زينتها is conjoined to الحياة; نوف is the apodosis, jussive by the deletion of the weak letter; إليهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿نوف﴾; أعمالهم is the direct object; فيها is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl; ﴿وهم﴾: the wāw is for the ḥāl (ḥāliyya), and هم is the mubtadaʾ; فيها is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يبخسون﴾; and the clause لا يبخسون is the khabar of هم.

muyesser-irab:16-16.t:
﴿أولئك الذين ليس لهم في الآخرة إلا النار﴾: the demonstrative is the mubtadaʾ, and الذين is its khabar; the clause of ﴿ليس﴾ is the ṣila of الذين, with no grammatical position; ﴿لهم﴾ is the fronted khabar of ﴿ليس﴾; في الآخرة is a ḥāl; إلا is a particle of restriction; and النار is the postponed noun of ﴿ليس﴾.
﴿وحبط ما صنعوا فيها وباطل ما كانوا يعملون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; حبط is a past verb, and ﴿ما﴾ is its agent; the clause صنعوا is the ṣila of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position; or ما is maṣdar-forming, and together with what it governs it is interpreted as a maṣdar that is the agent of حبط; فيها is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿صنعوا﴾ or to ﴿حبط﴾; ﴿وباطل﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and باطل is a fronted khabar; ما is a relative noun, the postponed mubtadaʾ; or ما is maṣdar-forming, and together with what it governs it is interpreted as a maṣdar that is the postponed mubtadaʾ; ﴿وكانوا﴾ is a defective, abrogating past verb, the wāw is its noun, and the clause يعملون is its khabar.

muyesser-irab:17-17.t:
﴿أفمن كان على بينة من ربه﴾: the hamza is for interrogation seeking affirmation (al-istifhām al-taqrīrī); the fāʾ is resumptive; من is a relative [noun], the mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is omitted, its implied form being: «كغيره» ("like someone else"), or: «كمن ليس كذلك» ("like one who is not so"); the answer to the interrogation is also omitted, its implied form being: «لا يستويان» ("the two are not equal"); كان is a defective past verb, and its noun is latent, referring back to ﴿مَن﴾; ﴿على بينة﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to its omitted khabar; ﴿من ربه﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted adjective of ﴿بينة﴾; and the clause ﴿أفمن كان...﴾ is resumptive with no grammatical position.
﴿ويتلوه شاهد منه﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; يتلوه شاهد is an imperfect verb, a direct object and an agent; and منه is an adjective of ﴿شاهد﴾.
﴿ومن قبله كتاب موسى إماما ورحمة﴾: the wāw is likewise a conjunction; ﴿من قبله﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl of ﴿كتاب موسى﴾, which is conjoined to ﴿شاهد﴾ as a conjoining of single words; or ﴿من قبله﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar, and كتاب موسى is a postponed mubtadaʾ; ﴿إمامًا﴾ is a ḥāl of ﴿كتاب موسى﴾; and رحمة is conjoined to ﴿إمامًا﴾.
﴿أولئك يؤمنون به﴾: أولئك is the mubtadaʾ, and the clause يؤمنون به is the khabar.
﴿ومن يكفر به من الأحزاب فالنار موعده﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; من is conditional, the mubtadaʾ; يكفر is the protasis; ﴿به﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يكفر﴾; ﴿من الأحزاب﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl; the fāʾ is linking; النار is the mubtadaʾ, and موعده is the khabar; and the nominal clause is the apodosis.
﴿فلا تك في مرية منه﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa; لا is prohibitive; ﴿تك﴾ is a jussive imperfect verb, the sign of its jussive being the sukūn implied on the nūn that has been deleted for lightening; the noun of ﴿تك﴾ is latent, its implied form being "you" (أنت); ﴿في مرية﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar; and ﴿منه﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted adjective of ﴿مرية﴾.
﴿إنه الحق من ربك ولكن أكثر الناس لا يؤمنون﴾: إنّ is an abrogating particle, and the hāʾ is its noun; الحق is its khabar; من ربك is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl; the wāw is for the ḥāl; لكنّ is an abrogating particle, and أكثر is its noun; الناس is the muḍāf ilayhi; and the clause لا يؤمنون is the khabar of لكنّ.

muyesser-irab:18-18.t:
﴿ومن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive with no grammatical position; مَن is interrogative, the mubtadaʾ [Translator's note: the source does not parse أظلم, which would be the khabar]; ممن is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أظلم﴾; the clause افترى is the ṣila of ﴿مَن﴾, with no grammatical position; على الله is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿افترى﴾; ﴿كذبا﴾ is the direct object of the verb افترى, i.e. he fabricated and contrived a lie; or an object of purpose, i.e. he fabricated for the sake of lying; or a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl, i.e. he fabricated while being a liar, and it is an emphatic ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida).
﴿أولئك يعرضون على ربهم﴾: أولئك is the mubtadaʾ; the clause يعرضون is its khabar, and the wāw is the deputy agent; and على ربهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يعرضون﴾.
﴿ويقول الأشهاد هؤلاء الذين كذبوا على ربهم ألا لعنة الله على الظالمين﴾: ﴿ويقول﴾ is conjoined to ﴿يعرضون﴾; الأشهاد is the agent; هؤلاء is the mubtadaʾ, and الذين is its khabar; the clause كذبوا على ربهم is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; ألا is a particle of drawing attention; لعنة الله is the mubtadaʾ; and على الظالمين is the khabar.

muyesser-irab:19-19.t:
﴿الذين يصدون عن سبيل الله ويبغونها عوجا﴾: الذين is a badal of الظالمين; the clause يصدون is the ṣila of الذين, with no grammatical position; عن سبيل الله is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يصدون﴾; يبغونها is conjoined to يصدون, and it is a verb, its agent and its object; and عوجًا is a ḥāl, i.e. crooked.
﴿وهم بالآخرة هم كافرون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿هم﴾ is the mubtadaʾ; بالآخرة is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿كافرون﴾; the second ﴿هم﴾ is an emphasis (taʾkīd) of the first ﴿هم﴾; and كافرون is the khabar of the first ﴿هم﴾.

muyesser-irab:20-20.t:
﴿أولئك لم يكونوا معجزين في الأرض﴾: أولئك is the mubtadaʾ; the clause لم يكونوا is the khabar; معجزين is the khabar of يكونوا; and في الأرض is a ḥāl.
﴿وما كان لهم من دون الله من أولياء﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ما is negative; كان is a defective past verb; لهم is the fronted khabar of كان; من دون الله is a ḥāl; من is an extra (ṣila) particle; and أولياء is the noun of كان in position.
﴿يضاعف لهم العذاب ما كانوا يستطيعون السمع وما كانوا يبصرون﴾: يضاعف is an imperfect verb built for that whose agent is not named; لهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to it; العذاب is the deputy agent; and the clause is resumptive with no grammatical position; ما is negative; كانوا: a defective, abrogating past verb, and the wāw is its noun; the clause يستطيعون السمع is the khabar of كان, and السمع is the direct object; and the clause وما كانوا يبصرون is conjoined to ما كانوا يستطيعون السمع.

muyesser-irab:21-21.t: ﴿أولئك الذين خسروا أنفسهم وضل عنهم ما كانوا يفترون﴾: أولئك is the mubtadaʾ, and الذين is the khabar; the clause خسروا أنفسهم is the ṣila of الذين, with no grammatical position; ضل عنهم is conjoined; ﴿ما﴾ is the agent of ﴿ضل﴾; and the clause ﴿كانوا يفترون﴾ is the ṣila of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:22-22.t: ﴿لا جرم أنهم في الآخرة هم الأخسرون﴾: لا is negative, and جرم is a past verb; ﴿أنهم﴾: أنّ together with what falls in its scope is in the position of a nominative as the agent of جرم; في الآخرة is a ḥāl; ﴿هم﴾ is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl), or a mubtadaʾ; and الأخسرون is the khabar of أنّ, or the khabar of ﴿هم﴾, the clause [then] being the khabar of أنّ.

muyesser-irab:23-23.t:
﴿إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات وأخبتوا إلى ربهم﴾: إنّ is an abrogating particle, and الذين is its noun; the clause آمنوا is the ṣila of الذين, with no grammatical position; the clause عملوا الصالحات is conjoined to آمنوا, and likewise the clause ﴿وأخبتوا إلى ربهم﴾.
﴿أولئك أصحاب الجنة هم فيها خالدون﴾: أولئك is the mubtadaʾ, and أصحاب الجنة is the khabar; هم is a mubtadaʾ; فيها is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿خالدون﴾; خالدون is the khabar of ﴿هم﴾; the clause أولئك أصحاب الجنة is the khabar of إنّ; and the clause هم فيها خالدون is a second khabar of ﴿إن﴾.

muyesser-irab:24-24.t:
﴿مثل الفريقين كالأعمى والأصم والبصير والسميع﴾: مثل is the mubtadaʾ, and الفريقين is the muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿كالأعمى﴾: the kāf is a noun meaning "like" (mithl), indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of a nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and الأعمى is the muḍāf ilayhi; الأصم is conjoined to الأعمى, a conjoining of an attribute to an attribute, the two being attributes of one person; ﴿والبصير والسميع﴾ is conjoined to ﴿الأعمى والأصم﴾, and البصير and السميع are two attributes of another person, i.e. like one who combines blindness and deafness and one who combines sight and hearing.
﴿هل يستويان مثلا أفلا تذكرون﴾: هل is an interrogative whose meaning is negation; يستويان is an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; مثلًا is a tamyīz converted from the agent, the original being: «هل يستوي مثلهم» ("is their likeness equal?"); ﴿أفلا تذكرون﴾: the interrogation is for disapproval and rebuke.

muyesser-irab:25-25.t: ﴿ولقد أرسلنا نوحا إلى قومه إني لكم نذير مبين﴾: a resumptive clause with no grammatical position; the lām occurs in the answer to an implied oath, and قد is a particle of verification (taḥqīq); أرسلنا is a verb and its agent; نوحًا is the direct object; إلى قومه is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أرسلنا﴾; ﴿إني﴾: إنّ is an abrogating particle, and the yāʾ is its noun; لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿نذير﴾; نذير is the khabar of إنّ; and مبين is its adjective.

muyesser-irab:26-26.t:
﴿أن لا تعبدوا إلا الله﴾: أن is explicative; لا is prohibitive; تعبدوا is an imperfect verb made jussive by ﴿لا﴾, and the wāw is the agent; إلا is a particle of restriction; and the Divine Name is the direct object. The clause ﴿لا تعبدوا...﴾ is explicative, with no grammatical position.
﴿إني أخاف عليكم عذاب يوم أليم﴾: إنّ is an abrogating particle, and the yāʾ is its noun; the clause أخاف is its khabar; عليكم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أخاف﴾; عذاب يوم is the object of أخاف; and أليم is an adjective of ﴿يوم﴾.

muyesser-irab:27-27.t:
﴿فقال الملأ الذين كفروا من قومه﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; قال الملأ is a verb and its agent; الذين is an adjective of الملأ; the clause كفروا is the ṣila of الذين, with no grammatical position; and من قومه is a ḥāl.
﴿ما نراك إلا بشرا مثلنا وما نراك اتبعك إلا الذين هم أراذلنا بادي الرأي﴾: the clause is what is said; ما is negative; نراك is an imperfect verb, a latent agent and a direct object; إلا is a particle of restriction; the seeing may be mental (qalbiyya) or visual (baṣariyya), so ﴿بشرًا﴾ is a second direct object on the first [view] and a ḥāl on the second; مثلنا is an adjective; the [second] ما نراك is conjoined to the first ما نراك, and it too may be mental or visual, so the clause اتبعك is either a second direct object or a ḥāl; إلا is a particle of restriction; الذين is the agent of اتبعك; هم أراذلنا is a mubtadaʾ and khabar, and the clause is the ṣila of الذين, with no grammatical position; and بادي الرأي is accusative as an adverb (ʿalā al-ẓarfiyya).
﴿وما نرى لكم علينا من فضل بل نظنكم كاذبين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ما نرى is conjoined to what precedes; لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿نرى﴾; علينا is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿فضل﴾; من is an extra (ṣila) particle; فضل is genitive in wording and a direct object, accusative in position; بل is a particle of digression (iḍrāb) and conjunction; نظنكم is conjoined to ﴿ما نرى﴾; the kāf is the first direct object; and كاذبين is the second direct object.

muyesser-irab:28-28.t:
﴿قال يا قوم أرأيتم إن كنت على بينة من ربي وآتاني رحمة من عنده﴾: the clause is resumptive with no grammatical position; يا قوم is a vocative (munādā) put in construct with the yāʾ of the first person, which has been deleted; ﴿وأرأيتم﴾: the hamza is for interrogation; رأى is a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn, and the tāʾ is the agent. Here the verb أرى requires the word البينة as a direct object, while ﴿كنت﴾ requires البينة in the genitive by ﴿على﴾; so the second was made to govern, and [a pronoun] was implied in the first, the implied form being: «أرأيتم البينة من ربي إن كنت عليها أنلزمكموها» ("have you considered the clear proof from my Lord, if I am upon it — shall we compel you to it?"); the first object was then omitted, and the interrogative clause is the second object; the apodosis is omitted because it is indicated. إن is conditional; كنت is the protasis, and the tāʾ is its noun; على بينة is the khabar of كنت; من ربي is an adjective; ﴿وآتاني﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and ﴿آتاني﴾ is a verb, a latent agent and a direct object; رحمة is the second direct object; and من عنده is an adjective of رحمة.
﴿فعميت عليكم أنلزمكموها وأنتم لها كارهون﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; عميت is a past verb built for that whose agent is not named, and the deputy agent is latent, its implied form being "she/it" (هي); عليكم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿عميت﴾; أنلزمكموها: the hamza is for interrogation, and the agent is latent, its implied form being "we" (نحن); the kāf is the first object, and ﴿ها﴾ is the second object; the mīm is the sign of the masculine plural, and the wāw is for prolonging the ḍamma on the mīm and is not a pronoun; ﴿وأنتم﴾: the wāw is for the ḥāl; أنتم is the mubtadaʾ; لها is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿كارهون﴾; كارهون is the khabar; and the clause is a ḥāl.

muyesser-irab:29-29.t:
﴿ويا قوم لا أسألكم عليه مالا﴾: conjoined to what precedes; لا is negative; أسألكم is a verb, a latent agent and a direct object; عليه is a ḥāl; and ﴿مالًا﴾ is the second direct object.
﴿إن أجري إلا على الله﴾: إن is negative; أجري is the mubtadaʾ, and the yāʾ of the first person is the muḍāf ilayhi; إلا is a particle of restriction; and على الله is the khabar.
﴿وما أنا بطارد الذين آمنوا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿ما﴾ is the Ḥijāzī negative [ما] which operates like ليس; ﴿أنا﴾ is the noun of ما; ﴿بطارد﴾: the bāʾ is an extra (ṣila) preposition, and ﴿طارد﴾ is the khabar of the Ḥijāzī ﴿ما﴾, accusative in position and genitive by the bāʾ in wording; ﴿الذين﴾ is the muḍāf ilayhi; and the clause ﴿آمنوا﴾ is the ṣila of الذين, with no grammatical position.
﴿إنهم ملاقو ربهم ولكني أراكم قوما تجهلون﴾: إنّ is an abrogating particle, and the hāʾ is its noun; ﴿ملاقو﴾ is its khabar, and ربهم is the muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿ولكني﴾: the wāw is for the ḥāl or a conjunction; لكنّ is an abrogating particle, and the yāʾ is its noun; the clause أراكم is its khabar; the kāf is the first object of أراكم; قومًا is the second direct object; and the clause تجهلون is an adjective.

muyesser-irab:30-30.t: ﴿ويا قوم من ينصرني من الله إن طردتهم أفلا تذكرون﴾: conjoined to what precedes it; من is an interrogative noun, the mubtadaʾ, and the clause ينصرني is the khabar; من الله is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿ينصرني﴾; إن is conditional; طردتهم is the protasis, and it is a past verb, an agent and a direct object; the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. then who would help me; ﴿أفلا تذكرون﴾: the hamza is for disapproving interrogation, and it either enters upon something implied, its implied form being: «أتأمروني بطردهم فلا تذكرون» ("do you order me to drive them away, and so do you not take heed?"), or it is brought forward from a later position, the original being: «فألا تذكرون», the hamza having been placed before the fāʾ because it has the right to the front of the clause (al-ṣadāra); and تذكرون is an imperfect verb.

muyesser-irab:92-92.t:
﴿قال يا قوم أرهطي أعز عليكم من الله﴾: the hamza is for disapproving, rebuking interrogation; رهطي is the mubtadaʾ (subject), and أعز is the khabar (predicate); ﴿عليكم﴾ and ﴿من الله﴾ are each a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أعز﴾.
﴿واتخذتموه وراءكم ظهريا﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) with قد implied, i.e. "while you have taken him behind you"; اتخذ takes two objects, the first of which is the hā' and the second ظهريًّا; ﴿وراءكم﴾ is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to ﴿اتخذتموه﴾, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) of ظهريًّا. Or اتخذ takes a single object, the hā' being its object and ظهريًّا a ḥāl. The wāw in اتخذتموه is for lengthening (ishbāʿ) the ḍamma of the mīm.
﴿إن ربي بما تعملون محيط﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (inna and its sisters), and ربي is its noun; ﴿بما﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿محيط﴾; the clause تعملون is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, a clause with no grammatical position; and محيط is the khabar of إن.

muyesser-irab:93-93.t:
﴿ويا قوم اعملوا على مكانتكم إني عامل﴾: اعملوا is an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent); على مكانتكم is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "while you are characterised by high standing and far-reaching power"; إن is an abrogating particle, the yā' is its noun, and عامل is its khabar (predicate).
﴿سوف تعلمون من يأتيه عذاب يخزيه ومن هو كاذب﴾: سوف is a particle of futurity; تعلمون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn; the clause is an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī), a clause with no grammatical position; من is a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿تعلمون﴾; the clause يأتيه is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿مَن﴾, with no grammatical position; the hā' is the object of يأتي, and عذاب is the fāʿil (agent) of يأتي; the clause يخزيه is an adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿عذاب﴾; and من is a relative noun conjoined to the first one; ﴿هو﴾ is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and كاذب the khabar (predicate); the clause ﴿هو كاذب﴾ is the ṣila of ﴿مَن﴾, with no grammatical position.
﴿وارتقبوا إني معكم رقيب﴾: ﴿وارتقبوا﴾ is conjoined according to the sense; ارتقبوا is an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent); إن is an abrogating particle, the yā' is its noun; معكم is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to ﴿رقيب﴾; and رقيب is the khabar of إن.

muyesser-irab:94-94.t:
﴿ولما جاء أمرنا نجينا شعيبا والذين آمنوا معه برحمة منا﴾: لما is temporal ("at the time when"), attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿نجينا﴾, or it is a linking particle (rābiṭa); جاء أمرنا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); نجينا شعيبا is a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); الذين is conjoined to ﴿شعيبا﴾; the clause آمنوا is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين, a clause with no grammatical position; معه is an adverb of place attached to ﴿آمنوا﴾; برحمة is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿نجينا﴾; and منا is an adjective (ṣifa) of رحمة.
﴿وأخذت الذين ظلموا الصيحة﴾: الذين is an object placed first, of ﴿أخذت﴾; the clause ظلموا is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; and الصيحة is the fāʿil (agent) of أخذت.
﴿فأصبحوا في ديارهم جاثمين﴾: أصبحوا is an incomplete (nāqiṣ), abrogating past verb (kāna and its sisters); the wāw is its noun, and جاثمين is its khabar (predicate); في ديارهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿جاثمين﴾.

muyesser-irab:95-95.t: ﴿كأن لم يغنوا فيها ألا بعدا لمدين كما بعدت ثمود﴾: كأن is lightened (mukhaffafa), its noun is omitted, and the clause ﴿لم يغنوا﴾ is its khabar (predicate); فيها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يغنوا﴾; ألا is a particle of alerting (tanbīh); ﴿بعدا﴾ is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, i.e. بعدوا بعدا, so it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) carrying the sense of an imprecation against them. ﴿لمدين﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿بعدا﴾. ﴿كما﴾: the kāf is a noun meaning "like" (mithl), indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative as an adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿بعدًا﴾, i.e. "a perishing for Madyan like the perishing of Thamūd"; ﴿ما﴾ is maṣdariyya; ﴿بعدت ثمود﴾ is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿بعدت﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the maṣdariyya ﴿ما﴾, a clause with no grammatical position; and the interpreted maṣdar formed from the maṣdariyya ﴿ما﴾ and the verb ﴿بعدت﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

muyesser-irab:96-96.t: ﴿ولقد أرسلنا موسى بآياتنا وسلطان مبين﴾: بآياتنا is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "while he was furnished with Our signs"; سلطان is conjoined to ﴿آياتنا﴾; and ﴿مبين﴾ is an adjective (ṣifa).

muyesser-irab:97-97.t:
﴿إلى فرعون وملئه فاتبعوا أمر فرعون﴾: إلى فرعون is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أرسلنا﴾; ملئه is conjoined to فرعون; فاتبعوا is conjoined to أرسلنا, the wāw being the fāʿil (agent); and أمر فرعون is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿وما أمر فرعون برشيد﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); ﴿ما﴾ is the Ḥijāzī negating mā, which operates like laysa; ﴿أمر﴾ is the noun of mā, and ﴿فرعون﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿برشيد﴾: the bā' is a redundant (ṣila) preposition, and ﴿رشيد﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of the Ḥijāzī ﴿ما﴾, accusative (manṣūb) in position and genitive (majrūr) in form because of the bā'.

muyesser-irab:98-98.t: ﴿يقدم قومه يوم القيامة فأوردهم النار وبئس الورد المورود﴾: the clause يقدم قومه is resumptive (mustaʾnafa), a clause with no grammatical position; the fā' is conjunctive; أوردهم النار is a verb with a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent); the hā' is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and النار the second; بئس is an inflexible (jāmid) past verb for expressing blame; الورد is the fāʿil of بئس, nominative, with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. "the place of watering"; ﴿المورود﴾ is the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bil-dhamm), and it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. هو, or it is a mubtadaʾ placed after, with the clause ﴿بئس﴾ as its khabar.

muyesser-irab:99-99.t:
﴿وأتبعوا في هذه لعنة ويوم القيامة بئس الرفد المرفود﴾: أتبعوا is a past verb in the passive form (built for that whose agent is not named), and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); ﴿في هذه﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أتبعوا﴾; يوم القيامة is conjoined to the position of ﴿في هذه﴾; بئس is an inflexible (jāmid) past verb for expressing blame; الرفد is the fāʿil (agent) of بئس, nominative, with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. "the place of the gift"; ﴿المرفود﴾ is the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bil-dhamm), and it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. هو, or a mubtadaʾ placed after, with the clause بئس as its khabar.
[Translator's note: the source text does not parse لعنة.]

muyesser-irab:100-100.t: ﴿ذلك من أنباء القرى نقصه عليك منها قائم وحصيد﴾: ذلك is the mubtadaʾ (subject); من أنباء القرى is its first khabar (predicate); the clause نقصه is its second khabar; عليك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿نقصه﴾; ﴿منها﴾ is a khabar placed first; قائم is the mubtadaʾ; حصيد is conjoined to قائم; and the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa), a clause with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:101-101.t:
﴿وما ظلمناهم ولكن ظلموا أنفسهم﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; ما is negating; ظلمناهم is a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); لكن is inoperative (muhmala), for rectification (istidrāk); and ظلموا أنفسهم is a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi.
﴿فما أغنت عنهم آلهتهم التي يدعون من دون الله من شيء﴾: the fā' is conjunctive; ما is negating; أغنت is a past verb; عنهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أغنت﴾; آلهتهم is the fāʿil (agent); التي is an adjective (ṣifa); the clause يدعون is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿التي﴾, a clause with no grammatical position; من دون الله is a ḥāl (circumstantial); من is a redundant (ṣila) particle; and شيء is genitive in form and accusative in position, as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿لما جاء أمر ربك وما زادوهم غير تتبيب﴾: لما is temporal ("at the time when"), attached to ﴿أغنت﴾, or it is a linking particle (rābiṭa); جاء أمر ربك is a verb and its fāʿil; ما زادوهم is conjoined to ما أغنت; زادوهم is a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; and غير تتبيب is a second mafʿūl bihi.

muyesser-irab:102-102.t:
