Abū Ḥayyān and others attached it to the verb «يعلم», because there is no need for an implied element, since there is no ambiguity in the meaning.]; (يستغشون ثيابهم) like «يثنون صدورهم»; (يعلم) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is "he"; (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative, mafʿūl bihi [Note: or it is a maṣdar-forming particle, and the interpreted maṣdar is mafʿūl bihi.], and the resumptive pronoun is omitted; (يسرّون) like «يثنون»; (الواو) conjunction; (ما يعلنون) like «ما يسرّون» and conjoined to it; (إنّه) like «إنّي» [Note: in verse 3 of this sūra.]; (عليم) khabar (predicate), nominative; (بذات) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «عليم»; (الصدور) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr).
The clause «إنّهم يثنون ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «يثنون ...» is in the position of the nominative as khabar of inna.
The clause «يستخفوا ...» has no grammatical position; ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle-relative (أن).
The clause «يستغشون ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «يعلم ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «يسرّون» has no grammatical position; ṣila of the relative (ما), whether nominal or particle.
The clause «يعلنون» has no grammatical position; ṣila of the second relative (ما).
The clause «إنّه عليم ...» has no grammatical position; causal (taʿlīliyya).

* Morphology:
(يثنون): it contains a vowel-weakening by quiescence (iʿlāl bi-l-taskīn) and a weakening by deletion (iʿlāl bi-l-ḥadhf); its original form is «يثنيون» with ḍamma on both yāʾs; the ḍamma on the second yāʾ was felt heavy, so it was made quiescent and its vowel was transferred to the nūn — weakening by quiescence — then the yāʾ was deleted because it met, while quiescent, the wāw of the plural — weakening by deletion; its pattern is يفعون.
(يستخفوا): it contains a weakening by quiescence and a weakening by deletion, following the course of «يثنون» ... its pattern is يستفعون [Translator's note: so in the source; the form in the verse is without nūn.].
(يستغشون): it contains a weakening by quiescence and a weakening by deletion, following the course of «يثنون»; its pattern is يستفعون.
(ثياب): plural of «ثوب», a primitive (jāmid) noun meaning clothing; its pattern is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn, and the pattern of «ثياب» is فعال, with kasra on the fāʾ.
Part Twelve
Remainder of Sūrat Hūd
From verse 6 to verse 123; Sūrat Yūsuf from verse 1 to verse 52

safi-cedvel:84-86.t:
* I'rab:
(وإلى مدين ... إله غيره) the i'rab of its parallel has passed [Note: In verse (50) of this sūra.. And see verse (85) of Sūrat al-Aʿrāf.]; (الواو) conjunction; (لا) the prohibitive lā, making jussive; (تنقصوا) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jazm being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (المكيال) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (الواو) conjunction; (الميزان) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to المكيال, accusative; (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb, and (الياء) a pronoun in the position of accusative, the noun of inna; (أراكم) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the rafʿ being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif, and the fāʿil is "I" (أنا).. and (كم) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (بخير) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second mafʿūl bihi — or a ḥāl (circumstantial); (الواو) conjunction; (إنّي أخاف) like إنّي أرى; (على) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (أخاف); (عذاب) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (يوم) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (محيط) a naʿt (adjective) of يوم, genitive.
The clause «(أرسلنا) إلى مدين ...» is conjoined to the clause (أرسلنا) mentioned in the context of the stories of the prophets mentioned earlier [Note: In verse (50) of this sūra.].
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: an explicative resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «يا قوم ...» is in the position of accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «اعبدوا ...» has no grammatical position: the response to the vocative.
The clause «ما لكم من إله ...» has no grammatical position: justificatory (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «لا تنقصوا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause اعبدوا.
The clause «إنّي أراكم ...» has no grammatical position: justificatory.
The clause «أراكم بخير ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of (the first) inna.
The clause «إنّي أخاف ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause إنّي أراكم.
The clause «أخاف عليكم ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of (the second) inna.
(الواو) conjunction; (يا قوم) its i'rab has passed [Note: In verse (50) of this sūra.]; (أوفوا) imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil; (المكيال) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الميزان) conjoined to المكيال by the wāw, accusative; (بالقسط) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl from the fāʿil of أوفوا; (الواو) conjunction; (لا تبخسوا الناس) like ولا تنقصوا المكيال; (أشياءهم) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative.. and (هم) is muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) conjunction; (لا تعثوا) like لا تنقصوا; (في الأرض) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تعثوا); (مفسدين) a ḥāl confirming the content of the clause, accusative, the sign of the naṣb being the yāʾ.
The clause «يا قوم ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the previous clause يا قوم.
The clause «أوفوا ...» has no grammatical position: the response to the vocative.
The clause «لا تبخسوا الناس ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause of the response to the vocative.
The clause «لا تعثوا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause of the response to the vocative.
(بقيّة) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative; (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (خير) khabar, nominative; (اللام) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to خير; (إن) a jussive conditional particle; (كنتم) defective past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).. and (تم) is a pronoun, the noun of kāna; (مؤمنين) khabar of kāna, accusative, the sign of the naṣb being the yāʾ; (الواو) conjunction; (ما أنا عليكم بحفيظ) like ما هي من الظالمين ببعيد [Note: In verse (83) of this sūra.].
The clause «بقيّة الله خير» has no grammatical position: a resumption within the scope of the speech.
The clause «إن كنتم مؤمنين» has no grammatical position: resumptive.. and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "if you are believers, then what remains from Allah is better for you"; so the good is conditional on faith.
The clause «ما أنا.. بحفيظ» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause إن كنتم مؤمنين.

* Morphology:
(المكيال): noun of instrument from the transitive triliteral كال, its pattern is مفعال with kasra on the mīm.
(بقيّة): it is written in the Muṣḥaf with the open tāʾ (بقيت), and nothing else in the Qur'an is written that way [Translator's note: this is the author's claim as written.].

* Rhetoric:
Repetition (takrār): in the words of Allah the Exalted «وَيا قَوْمِ أَوْفُوا الْمِكْيالَ وَالْمِيزانَ بِالْقِسْطِ».
Repetition occurs in this story in three ways, because He said "and do not diminish the measure and the scale" (ولا تنقصوا المكيال والميزان), and this is exactly the first, and there is nothing in it except the expression "and do not defraud people of their things" (تبخسوا الناس أشياءهم). Its benefit is that, since the people persisted in that ugly practice, forbidding them from it required exaggeration in emphasis, and repetition conveys intense concern with the matter. They were first forbidden the ugly thing they were doing, namely diminishing the measure and the scale; then the command to give full measure came, stated explicitly in its own word, so that it would be more stirring toward it and more inviting to desire for it.

safi-cedvel:87-87.t:
* I'rab:
«قالوا يا شعيب» is like قالوا يا صالح [Note: In verse (62) of this sūra.]; (الهمزة) for the sarcastic interrogative; (صلاتك) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ).. and (الكاف) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (تأمرك) imperfect verb, nominative.. and (الكاف) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil (agent) is "she/it" (هي); (أن) a maṣdar-forming particle of naṣb; (نترك) imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), and the fāʿil is "we" (نحن); (ما) relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative, mafʿūl bihi; (يعبد) like تأمر; (آباؤنا) fāʿil, nominative.. and (نا) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (أو) a conjunction; (أن نفعل) like أن نترك; (في أموالنا) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (نفعل).. and (نا) is like the last; (ما) like the first; (نشاء) like تأمر, and the fāʿil is "we".
The interpreted maṣdar (أن نترك) is in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl bihi, its governing word being تأمر [Note: Or in the position of genitive by an omitted preposition attached to (تأمر), i.e. تأمرك بأن نترك.].
The interpreted maṣdar (أن نفعل..) is in the position of accusative — or genitive — conjoined to the first interpreted maṣdar.
(إنّك) is like إنّي [Note: In verse (84) of this sūra.]; (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); (أنت) detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative, mubtadaʾ; (الحليم) khabar (predicate), nominative; (الرشيد) second khabar, nominative.
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يا شعيب ...» is in the position of accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «أصلاتك تأمرك ...» has no grammatical position: the response to the vocative.
The clause «تأمرك ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ صلاتك.
The clause «نترك» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the first particle-relative (أن).
The clause «يعبد آباؤنا» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «نفعل ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second particle-relative (أن).
The clause «نشاء» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second relative (ما).
The clause «إنك لأنت الحليم» has no grammatical position: a resumption within the scope of the speech.
The clause «أنت الحليم» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of (إنّك).

* Morphology:
(شعيب): a proper name, its pattern is فعيل in the form of the diminutive [Translator's note: the source has التصفير, evidently a misprint for التصغير "diminutive".], which is among the patterns most proper to names, and therefore it is declined as a triptote.

* Benefits:
- A sound opinion on the i'rab of (أن نفعل):
Allah the Exalted said in this verse أَصَلاتُكَ تَأْمُرُكَ أَنْ نَتْرُكَ ما يَعْبُدُ آباؤُنا أَوْ أَنْ نَفْعَلَ فِي أَمْوالِنا ما نَشؤُا. What first comes to mind is conjoining (أَنْ نَفْعَلَ) to (أَنْ نَتْرُكَ), and that is false, because he did not command them to do with their wealth as they please; rather it is conjoined to ما, so it is governed by "leaving", and the meaning is "that we leave doing ...". Yes, whoever reads تفعل and تشاء with tāʾ, not nūn, then the conjunction is to أن نترك. What gives rise to the mentioned misconception is that the parser sees أن with the verb twice, with a conjunction between them.
Abu al-Baqāʾ al-ʿUkbarī confirmed this same i'rab, saying: (أَوْ أَنْ نَفْعَلَ) is in the position of accusative, conjoined to ما يعبد, and the implied sense is "Does your prayer command you that we leave what our fathers worship, or that we leave doing ...", and it is not conjoined to أن نترك, since the meaning is not "Does your prayer command you that we do with our wealth".

safi-cedvel:44-44.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (قيل) past verb, passive (أرض) the one addressed, an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of accusative (يا) vocative particle [Translator's note: the source lists (يا) after (أرض); the order is kept.] (ابلعي) imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn.. and (الياء) an attached pronoun in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent) (ماءك) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb).. and (الكاف) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) (الواو) conjunction (يا سماء أقلعي) like يا أرض ابلعي (الواو) conjunction (غيض) like قيل, (الماء) nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative (marfūʿ) (الواو) conjunction (قضي الأمر) like غيض الماء (الواو) conjunction (استوت) past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif that was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescents.. and the tāʾ is for the feminine, and the fāʿil is "it", i.e. the Ark (على الجوديّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (استوت), (الواو) conjunction (قيل) like the first (بعدا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, i.e. ابعدوا or بعدوا, by way of imprecation (للقوم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the maṣdar (بعدا) [Note: Abū Ḥayyān said: The lām in (للقوم) belongs to the complement of the maṣdar; a group disallowed attaching it to the maṣdar and said it is attached to His saying (قيل), the implied meaning being: and it was said for the sake of the wrongdoers, since one who has perished cannot be addressed except figuratively. Someone else said: it is for specification and clarification, attached to (قيل).. And it was said: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to a khabar (predicate) whose mubtadaʾ (subject) is omitted, its implied form being "the imprecation", i.e. the imprecation is against the wrongdoing people.. so there are two clauses in the construction..
(2, 3) Because it is originally the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).. The majority make the nāʾib fāʿil omitted, its implied form being (القول), and the clause explicative.], (الظالمين) naʿt (adjective) of القوم, genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
The clause «قيل ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «يا أرض ...» is in the position of nominative as nāʾib fāʿil «2».
The clause «ابلعي ...» has no grammatical position; the reply to the vocative.
The clause «يا سماء ...» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause يا أرض.
The clause «أقلعي ...» has no grammatical position; the reply to the second vocative.
The clause «غيض الماء ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «قضي الأمر ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «استوت على الجوديّ» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «قيل (the second) ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «(بعد) بعدا..» is in the position of nominative as nāʾib fāʿil «3».

* Morphology:
(غيض): in it the alif reverts to yāʾ and the first radical (fāʾ) of the word takes kasra
to suit the yāʾ.
(استوت): in it there is a weak-letter change (iʿlāl) by dropping because of the meeting of two quiescents: the alif came quiescent before the tāʾ of the feminine and was dropped; its pattern is افتعت.
(الجوديّ): a non-derived (jāmid) noun for a specific mountain; and it is said: every mountain is called a jūdī.
(بعدا): an aurally-transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar of the verb بعد يبعد, of the كرم class, its pattern being فُعْل with ḍamma then sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
1- This noble āya is examined from four angles: from the angle of the science of bayān and from the angle of the science of maʿānī – these two being the foundations of rhetoric – and from the angle of eloquence of meaning and the angle of eloquence of wording. As for examining it from the angle of the science of bayān, which is examining the majāz (figurative usage), the istiʿāra (metaphor) and the kināya (metonymy) in it, and what is connected with that of the qarīna (contextual indicator), the tarshīḥ (reinforcement of the metaphor) and the taʿrīḍ (allusion): when He, mighty is His dominion, wanted to build the meaning: "We wanted to return what had burst forth from the earth to its belly, so it returned; and to cut off the deluge of the sky, so it was cut off; and to make the water that came down from the sky abate, so it abated; and to accomplish the affair of Nūḥ, peace be upon him – which is fulfilling what We had promised him of drowning his people – so it was accomplished; and to settle the Ark on al-Jūdī, so it settled; and We left the wrongdoers drowned," He, glory be to Him, built the speech on likening the thing intended with this to one commanded, from whom disobedience is impossible – because of the perfect awe in which he holds the commander – and on likening the bringing into being of what is intended to a decisive command, effective in bringing about what is sought, as a depiction of His immense power, glory be to Him, and that these immense bodies of the heavens and the earth follow His will, the Exalted, in bringing into existence and annihilating, and follow His wish concerning them in alteration and change, as if they were rational, discerning beings. Then upon the combination of the two similes He built the composition of the speech, and He, majestic and exalted, said: «قيل ...» as a majāz for will, of the type of mentioning the effect and intending the cause, because will is a cause of the occurrence of speech in general; and He made the qarīna of this majāz the addressing of inanimate things, namely «يا أرض ...» «ويا سماء ...»; and this address to the earth and the sky is by way of istiʿāra, because of the mentioned resemblance. What appears is that he [Translator's note: the author being drawn upon, unnamed here] meant there is an istiʿāra bi-l-kināya (implicit metaphor) here, since the thing likened is mentioned (I mean the sky and the earth, from which the occurrence of a matter is intended) and what it is likened to is intended (I mean the one commanded who is described as being incapable of disobedience, by way of claim), with the qarīna being the attribution of the address to it and the entry of the vocative particle upon it – both of these being properties of the obedient one commanded – and this would be a takhyīl (imaginative attribution). Then for the sinking of water into the earth He borrowed "swallowing", which is the action of drawing food in, because of the resemblance between them, namely going to a hidden resting place.
In al-Kashshāf: "swallowing" is made a metaphor for the earth's soaking up of the water, and this is better, because soaking up indicates a drawing by the parts of the earth of what is on it, like swallowing in relation to an animal, and because soaking up is the action of the earth while sinking is the action of the water, together with the correspondence (ṭibāq) between the two verbs in transitivity. Then He borrowed "water" for food by way of istiʿāra bi-l-kināya, likening it to food, because the earth gains strength through water in growing crops and trees as the eater gains strength through food; and He made the qarīna of the metaphor the word «ابلعي ...», because it is coined for use with food and not with water.
Then He, majestic and exalted, said: «ماءك ...», annexing the water to the earth, by way of majāz, likening the connection of the water with the earth to the connection of property with the owner; and He chose the pronoun of address for the sake of tarshīḥ. Its upshot is that there is a linguistic majāz in the annexation form that indicates possessive specification, and for this reason the address was made a tarshīḥ for this metaphor, in that the address indicates the earth's fitness for ownership.
Then for the withholding of the rain He chose "desisting" (iqlāʿ), which is an agent's leaving off an action, because of the resemblance between them in the cessation of what there was of rain or action; so in «أقلعي ...» there is an istiʿāra with respect to its substance, and likewise with respect to its form as well. It is built on likening the bringing into being of what is intended to a decisive, effective command, and the address in it is also a tarshīḥ of the metaphor of the vocative.
Then He, glory be to Him, said «وَغِيضَ الْماءُ وَقُضِيَ الْأَمْرُ وَاسْتَوَتْ عَلَى الْجُودِيِّ وَقِيلَ بُعْداً ...»
So He, majestic and exalted, did not state explicitly who made the water abate, nor who accomplished the affair, settled the Ark and said "away with". Likewise He, glory be to Him, did not state explicitly the one who said «يا أَرْضُ ...» «وَيا سَماءُ ...» at the beginning of the āya, following in each of these the path of kināya, because those immense matters issue only from One possessed of power whose essence cannot be fathomed, an Overpowering One who cannot be overcome; so there is no room for the imagination to go to someone other than Him, majestic is His greatness, being the one saying «يا أَرْضُ ...» and «يا سَماءُ ...», nor the one making abate what abated, nor the one accomplishing such a dreadful affair, nor that the settling and fixing of the Ark could be by the settling of anyone else.
Then He, the Exalted, sealed the speech with taʿrīḍ, as a warning to those who tread the path of those people in denying the messengers, peace be upon them, wronging only themselves and nothing else; and as a display of the place of displeasure and of the respect in which they deserved it, and that the rising of the deluge and that dreadful scene were only because of their wrongdoing, as the imprecation of destruction after their destruction announces, and the description with wrongdoing together with the ruling being tied to it.
As for examining it from the angle of the science of maʿānī, which is examining the benefit of each word in it and the reason for each fronting and postponing among its clauses: «يا ...» was chosen rather than the rest of its sisters because it is more frequent in use, and because it indicates the distance of the one addressed, which the situation of displaying greatness and showing the dignity of might and omnipotence calls for. As for looking at the order of the clauses: the vocative was put before the command, so it was said: «يا أَرْضُ ابْلَعِي ...» «وَيا سَماءُ أَقْلِعِي ...»
rather than saying: "Swallow, O earth, and desist, O sky", following what is required – in the case of one who is truly commanded – of putting the alerting first, so that the command coming after it may settle firmly in the soul of the one addressed, intending thereby the meaning of tarshīḥ for the implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya) in the earth and the sky. Then He put the command to the earth before the command to the sky, because it is the origin, given that the deluge began from it, as its oven gushed forth first.
All this is examining the āya from the two sides of rhetoric. Ibn Abī al-Iṣbaʿ mentioned that it contains twenty kinds of badīʿ (embellishment), although it is seventeen words, namely: complete correspondence (munāsaba tāmma) in «ابلعي ...» and «اقلعي ...»; the istiʿāra in them; the ṭibāq (antithesis) between the earth and the sky; the majāz in «يا سَماءُ ...», for the literal is "O rain of the sky"; ishāra (allusion) in «وَغِيضَ الْماءُ ...», for many meanings are expressed by it, because the water does not abate until the rain of the sky desists and the earth swallows what comes out of it, so what is on the face of the earth decreases; irdāf (expressing by a consequent) in «وَاسْتَوَتْ ...»; tamthīl (representation) in «وَقُضِيَ الْأَمْرُ ...»; taʿlīl (causation), for the abating of the water is the cause of the settling; ṣiḥḥat al-taqsīm (sound division), for it covers the divisions of the water in the state of its decrease; iḥtirās (precaution) in the imprecation, lest it be imagined that the drowning, because of its generality, included those who did not deserve destruction, for His justice, the Exalted, prevents Him from invoking against one who does not deserve it; ḥusn al-nasaq (fine sequence); iʾtilāf al-lafẓ maʿa al-maʿnā (harmony of wording with meaning); ījāz (concision), for He, glory be to Him, told the story comprehensively in the briefest expression; tashīm (foreshadowing), because the beginning of the āya indicates its end; tahdhīb (refinement), because its individual words are described with attributes of beauty; ḥusn al-bayān (clarity of exposition), in that the listener does not hesitate in understanding the meaning of the speech and nothing of it is obscure to him; tamkīn (settledness), because the fāṣila (verse-ending) is settled in its place, at rest in its position; and insijām (flow). Al-Jalāl al-Suyūṭī added iʿtirāḍ (parenthesis).
[Translator's note: the list as given in the source names fewer than twenty kinds; it is translated as written.]

* Benefits:
1- Rhetorical inimitability in the Qur'an:
This āya comprises arts of rhetoric exceeding twenty-five arts, which the scholars of rhetoric have mentioned in detail and there is no room to set them out; one can only fall prostrate before the greatness of Allah, mighty and majestic, and bow before His inimitable expression, acknowledging that falsehood cannot come to it from before it or from behind it, a revelation from One Wise, Praiseworthy. It is related that a great scholar tried to criticize the Noble Qur'an by discovering a simple flaw in it, and the attempt went on for months; he had a group who kept coming to him and asking him what he had done. But in the end he broke the pen and the inkwell and said: This is the speech of Allah; it is not to be disputed. Then he passed by a mosque and heard a boy reciting this āya, and he said: It is not for a human being to say speech like this.
2- Imām al-Nasafī's comment on this āya:
And from the angle of eloquence of meaning: it is, as you see, a subtle arrangement of the meanings, and a conveying of them summarized and made clear; no complexity besets the mind in seeking what is intended, and no twisting makes the road to the seeker doubtful. And from the angle of eloquence of wording: its words, as you see, are Arabic and in use, free from dissonance, far from ugliness, sweet on the tongue-tips, smooth on the tongue-edges; each of them is like water in smoothness, like honey in sweetness, and like the breeze in gentleness. Hence the obstinate opponents agreed that human capacity falls short of producing the like of this āya. How excellent is the status of the Revelation! A scholar does not contemplate one of its āyas without perceiving subtleties beyond counting; and do not think the āya is restricted to what has been mentioned, for perhaps what has been left out is more than what has been written.

safi-cedvel:45-45.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (نادى نوح ربّه) like نادى نوح ابنه [Note: In āya (42) of this sūra.], (الفاء) conjunction (قال) past verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is "he" (ربّ) the one addressed, a muḍāf, accusative (manṣūb); the vocative particle has been dropped from it, and the sign of the accusative is the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on what precedes the yāʾ dropped for lightness.. and (الياء), dropped, is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb (ابني) the noun of inna, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied on what precedes the yāʾ.. and (الياء) muḍāf ilayhi (من أهل) a preposition and its genitive noun, [attached to] the khabar (predicate) of inna [Translator's note: the source reads "جارّ ومجرور بخبر إنّ", apparently missing the word متعلّق], and (الياء) muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) conjunction (إنّ وعدك) like إنّ ابني, the fatḥa being overt (الحقّ) the khabar of inna, nominative (marfūʿ) (الواو) conjunction (أنت) detached pronoun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) (أحكم) khabar, nominative (الحاكمين) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
The clause «نادى نوح ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause نادى, and it is an explicative or detailing conjunction.
The clause «ربّ ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl) [Note: Or it is parenthetical with no grammatical position, and the clause after it is the object of the saying.].
The clause «إنّ ابني من أهلي» has no grammatical position; the reply to the vocative.
The clause «إنّ وعدك الحقّ» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause that is the reply to the vocative.
The clause «أنت أحكم الحاكمين» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause that is the reply to the vocative.

* Benefits:
Was Canaan (Kanʿān), the drowned one, the son of Nūḥ? Most exegetes hold that he was Nūḥ's son from his own loins.
This is the correct view, and whatever is other than it is false. The majority have transmitted what is authentic from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he said: The wife of a prophet never committed fornication (mā baghat, i.e. mā zanat). And He, the Exalted, stated explicitly in His saying وَنادى نُوحٌ ابْنَهُ, just as his father called him in his saying (يا بني اركب معنا). The exegetes said: If the wife of a prophet disbelieves, this does not disgrace him or touch his honour; but fornication is a disgrace and may never occur from the wife of a prophet, as has come from Ibn ʿAbbās. What appears to me – and Allah knows best – is that His saying, the Exalted: "Indeed he is not of your family" means that by his choosing disbelief the moral kinship between him and his father was cut off, because faith is the fundamental bond and the true kinship.

safi-cedvel:6-11.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (ما) negating; (من) a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; (دابّة) genitive (majrūr) in form, nominative (marfūʿ) in position, mubtadaʾ (subject); (في الأرض) a preposition and its genitive noun, a naʿt (adjective) of «دابّة»; (إلّا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (على الله) a preposition and its genitive noun, a fronted khabar (predicate); (رزق) a postponed mubtadaʾ, nominative, and (ها) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), in the position of the genitive; (الواو) conjunction; (يعلم) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو"; (مستقرّ) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and (ها) like the first; (الواو) conjunction; (مستودعها) like «مستقرّها» and conjoined to it; (كلّ) mubtadaʾ, nominative [Note: What permitted beginning with an indefinite noun is that it denotes generality, and that it is on the assumption of an implied muḍāf, i.e.: every thing in life.. or everything mentioned at the beginning of the verse.]; (في كتاب) a preposition and its genitive noun, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ; (مبين) a naʿt of «كتاب», genitive.
The clause «ما من دابّة ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «على الله رزقها» is in the position of the nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ «دابّة».
The clause «يعلم ...» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the preceding khabar clause.
The clause «كلّ في كتاب ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive and causal (taʿlīliyya).
(الواو) conjunction; (هو) a detached pronoun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ; (الذي) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ; (خلق) a past verb, and the fāʿil is "he", and it is the resumptive pronoun; (السموات) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, its sign of the accusative being the kasra; (الأرض) conjoined to «السموات» by the wāw, accusative; (في ستة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (خلق); (أيّام) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (الواو) parenthetical; (كان) a defective past verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) —; (عرش) the noun of kāna, nominative, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi, in the position of the genitive; (على الماء) a preposition and its genitive noun, the khabar of kāna; (اللام) for causation (taʿlīl); (يبلو) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied «أن» after the lām, and (كم) a pronoun in the position of the accusative, mafʿūl bihi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يبلوكم..) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to (خلق); (أيّ) an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ, nominative, and (كم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, muḍāf ilayhi; (أحسن) khabar, nominative; (عملا) tamyīz (specification), accusative; (الواو) resumptive; (اللام) paving the way for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam); (إن) a conditional particle that makes the verb jussive (majzūm); (قلت) a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb — an abrogator — and (كم) a pronoun in the position of the accusative, the noun of inna; (مبعوثون) the khabar of inna, nominative, its sign of the nominative being the wāw; (من بعد) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (مبعوثون); (الموت) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (اللام) the lām of the oath; (يقولنّ) an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the nominative.. and (النون) is the nūn of emphasis; (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative, fāʿil; (كفروا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma.. and the wāw is fāʿil; (إن) a negating particle; (ها) a particle of alerting (tanbīh); (ذا) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ; (إلّا) a particle of restriction; (سحر) khabar, nominative; (مبين) a naʿt of «سحر», nominative.
The clause «هو الذي ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the resumptive clause «ما من دابة..».
The clause «خلق ...» has no grammatical position; ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun «الذي».
The clause «كان عرشه على الماء» has no grammatical position; parenthetical.
The clause «يبلوكم ...» has no grammatical position; ṣila of the implied particle-relative (أن).
The clause «أيّكم أحسن ...» is in the position of the accusative as the second mafʿūl bihi of the verb of testing, which is suspended (muʿallaq) from operating by the interrogative [Note: This is according to the view of al-Zamakhsharī, and Abū Ḥayyān followed him, because testing contains the sense of knowing; but Ibn Hishām rejected this analysis, so the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.].
The clause «قلت ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «إنّكم مبعوثون ...» is in the position of the accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «يقولنّ الذين كفروا» has no grammatical position; the response to the implied oath..
And the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by the response to the oath.
The clause «كفروا» has no grammatical position; ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «إن هذا إلّا سحر» is in the position of the accusative as the second object of saying.
(الواو) conjunction; (لئن أخّرنا) like «لئن قلت»; (عن) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (أخّرنا); (العذاب) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (إلى أمّة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أخّرنا); (معدودة) a naʿt of «أمّة», genitive; (اللام) the lām of the oath; (يقولنّ) an imperfect verb, nominative, its sign of the nominative being the retention of the nūn, which has been deleted because of the succession of like letters, and the wāw, deleted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is a pronoun in the position of the nominative, fāʿil, and (النون) is the nūn of emphasis; (ما) an interrogative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ; (يحبس) an imperfect verb, nominative, and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is "he". (ألا) a particle of alerting; (يوم) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (مصروفا); (يأتي) an imperfect verb, nominative, its sign of the nominative being an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the yāʾ, and the fāʿil is "it", i.e., the punishment, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (ليس) a defective, inflexible (jāmid) past verb — an abrogator — and its noun is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "هو"; (مصروفا) the khabar of laysa, accusative; (عنهم) like the first, attached to (مصروفا); (الواو) conjunction; (حاق) a past verb; (بهم) like «عنهم», attached to (حاق); (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative, fāʿil; (كانوا) a defective past verb — an abrogator — indeclinable on the ḍamma.. and the wāw is an attached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative, the noun of kāna; (به) like «عنهم», attached to (يستهزئون), which is an imperfect verb, its sign of the nominative being the retention of the nūn.. and the wāw is fāʿil.
The clause «إن أخرنا ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause «إن قلت».
The clause «يقولنّ ...» has no grammatical position; the response to the oath.. and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by the response to the oath.
The clause «ما يحبسه» is in the position of the accusative as the object of saying.
The clause «يحبسه» is in the position of the nominative as khabar of «ما».
The clause «يأتيهم» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «ليس مصروفا ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «حاق بهم ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause «ليس مصروفا».
The clause «كانوا ...» has no grammatical position; ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «يستهزئون» is in the position of the accusative as khabar of «كانوا».
(الواو) conjunction; (لئن أذقنا) like «لئن قلت»; (الإنسان) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (من) a preposition and (نا) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to an [omitted] ḥāl (circumstantial) of «رحمة» — a naʿt placed before the noun it qualifies —; (رحمة) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (ثمّ) a conjunction; (نزعنا) a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn.. and (نا) a pronoun, fāʿil, and the verb is in the position of the jussive, conjoined to (أذقنا), and (ها) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (منه) like «منّا», attached to (نزعنا); (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the accusative, the noun of inna; (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), conveying emphasis [Note: This lām is obligatory here because the clause is the response to the oath, so the lām has the status of the lām of the oath.]. (يئوس) the khabar of inna, nominative [Translator's note: the source repeats «مرفوع».]; (كفور) a second khabar, nominative.
The clause «إن أذقنا ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause «إن قلت»..
The clause «نزعناها ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause «إن أذقنا».
The clause «إنّه ليؤوس ...» has no grammatical position; the response to the implied oath..
And the apodosis is omitted, indicated by the response to the oath.
(الواو) conjunction; (لئن أذقنا) like «لئن قلت», and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (نعماء) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and it is prevented from taking tanwīn because it ends in the extended alif of the feminine; (بعد) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (أذقناه); (ضرّاء) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, its sign of the genitive being the fatḥa, for it is like «نعماء»; (مسّ) a past verb, and (التاء) is the tāʾ of the feminine, and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "هي"; (ليقولنّ) like the first, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "هو"; (ذهب) like «خلق»; (السيّئات) fāʿil, nominative; (عنّي) like «عنهم», and in it is the nūn of protection (wiqāya) before the yāʾ of the speaker, attached to (ذهب); (إنّه لفرح فخور) like «إنّه ليؤوس كفور».
The clause «إن أذقناه ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause «إن قلت».
The clause «مسّته ...» is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt of «ضرّاء».
The clause «يقولنّ» has no grammatical position; the response to the implied oath.. and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by the response to the oath.
The clause «ذهب السيّئات» is in the position of the accusative as the object of saying.
The clause «إنّه لفرح ...» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl of the genitive pronoun, so it is a ḥāl corroborating the content of the clause before it [Note: or it is resumptive, with no grammatical position.].
(إلّا) a particle of exception [Note: It may mean «لكن» ("but"), and what follows it is a nominal clause of mubtadaʾ and khabar.]; (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative as the excepted in a connected exception [Note: from «الإنسان» mentioned earlier in the previous verse, which denotes the genus.. And the exception may be disconnected if «الإنسان» is a specific man.]; (صبروا) like «كفروا», and like it is (عملوا); (الصالحات) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, its sign of the accusative being the kasra; (أولئك) a demonstrative, indeclinable on the kasra, in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ.. and (الكاف) a particle of address; (اللام) a preposition and (هم) an attached pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (مغفرة) a postponed mubtadaʾ, nominative; (أجر) conjoined to «مغفرة» by the wāw, nominative; (كبير) a naʿt of «أجر», nominative.
The clause «صبروا ...» has no grammatical position; ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «عملوا ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «أولئك لهم مغفرة ...» has no grammatical position; an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «لهم مغفرة ...» is in the position of the nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أولئك).

* Morphology:
(مصروفا): passive participle of the triliteral صرف; its pattern is مفعول.
(حاق): it contains a weakening by substitution (iʿlāl bi-l-qalb); its original form is «حيق», its imperfect «يحيق»; the yāʾ came voweled after a fatḥa, so it was changed into an alif.. See verse (10) of Sūrat al-Anʿām.
(يئوس): intensive form of the active participle from «يئس ييئس», of the فرح class; its pattern is فعول.. It may be an assimilated adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha).
(كفور): intensive form of the active participle from «كفر يكفر», of the نصر class; its pattern is فعول..

* Morphology:
(نوفّ): it contains a weakening by deletion on account of the jussive; its original form is «نوفّي», and it may be an assimilated adjective [Translator's note: so in the source; this word belongs to verse 15 and the final remark appears misplaced.].
(نعماء): a noun meaning «النعمى» (blessing), from «نعم ينعم» of the first, third and fourth classes; its pattern is فعلاء, and the hamza is added for the feminine.

* Rhetoric:
1- The saying of the Exalted: «إِنْ هذا إِلَّا سِحْرٌ مُبِينٌ», i.e., like it in deception and falsehood; the construction is an eloquent simile (tashbīh balīgh), and what is meant is denial of the resurrection by way of allusive metonymy (kināya īmāʾiyya).
2- Implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya): in the saying of the Exalted «وَلَئِنْ أَذَقْنَا الْإِنْسانَ مِنَّا رَحْمَةً», i.e., We gave him a blessing of health, security and wealth. Tasting (al-idhāqa) originally is taking something with the mouth to perceive food; then it was borrowed for pleasure, likening it to what is tasted and then quickly disappears, as flavours disappear.
3- Antithesis (ṭibāq): between «النعماء» and «الضراء».

* Benefits:
- Suspending the verb from operating (taʿlīq):
In this verse occurs the saying of the Exalted: لِيَبْلُوَكُمْ أَيُّكُمْ أَحْسَنُ عَمَلًا. In this verse we say that the verb (يبلوكم) is suspended from putting the mafʿūl bihi in the accusative, because the mafʿūl bihi comes as a nominal clause headed by an interrogative. In the i'rab we say: «أيكم» is a mubtadaʾ, nominative, and the kāf is an attached pronoun in the position of the genitive by annexation, and the mīm is for the plural; «أحسن» is khabar, nominative; and the clause «أيكم أحسن» is in the position of the accusative as the second mafʿūl bihi of the verb «يبلوكم».
It is useful in this context to mention a brief account of what relates to this important topic:
1- A verb that is transitive to one object may be suspended from operating, and that is when the clause is headed by an interrogative, as in the saying of the Exalted: فَلْيَنْظُرْ أَيُّها أَزْكى طَعاماً and the saying of the Exalted: يَسْئَلُونَ أَيَّانَ يَوْمُ الدِّينِ 2- And a verb that is transitive to two objects may be suspended from operating if the clause is headed by an interrogative, and we parse it as a clause standing in place of the two objects, as in the saying of the Exalted: وَلَتَعْلَمُنَّ أَيُّنا أَشَدُّ عَذاباً لِنَعْلَمَ أَيُّ الْحِزْبَيْنِ أَحْصى

safi-cedvel:88-89.t:
* I'rab:
(قال يا قوم ... رزقا حسنا) the i'rab of its parallel has passed [Note: In verse (28) of this sūra.], and the second object is omitted, its implied form being "shall I go against His command?" (هل أخالف أمره) [Note: Or "shall I betray His revelation?".. or "shall I follow error?", or "shall I defraud people of their things?".. etc.]; (الواو) conjunction; (ما) a particle of negation; (أريد) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the fāʿil (agent) is "I" (أنا); (أن أخالفكم) like أن نترك [Note: In verse (87) of this sūra.], and (كم) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the interpreted maṣdar (أن أخالفكم) is in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl bihi, its governing word being the negated أريد.
(إلى) a preposition; (ما) relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أخالف) [Note: (ما) may be an indefinite noun described by a following clause, in the position of genitive.. and the clause after it is its naʿt (adjective), in the position of genitive.]; (أنهاكم) imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the rafʿ being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif, and the fāʿil is "I".. and (كم) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (عن) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (أنهاكم); (إن) a particle of negation; (أريد) like the first; (إلّا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (الإصلاح) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb); (ما) a maṣdar-forming temporal particle; (استطعت) past verb and its fāʿil.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما استطعت..) is in the position of accusative as an adverb of time, attached to (أريد), i.e. "I want reform for as long as I am able".
(الواو) conjunction; (ما) a particle of negation; (توفيقي) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative, the sign of the rafʿ being the ḍamma implied on what precedes the yāʾ, and (الياء) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (إلّا) like the first; (بالله) preposition and its genitive noun, the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; (عليه) like عنه, attached to (توكّلت), which is parsed like استطعت; (الواو) conjunction; (إليه) like عنه, attached to (أنيب), which is parsed like أريد.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «the vocative and its response ...» is in the position of accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «أرأيتم ...» has no grammatical position: the response to the vocative.
The clause «إن كنت ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical.. and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by the preceding speech.
The clause «رزقني ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the parenthetical clause.
The clause «ما أريد ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause of the response to the vocative.
The clause «أخالفكم ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «أنهاكم ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «إن أريد ...» has no grammatical position: justificatory (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «استطعت» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle-relative (ما).
The clause «ما توفيقي إلّا بالله» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the response to the vocative.
The clause «عليه توكّلت ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive within the scope of the speech.
The clause «إليه أنيب» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause توكّلت.
(الواو) conjunction; (يا قوم) like the first; (لا) the prohibitive lā, making jussive; (يجرمنّ) imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of jussive.. and (النون) is the nūn of emphasis, and (كم) is a pronoun, first mafʿūl bihi; (شقاقي) fāʿil, nominative, the sign of the rafʿ being the ḍamma implied on what precedes the yāʾ.. and (الياء) is muḍāf ilayhi [Note: This pronoun is, in meaning, the object of the maṣdar, i.e. "your hostility to me".]; (أن يصيبكم) like أن أخالفكم [Note: In verse (88) of this sūra.]; (مثل) fāʿil, nominative [Note: It is originally the adjective of an omitted described noun, i.e. "a punishment like what befell ...".]; (ما) relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; (أصاب) past verb, and the fāʿil is "he/it" (هو), which is the referent pronoun (ʿāʾid); (قوم) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (نوح) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (أو) a conjunction in both places; (قوم هود — قوم صالح) like قوم نوح, both conjoined to it; (الواو) resumptive; (ما قوم لوط منكم ببعيد) like ما هي من الظالمين ببعيد [Note: In verse (83) of this sūra.].
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يصيبكم) is in the position of accusative as the second mafʿūl bihi, its governing word being يجرمنّكم.
The clause «يا قوم» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the first clause يا قوم.
The clause «لا يجرمنكم شقاقي» has no grammatical position: the response to the vocative.
The clause «يصيبكم» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «أصاب ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «ما قوم.. ببعيد» has no grammatical position: resumptive or parenthetical.

* Morphology:
(استطعت): it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion in keeping with being built on the sukūn; its origin is استطاعت, and when the verb was built on the sukūn because of its being attached to the nominative pronoun, the alif was dropped because of the meeting of two vowelless letters; its pattern is استفلت.

safi-cedvel:12-12.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive; (لعلّ) a particle resembling the verb, for hope (tarajjī) [Note: It is said to be for affirmation (taqrīr).. and it is said to be for interrogation.. and it is said to be for making remote (tabʿīd), because hope, which entails expectation, does not befit the station of prophethood.] — an abrogator (nāsikh) —; (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of the accusative, the noun of laʿalla; (تارك) khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ); (بعض) mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the active participle «تارك», accusative (manṣūb); (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the genitive, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (يوحى) a passive imperfect verb, nominative, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو", and it is the resumptive pronoun; (إلى) a preposition and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يوحى); (الواو) conjunction; (ضائق) conjoined to «تارك», nominative [Note: or it is a fronted khabar and (صدرك) a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject).. and the clause is conjoined to «تارك».]; (الباء) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to «ضائق»; (صدر) fāʿil (agent) of the active participle «ضائق», nominative, and (الكاف) muḍāf ilayhi; (أن) a maṣdar-forming particle that puts the verb in the accusative; (يقولوا) an imperfect verb, accusative, its sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is fāʿil; (لولا) a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ) meaning «هلّا»; (أنزل) a passive past verb; (على) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (أنزل); (كنز) nāʾib fāʿil, nominative; (أو) a conjunction; (جاء) a past verb; (مع) an adverb (ẓarf), accusative, attached to (جاء) [Note: or attached to an [omitted] ḥāl (circumstantial) of «ملك».], and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (ملك) fāʿil, nominative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يقولوا) is in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), on the assumption of an omitted muḍāf, i.e., "for fear that they say" [Note: It may be genitive by an implied lām of causation, negated, i.e., «لئلّا يقولوا» ("lest they say") ...]; (إنّما) the restraining mā with what it restrains (kāffa wa-makfūfa); (أنت) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ; (نذير) khabar of the mubtadaʾ, nominative; (الواو) conjunction; (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ, nominative; (على كلّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «وكيل»; (شيء) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (وكيل) khabar, nominative.
The clause «لعلّك تارك ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «يوحى إليك ...» has no grammatical position; ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «يقولوا ...» has no grammatical position; ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «أنزل عليه كنز» is in the position of the accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «جاء معه ملك» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause that is the object of saying.
The clause «أنت نذير» has no grammatical position; a cause for something implied, i.e.: do not listen to them, for you are a warner to them.
The clause «الله.. وكيل» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause «أنت نذير».

* Morphology:
(تارك): active participle of the triliteral ترك; its pattern is فاعل.
(ضائق): active participle of the triliteral ضاق; its pattern is فاعل, and its weak letter has been changed into a hamza, and this is the case with every hollow weak verb.
(كنز): a noun meaning "the thing hoarded", from the verb «كنز يكنز», of the ضرب class; its pattern is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn.

* Benefits:
- Did the Messenger (Allah bless him and his family and grant him peace) conceal some of what was revealed to him?
In this verse occurs the saying of the Exalted: فَلَعَلَّكَ تارِكٌ بَعْضَ ما يُوحى إِلَيْكَ. The address is to the Prophet (Allah bless him and his family and grant him peace). Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says to His Prophet: perhaps you would leave some of what your Lord reveals to you, [failing] to convey it to those to whom He commanded you to convey it. وَضائِقٌ بِهِ صَدْرُكَ means: and your breast is straitened by what is revealed to you, so you do not convey it to them. That is because the disbelievers of Mecca said: "Bring a Qur'an other than this, in which there is no reviling of our gods." So the Prophet (Allah bless him and his family and grant him peace) was inclined to leave off mentioning their gods openly, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down: فَلَعَلَّكَ تارِكٌ بَعْضَ ما يُوحى إِلَيْكَ — of the mention of their gods. This is what the exegetes mentioned. The Muslims have agreed unanimously that the Prophet (Allah bless him and his family and grant him peace), in whatever pertained to conveying [the message], was protected (maʿṣūm) in it from reporting anything of it [falsely] [Translator's note: the source reads literally "protected in it from reporting anything of it"; the bracketed word is added for sense.], and that he (Allah bless him and his family and grant him peace) conveyed all that Allah sent down to him to his community and concealed nothing of it. And they agreed unanimously that it is not possible for the Messenger of Allah (Allah bless him and his family and grant him peace) to betray [the trust] in revelation and warning, nor to leave anything of what was revealed to him. The scholars responded to this doubt in the verse by saying: the disbelievers used to mock the Qur'an and laugh at it, and the breast of the Messenger of Allah (Allah bless him and his family and grant him peace) was straitened by that; so Allah, Glorified and Exalted, commanded him to convey what He revealed to him and not to pay attention to their mockery, and made clear to him that bearing their harm is easier than concealing anything of the revelation from them. And it is said: Allah, Glorified and Exalted, despite His knowledge that the Messenger of Allah (Allah bless him and his family and grant him peace) would not leave anything of the revelation, stirred him to deliver the message and to cast aside concern over their mockery; and the Exalted said: يا أَيُّهَا الرَّسُولُ بَلِّغْ ما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ مِنْ رَبِّكَ

safi-cedvel:46-46.t:
* I'rab:
(قال يا نوح) its i'rab has been given [Note: In āya (32) of this sūra.], (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb – an abrogator (nāsikh) – and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of inna (ليس) defective, non-inflecting (jāmid) past verb, and its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "he" (من أهلك) like من أهلي, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of laysa [Note: In the previous āya (45).] (إنّه) like the first (عمل) the khabar of inna, nominative (marfūʿ), on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "one of (a) deed" (ذو عمل) (غير) naʿt (adjective) of عمل, nominative (صالح) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr) (الفاء) linking to the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition (لا) prohibitive, putting into the jussive [Translator's note: the source has حازمة, evidently for جازمة] (تسألن) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm).. and (النون) is for protection (wiqāya), and (الياء), dropped for lightness, is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) (ما) relative noun [Note: Or it is an indefinite noun qualified by what follows, meaning "a thing".. and the clause after it is in the position of accusative as a naʿt of it.], indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative as a second mafʿūl bihi (ليس) like the first (اللام) a preposition, and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to the fronted khabar (به) like لك, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (علم), which is the postponed noun of laysa, nominative [Translator's note: the source has لبس, evidently for ليس] (إنّي) like إنّه (أعظ) imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil (agent) is "I", and (الكاف) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (أن) maṣdar particle (تكون) defective imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), and its noun is a latent pronoun, implied as "you" (من الجاهلين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar of تكون.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تكون) is in the position of genitive by an omitted preposition, its implied form being من, attached to (أعظك) in the sense of "I forbid you" [Note: Or it is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e.: I admonish you out of dislike that you be among the ignorant.].
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «يا نوح ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl) [Note: Or it is parenthetical with no grammatical position, and the clause after it is the object of the saying.].
The clause «إنّه ليس من أهلك» has no grammatical position; the reply to the vocative.
The clause «ليس من أهلك» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of inna.
The clause «إنّه عمل ...» has no grammatical position; causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «لا تسألن ...» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e.: i.e. if knowledge of this has come to you, then do not ask Me ...
The clause «ليس لك به علم» has no grammatical position; the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما).
The clause «إنّي أعظك ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «أعظك ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of inna.
The clause «تكون ...» has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the particle relative (أن).

* Benefits:
1- The infallibility (ʿiṣma) of the prophets:
Those who do not hold the infallibility of the prophets have taken these āyas as evidence, saying that what is meant by His saying, the Exalted, إِنَّهُ عَمَلٌ غَيْرُ صالِحٍ is the asking, and it is forbidden; therefore He forbade him from it by His saying فَلا تَسْئَلْنِ ما لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ; and His saying, glory be to Him and exalted, إِنِّي أَعِظُكَ أَنْ تَكُونَ مِنَ الْجاهِلِينَ indicates that that asking was ignorance, so it contains rebuke and threat; and seeking forgiveness and mercy for it indicates that a sin was committed. The answer is that Allah, mighty and majestic, had promised Nūḥ, upon him be blessings and peace, that He would save him and his family; so Nūḥ took the apparent sense of the wording and followed the interpretation according to the apparent sense, not knowing what was hidden from him, and without doubting the promise of Allah, glory be to Him and exalted; so he ventured this question for this reason. Allah, mighty and majestic, then reproached him for asking about what he had no knowledge of, and made clear to him that he was not of his family whose rescue He had promised him, because of his disbelief and his deed, which is not righteous; and Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, informed him that He would drown him with those who did wrong, and forbade him from addressing Him concerning them. So Nūḥ became fearful about his having ventured to ask his Lord about something he had not been permitted, and feared destruction from that; so he took refuge in his Lord, mighty and majestic, humbled himself before Him, sought refuge with Him, and asked Him for forgiveness and mercy, because the good deeds of the righteous are the bad deeds of those brought near. There is nothing in the āya that requires the commission of a sin or act of disobedience by Nūḥ, upon him be blessings and peace, other than his interpretation and his venturing to ask about what he had not been permitted, and this is neither a sin nor an act of disobedience. And in this incident there is said what was said concerning the Prophet's ﷺ ransoming of the captives of Badr; and Allah knows best.
2- Dropping the yāʾ for lightness:
In the Noble Qur'an the yāʾ is dropped from some nouns and verbs without a grammatical reason requiring it, and the grammarians said that the reason for its dropping is lightness; in parsing we consider it present and parse it. It occurs in this āya in His saying, the Exalted: فلا تسألن, originally فلا تسألني; the yāʾ was dropped for lightness, and it is an attached pronoun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi. In Sūrat al-Kahf there is His saying, the Exalted, ذلِكَ ما كُنَّا نَبْغِ, i.e. نبغي; and it also occurs in another place in the Noble Qur'an: وَإِذا مَرِضْتُ فَهُوَ يَشْفِينِ; and in the previous āya there occurs رَبِّ إِنَّ ابْنِي مِنْ أَهْلِي, i.e. (ربي). This is a feature of the speech of Allah, mighty and majestic, that distinguishes it from the speech of human beings; the dropping of the yāʾ has a purpose and wisdom, and harmony and accord with the concordant musical cadence of the Noble Qur'an, and in it there is a pointer to some subtle meanings. For example, in His saying, the Exalted, رَبِّ اغْفِرْ وَارْحَمْ there is a pointer to the nearness of Allah, mighty and majestic, to the servant and His answering him before he has completed the word (ربي). And Allah knows best.

safi-cedvel:47-47.t:
* I'rab:
(قال ربّ) its i'rab has been given [Note: In āya (45) of this sūra.
(2, 3, 4) In the previous āya (46).], (إنّي) like إنّه «2», (أعوذ) like أعظ «3», (الباء) a preposition, and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أعوذ), (أن) maṣdar and accusative-governing particle (أسأل) imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), and the fāʿil (agent) is "I", and (الكاف) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) (ما ليس لي به علم) like ما ليس لك به علم «4».
The interpreted maṣdar (أن أسألك..) is in the position of genitive by an omitted preposition, its implied form being "من أن أسألك..", attached to (أعوذ).
(الواو) conjunction (إنّ) conditional particle putting into the jussive [Translator's note: written thus with shadda in the source; the conditional particle is إن, merged with لا in the text as إلّا] (لا) negative (تغفر) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), and the fāʿil is "you" (لي) like لك, attached to (تغفر), (الواو) conjunction (ترحم) imperfect verb, jussive, conjoined to (تغفر), and (النون) is for protection (wiqāya) and (الياء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is "you" (أكن) defective imperfect verb, jussive, the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as (أنا) (من الخاسرين) a preposition and its genitive noun, the khabar (predicate) of أكن.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «ربّ ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «إنّي أعوذ ...» has no grammatical position; the reply to the vocative.
The clause «أعوذ ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of inna.
The clause «أسألك ...» has no grammatical position; the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «ليس لي به علم» has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative (ما) [Note: Or in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of (ما), the qualified indefinite meaning "a thing".].
The clause «إلّا تغفر ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause that is the reply to the vocative.
The clause «ترحمني ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause تغفر.
The clause «أكن من الخاسرين» has no grammatical position; the apodosis not joined with fāʾ.

safi-cedvel:48-48.t:
* I'rab:
(قيل) past verb, passive (يا نوح) its i'rab has been given [Note: In āya 32 of this sūra.], (اهبط) imperative verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is "you" (بسلام) a preposition and its genitive noun, ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of اهبط (من) a preposition, and (نا) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of سلام [Note: Or attached to سلام.], (الواو) conjunction (بركات) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to سلام, genitive (majrūr) (على) a preposition, and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to a naʿt of بركات [Note: Or attached to بركات.], (الواو) conjunction (على أمم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a naʿt of بركات – or to بركات – so it is conjoined to the first genitive with repetition of the preposition (من) a preposition (من) relative noun in the position of genitive, attached to a naʿt of أمم (مع) adverb, accusative (manṣūb), attached to the omitted ṣila (relative clause) of من, and (الكاف) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) (الواو) resumptive (أمم) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ).. its khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e.: من ذرّيتك أمم (السين) particle of the future (نمتع) imperfect verb, nominative, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil is "We", for magnification (ثمّ) conjunction (يمسّهم) like نمتّعهم (منّا) like the first, attached to a ḥāl from (عذاب), which is the fāʿil of يمسّهم, nominative (أليم) naʿt of عذاب, nominative.
The clause «قيل ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «يا نوح ...» is in the position of nominative as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) [Note: Because it is originally the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).. See āya (11) of Sūrat al-Baqara.].
The clause «اهبط بسلام» has no grammatical position; the reply to the vocative.
The clause «من ذرّيتك أمم» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «سنمتّعهم» is in the position of nominative as a naʿt of أمم.
The clause «يمسّهم منّا عذاب ...» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause سنمتّعهم.

safi-cedvel:49-49.t:
* I'rab:
(تلك) demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn overt on the yāʾ dropped because of the meeting of two quiescents, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) [Note: The reference is to the āyas that relate the story of Nūḥ, peace be upon him.] [Translator's note: translated as written; the phrase "the sukūn overt on the dropped yāʾ" is as in the source.], and (اللام) is for distance and (الكاف) for address (من أنباء) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ [Note: Or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the overt pronoun in (نوحيها).], (الغيب) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr) (نوحي) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the implied (muqaddar) ḍamma, and the fāʿil (agent) is "We", for magnification, and (ها) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) (إلى) a preposition, and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (نوحيها), (ما) negative (كنت) defective past verb – an abrogator (nāsikh) – and its noun [is the tāʾ] [Translator's note: the source reads "واسمه" with nothing following] (تعلمها) like نوحيها, and the fāʿil is "you", a latent (mustatir) pronoun (أنت) a visible detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as tawkīd (emphasis) of the agent (الواو) conjunction (لا) redundant (zāʾida), to reinforce the negation (قوم) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the latent pronoun that is the agent of تعلم, nominative, and (الكاف) muḍāf ilayhi (من قبل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تعلمها), (ها) particle of alerting (ذا) demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi [Note: The reference is to the Noble Qur'an.], (الفاء) resumptive [Note: Or linking to the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition.], (اصبر) imperative verb, and the fāʿil is "you" (إنّ العاقبة) a particle resembling the verb and its accusative noun (للمتّقين) a preposition and its genitive noun, the khabar of inna.
The clause «تلك من أنباء ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «نوحيها ...» is in the position of nominative as a second khabar of the mubtadaʾ تلك [Note: Or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from أنباء.].
The clause «ما كنت تعلمها» is in the position of nominative as a third khabar [Note: It may be a ḥāl.. either from the object pronoun in (نوحيها) or from the genitive pronoun in إليك).].
The clause «تعلمها» is in the position of accusative as the khabar of كنت.
The clause «اصبر» has no grammatical position; resumptive [Note: Or in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e.: if you are harmed in conveying what has been sent to you, then be patient.].
The clause «إنّ العاقبة للمتّقين» has no grammatical position; causal (taʿlīliyya).

safi-cedvel:90-90.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction; (استغفروا) imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (ربّكم) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb).. and (كم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (ثمّ) a conjunction; (توبوا) like استغفروا; (إلى) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (توبوا); (أنّ) [Translator's note: the source writes أنّ; the particle in the verse is إنّ, and the source itself goes on to say "noun of inna".] a particle resembling the verb; (ربّي) noun of inna, accusative, the sign of the naṣb being the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on what precedes the yāʾ.. and (الياء) is muḍāf ilayhi; (رحيم) khabar (predicate) of inna, nominative (marfūʿ); (ودود) second khabar, nominative.
The clause «استغفروا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the response to the vocative in the previous (verse).
The clause «توبوا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause استغفروا.
The clause «إنّ ربّي رحيم» has no grammatical position: justificatory (taʿlīliyya).

* Morphology:
(ودود): one of the intensive forms (ṣiyagh al-mubālagha) of the transitive verb ودّ يودّ, of the bāb of fataḥa [Translator's note: so in the source; ودّ يودّ is usually classed under the bāb of fariḥa (وَدِدَ يَوَدُّ).]; its pattern is فعول.

safi-cedvel:91-91.t:
* I'rab:
(قالوا يا شعيب) is like قالوا يا صالح [Note: In verse (62) of this sūra.]; (ما) negating; (نفقه) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the fāʿil (agent) is "we" (نحن); (كثيرا) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (من) a preposition; (ما) relative noun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of (كثيرا) [Note: It may be a maṣdar-forming particle, and the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of genitive.
(3, 4) In verse (84) of this sūra.]; (تقول) like نفقه, and the fāʿil is "you" (أنت); (الواو) conjunction; (إنّا) like إنّي «3»; (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), conveying emphasis; (نراك) imperfect verb like أراكم «4», and the fāʿil is "we"; (في) a preposition and (نا) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (نراك); (ضعيفا) ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, from the pronoun of address [Note: Or a second mafʿūl bihi of the verb of seeing, if it is mental (qalbiyya).]; (الواو) conjunction; (لولا) a non-jussive conditional particle; (رهطك) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative.. and (الكاف) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the khabar (predicate) is omitted; (اللام) occurring in the apodosis of لولا; (رجمنا) past verb and its fāʿil; (الكاف) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (الواو) conjunction; (ما) negating, operating like laysa; (أنت) detached pronoun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative, the noun of mā; (علينا) like فينا, attached to (عزيز); (الباء) a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; (عزيز) genitive in form, accusative in position, the khabar of mā.
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «the vocative and its response» is in the position of accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «ما نفقه ...» has no grammatical position: the response to the vocative.
The clause «تقول ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of (ما), the nominal or the particle relative.
The clause «إنّا لنراك ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause of the response to the vocative.
The clause «نراك ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of inna.
The clause «لولا رهطك» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the response to the vocative.
The clause «رجمناك» has no grammatical position: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «ما أنت.. بعزيز» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the response to the vocative [Note: It may be a ḥāl from the pronoun of address in (رجمناك).].

* Morphology:
(رهط): a collective noun (ism jamʿ).. al-Zamakhsharī said: from three to ten, and it is said: up to nine; its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn; its plural is أرهط, and this is pluralized as أراهط.

safi-cedvel:92-92.t:
* I'rab:
(قال يا قوم) its i'rab has passed [Note: In verse (78) of this sūra.]; (الهمزة) for interrogation; (رهطي) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the rafʿ being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on what precedes the yāʾ.. and (الياء) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (أعزّ) khabar (predicate), nominative; (على) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) أعزّ; (من الله) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to أعزّ; (الواو) the wāw of ḥāl; (اتّخذتم) past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and (الواو) is redundant (zāʾida), a lengthening (ishbāʿ) of the vowel of the mīm; (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (وراءكم) an adverb, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (اتّخذتم) [Note: It may be attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (ظهريّا), and it may be the second object of (اتّخذتم), with ظهريّا a ḥāl.]. And (كم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (ظهريّا) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative, of the verb اتّخذتم [Note: It is a ḥāl from the object if the verb is taken as transitive to a single object.]; (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb; (ربّي) noun of inna, accusative, the sign of the naṣb being the implied fatḥa.. and (الياء) is muḍāf ilayhi; (الباء) a preposition; (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle [Note: Or a relative noun in the position of genitive, with the referent pronoun omitted.]; (تعملون) imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is the fāʿil; (محيط) khabar of inna, nominative.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما تعملون) is in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, attached to محيط.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يا قوم ...» is in the position of accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «أرهطي أعزّ ...» has no grammatical position: the response to the vocative.
The clause «اتّخذتموه ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, with (قد) implied.
The clause «إنّ ربّي.. محيط» has no grammatical position: a resumption within the scope of the speech.
The clause «تعملون» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of (ما), the particle or the nominal relative.

* Morphology:
(ظهريّا): a word with the relative (nisba) ending, attributed to الظهر ("the back"); its pattern is فعليّ with kasra on the fāʾ, the kasra being one of the changes of the nisba, while the fatḥa is more regular.

safi-cedvel:93-93.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction; (يا قوم) its i'rab has passed [Note: In verse (78) of this sūra.]; (اعملوا) imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (على مكانة) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of اعملوا, i.e. "being upon your position".. and (كم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (إنّي) a particle resembling the verb and its noun; (عامل) khabar (predicate) of inna, nominative (marfūʿ); (سوف) a particle of the future; (تعلمون) like تعملون [Note: In the previous verse.]; (من) relative noun in the position of accusative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) [Note: Or an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar is the clause يأتيه عذاب.]; (يأتي) imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the rafʿ being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ, and (الهاء) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (عذاب) fāʿil, nominative; (يخزيه) like يأتيه; (الواو) conjunction; (من) like the first and conjoined to it; (هو) a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ; (كاذب) khabar, nominative; (الواو) conjunction; (ارتقبوا) like اعملوا; (إنّي) a particle resembling the verb and its noun; (معكم) an adverb, accusative (manṣūb), attached to رقيب..
and (كم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (رقيب) khabar of inna, nominative.
The clause «يا قوم ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the earlier vocative clause [Note: In the previous verse (92).].
The clause «اعملوا ...» has no grammatical position: the response to the vocative.
The clause «إنّي عامل ...» has no grammatical position: an explicative resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «سوف تعلمون ...» has no grammatical position: another explicative resumption.
The clause «يأتيه عذاب» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من) [Note: Or it is the khabar of the interrogative mubtadaʾ (من).].
The clause «هو كاذب» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second relative (من).
The clause «ارتقبوا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause of the response to the vocative.. and what lies between the conjoined and what it is conjoined to is a kind of parenthesis.
The clause «إنّي معكم رقيب» has no grammatical position: justificatory (taʿlīliyya).

* Rhetoric:
1- The explicative resumption (al-istiʾnāf al-bayānī): in the words of Allah the Exalted «وَيا قَوْمِ اعْمَلُوا عَلى مَكانَتِكُمْ إِنِّي عامِلٌ سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ».
If you say: what difference is there between inserting the fāʾ and omitting it in «سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ»?
I say: inserting the fāʾ is an overt connection by a particle designed for connection, and omitting it is a hidden, implied connection by way of resumption, which is the answer to an implied question, as though they said: "So what will happen if we act according to our position and you act?" So he said: "You will come to know". Thus the connection is sometimes made by the fāʾ and sometimes by resumption, for variety in eloquence, as is the custom of the eloquent Arabs; and the stronger and more eloquent of the two connections is the resumption, which is one of the chapters of the science of bayān whose beauties are many.
